source.title: Smith theory and cyclic base change functoriality
source.authors: Tony Feng, with an appendix by Tony Feng and Gus Lonergan
source.venue: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), published online 15 January 2024
readSections: Read in full in the published open-access text, fetched from Cambridge Core on 22 September 2026 (doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024)): §1 Introduction, §2 Functoriality and the excursion algebra, §3 Smith theory in locally finite type, §4 Parity sheaves and the base change functor, §5 On global base change, §6 On local base change, Appendix A (the base change functor realizes Langlands functoriality, with Gus Lonergan) and Appendix B (applying Drinfeld's lemma to Tate cohomology).

The LaTeX source of arXiv:2009.14236v6 (29 November 2023, the latest version; source archive sha256 9b813ef62f781c49163ff3930129c72c2b983134f15fb42a6f6f2d497ad9210d, file Smith_base_change.tex, 3549 lines) was read alongside it and used for the mechanical audits. The numbering of the two versions agrees statement by statement — checked across all eight sections, including the appendices, from Proposition 2.1 through Remark 6.27, Lemma A.3 and Lemma B.5 — so every locator below is valid for both; they are given for the published version.

All environments share one counter per section (\newtheorem{thm}{Theorem}[section] with the others declared [thm]), so a number such as 6.17 determines the statement uniquely. There are 109 numbered statements, of which 22 are remarks and 4 are examples; there are no duplicate labels and no undefined references.

Checks run on the source: a duplicate-label audit (none), an undefined-reference audit (none), and a cross-reference type audit comparing the word before each \ref with the environment carrying that label, which found the single mismatch recorded as source issue E7. Every source issue below was then confirmed against the published text.

Independent review REV-PAPER-FENG-24, 2026-09-28: every item checked against the published open-access text (doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32; Cambridge Core serves a per-download PDF, so its hash varies between downloads) with formulas checked on page images, and against the arXiv v6 TeX source (source archive sha256 9b813ef6…).

summary:
The paper states general results on cyclic base change functoriality in the Langlands correspondence over function fields, with mod p coefficients and without any trace formula. Let k be an algebraic closure of F_p, let F_v be a local function field of residue characteristic ℓ ≠ p, H a connected reductive group over F_v, E_v/F_v cyclic of degree p and G = Res_{E_v/F_v}(H_{E_v}), with φ_BC: ^LH → ^LG the diagonal on dual groups. Theorem 1.1: every irreducible k-representation of H(F_v) has a base change to G(F_v), for the Genestier–Lafforgue semisimplified local Langlands correspondence. Theorem 1.2, the Treumann–Venkatesh conjecture: if Π is σ-fixed and π is an irreducible subquotient of T^0(Π) or T^1(Π) as an H(F_v)-representation, then φ_BC ∘ ρ_π ≅ ρ_{Π^{(p)}} — Tate cohomology realises functoriality. Theorem 1.4: there is a base change homomorphism Z_TV of mod p Bernstein centers with the right effect on parameters, the construction Haines envisaged, for general groups and arbitrary depth. Theorem 1.6: strong global base change, transporting a whole automorphic L-parameter and not only the unramified Hecke eigensystem. The method has three layers. Sheaf-theoretic Smith theory is extended from finite type to locally finite type schemes, giving the Tate categories and the Smith operation Psm with its equivariant localisation theorem. Parity sheaves and Leslie–Lonergan's Tate-parity sheaves make the construction compatible with Geometric Satake, producing a base change functor BC on normalized parity sheaves which, by Theorem 4.20 and the appendix with Gus Lonergan, is restriction along the diagonal on tilting modules for the dual group: a categorification of the normalized Brauer homomorphism of Treumann–Venkatesh. Applied to moduli of shtukas, where the fixed-locus identification with Sht_H is valid for finite étale covers, this yields an identity between excursion operators for G and for H on Tate cohomology, and hence the global theorem; local-global compatibility of the Genestier–Lafforgue correspondence then gives the local ones. What the atlas lacks: sheaf-theoretic Smith theory, Tate categories, parity sheaves, Tate-parity sheaves and tilting modules for a dual group in characteristic p; Tate cohomology of shtukas, Drinfeld's lemma for it, and the whole mod p side of Lafforgue's construction, the atlas's shtuka roadmap being written for ℓ-adic characteristic-zero coefficients; and mod p Bernstein centers at Moy–Prasad level with the Brauer homomorphism and the Genestier–Lafforgue correspondence. What it already has: the excursion algebra with its relations and the reconstruction of semisimple L-parameters, shtuka stacks with legs and level, the dual group and the L-group, buildings and parahorics, and, in the libraries, Tate cohomology of a finite cyclic group and Witt vectors. Review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24). The review checked each item against the published text and the arXiv v6 source, checking formulas on page images, and made the following corrections.
- Theorem 1.1 holds under the standing hypothesis that p is an odd prime that is good for Ĝ; its only proof, Theorem 6.26, assumes this.
- Theorems 1.2, 1.4 and 1.6 also need the unstated but true lemma that φ_BC∘ρ is semisimple whenever ρ is. Lemma 2.7 is false as printed for a general admissible φ: φ^* sends ρ to (φ∘ρ)^ss.
- Lemma 3.8 needs bounded dimension.
- Lemmas 4.16 and 4.24 are false as printed. §4.6.3 needs their non-equivariant, object-level forms, and the proof of Proposition 5.12(i) needs a further argument.
- §A.4 proves Theorem 4.20 object by object and after restriction to the torus, but not as a natural isomorphism over Ĥ.
- Proposition 6.3 and Corollary 6.4 are false at r = 0, and the Galois-fixed special vertex of §6.2.3 need not exist. Both are repaired by working at r > 0 at any point of B(H/F_v).
- The proof of Theorem 5.13 gives the support statement only for the whole cohomology; the component repair works under a valid descent/localization comparison; E58 qualifies it to finite étale covers at present.
- Theorem 6.26 at r = 0 is unproved.
These corrections are recorded as 50 new source issues, and E1–E7 are confirmed.
Ownership and coverage:
- The excursion algebra, its reconstruction theorem and the Satake functor are used over k = F̄_p, which the atlas does not plan, contrary to the sentence above on what the atlas already has. They moved from the source route to route 2.
- The Tate diagonal and the Frobenius twist of algebras moved to route 1, as the general form of Treumann–Venkatesh §3.4.
- Route 3 imports the Brauer homomorphism, plain subgroups, linkage and the conjecture from the Treumann–Venkatesh Part II.
- The review adds 35 items.
Fix contract (2026-10-01): finite étale descent replaces the unqualified ramified fixed-locus assertion. Unrestricted global/local base change remains the published target, with the ramified comparison proof obligation routed once to the global Part II. The abstract excursion mechanism is coefficient-linear and geometric before Galois descent, preserving all full-L-group generators. rev-6 keeps finite-Tor preservation for Rj_* without its false relative-dimension bound. E58–E60 record the three source-level defects; the rev-6 strengthening is an extraction-review error, not a paper error.

items.name: Coefficients, σ-actions and the norm element
items.statement: k is an algebraic closure of F_p, with the discrete topology. Geometric objects live over fields of characteristic ≠ p (in the applications a field of characteristic ℓ ≠ p). Étale sheaves have p-adically complete coefficients: k, or W(k). σ denotes a generator of a group isomorphic to Z/pZ, and a 'σ-action' on an object is an action of a cyclic group of order p with chosen generator σ. N := 1 + σ + ··· + σ^{p−1} ∈ Z[σ], and N also denotes the induced operator on any Z[σ]-module. For a Z[σ]-ring or module A, A^σ denotes its σ-invariants. Where a monoidal operation ∗ is present, Nm(a) := a ∗ σ(a) ∗ ··· ∗ σ^{p−1}(a). Reductive groups are connected, Ĝ is a split reductive group over k, and 𝟙 denotes the trivial representation.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, §1.5 (Notation), p. 7; with footnote 1, p. 2, and footnote 5, p. 7
items.note: This inversion of the usual arithmetic-geometry convention is the standing convention of Smith theory and is used throughout the paper. Review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24), status check: Partly in the library, although the item cites nothing. N acting on a module is mathlib:Representation.norm (∑_g ρ g) and mathlib:Rep.norm. A^σ is mathlib:Representation.invariants, and k can be AlgebraicClosure (ZMod p). The monoidal Nm is made precise only by the later constructions: items 42 (Definition 4.12) and 65 (Definition 5.14). Cite these declarations. Keep 'missing' only for the convention bundle, or split the item.
items.originalStatement: k is an algebraic closure of F_p with the discrete topology; σ denotes a chosen generator of a group isomorphic to Z/pZ; N = 1 + σ + ··· + σ^{p-1} ∈ Z[σ] and also the induced operator on any Z[σ]-module, while Nm(a) = a * σ(a) * ··· * σ^{p-1}(a) in any monoidal setting. Geometric objects live over fields of characteristic ℓ ≠ p while the coefficients have characteristic p.

review.reason: Wrong section number. In the published version, which the locators follow, the Notation is §1.5 on p. 7. In arXiv v6 it is §1.6, after an Acknowledgments subsection that the journal version does not have there. The item also says the coefficients have characteristic p, but §1.5 says 'étale sheaves over p-adically complete coefficients': Λ = k, and also W(k) from §3.1 on. It omits the conventions that A^σ denotes σ-invariants, that reductive groups are connected, and that Ĝ is a split reductive group over k. Nothing names the characteristic of the geometric fields ℓ in §1.5; ℓ first appears for F_v and in §5.

items.name: Odd good primes for the dual group
items.statement: p is an odd good prime for G-hat if p > 2 when G-hat has simple factors of type A, B, C or D; p > 3 when it has simple factors of type G_2, F_4, E_6 or E_7; and p > 5 when it has simple factors of type E_8.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Theorem 1.2; the footnote to the hypothesis
items.note: The standing hypothesis of Theorems 1.2, 1.4, 1.6 and 6.26. Goodness of p is what makes all parity sheaves on Gr_G exist and be perverse (Theorem 4.8). Review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24), status check: Missing confirmed. No atlas stage matches 'good prime|bad prime|torsion prime' in this sense, and neither Mathlib at 082e2d3 nor Tau Ceti at f790474 defines good primes of a root datum. Statement and locator (footnote 3, p. 3) agree with the page image.

items.name: Existence of local mod p cyclic base change (Theorem 1.1)
items.statement: Assume p is an odd good prime for Ĝ. Let F_v be a local field of positive characteristic ℓ ≠ p, H a connected reductive group over F_v, E_v/F_v a cyclic extension of degree p, and G = Res_{E_v/F_v}(H_{E_v}). Let φ_BC: ^LH → ^LG be the admissible homomorphism that is the diagonal Ĥ → Ĥ^p = Ĝ on dual groups. Then for every irreducible representation π of H(F_v) over k there is an irreducible representation Π of G(F_v) over k with ρ_Π ≅ φ_BC ∘ ρ_π, where ρ denotes the Genestier–Lafforgue semisimple L-parameter.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Theorem 1.1, p. 2; proved as Theorem 6.26, p. 55, which assumes p is an odd good prime for Ĝ and adds level control (U_r-fixed vectors give K_r-fixed vectors)
items.note: The first general existence theorem for local cyclic base change of all irreducible representations of an arbitrary reductive group over a local function field, with no trace formula. Vignéras's full local Langlands gives a sharper statement for GL_n only. This is retained as the published unrestricted main target. The counterexample E58 disproves the stated fixed-locus lemma at permitted ramified levels, not this existence/parameter target. Its quoted proof requires the ramified comparison repair identified at items 60–64 and in routes 2–3; do not claim the finite-étale correction supplies it automatically.
items.originalStatement: Let F_v be a local function field of residue characteristic ℓ ≠ p, H a connected reductive group over F_v, E_v/F_v cyclic of degree p and G = Res_{E_v/F_v}(H_{E_v}); let φ_BC: ^LH → ^LG be the admissible homomorphism which is the diagonal on the dual groups. items.name: Tate cohomology realises cyclic base change (Theorem 1.2)
items.statement: Assume p is an odd good prime for Ĝ. Let F_v be a local field of positive characteristic ℓ ≠ p, H connected reductive over F_v, E_v/F_v cyclic of degree p, and G = Res_{E_v/F_v}(H_{E_v}). Let σ be a generator of Gal(E_v/F_v), acting on G(F_v) = H(E_v) by the Galois action, so that H(F_v) = G(F_v)^σ. Let Π be an irreducible representation of G(F_v) over k whose isomorphism class is fixed by σ. Give Π the unique σ-action compatible with the G(F_v)-action (Lemma 6.16), and put Π^{(p)} := Π ⊗_{k,Frob} k. Let π be any irreducible admissible subquotient of the Tate cohomology T^0(Π) or T^1(Π), taken as an H(F_v)-representation, and let ρ_π: W_v → ^LH(k) be its Genestier–Lafforgue parameter. Then φ_BC ∘ ρ_π ≅ ρ_{Π^{(p)}}.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Theorem 1.2, p. 3 (with footnote 3); proved as Theorem 6.21, p. 52
items.note: This verifies Conjecture 6.3 of Treumann–Venkatesh for the Genestier–Lafforgue correspondence, uniformly in the group and the representation. It was known only for certain depth-zero supercuspidals of GL_n, by Ronchetti's direct computation. This is retained as the published unrestricted main target. The counterexample E58 disproves the stated fixed-locus lemma at permitted ramified levels, not this existence/parameter target. Its quoted proof requires the ramified comparison repair identified at items 60–64 and in routes 2–3; do not claim the finite-étale correction supplies it automatically.
items.originalStatement: Assume p is an odd good prime for G-hat. Let Π be an irreducible representation of G(F_v) over k whose isomorphism class is fixed by σ, with Π^{(p)} = Π ⊗_{k,Frob} k its Frobenius twist. Let π be any irreducible admissible subquotient of T^0(Π) or T^1(Π) as an H(F_v)-representation, with Genestier–Lafforgue parameter ρ_π: W_v → ^LH(k). Then φ_BC ∘ ρ_π ≅ ρ_{Π^{(p)}}.

review.reason: Incomplete. The item does not define σ or the σ-action on Π, so T^0(Π) and T^1(Π) are undefined in it. σ is a generator of Gal(E_v/F_v) acting on G(F_v) = H(E_v) by the Galois action, and the σ-action on Π is the unique one compatible with the G(F_v)-action (Lemma 6.16, cited on p. 3). The setting of Theorem 1.1 is not restated. The mathematics is otherwise exact.

items.name: Base change homomorphism for Bernstein centers (Theorem 1.4)
items.statement: Let F_v be a local field of positive characteristic with residue characteristic ℓ ≠ p, k an algebraic closure of F_p, H a connected reductive group over F_v, E_v/F_v a cyclic extension of degree p, G := Res_{E_v/F_v}(H_{E_v}), and φ_BC: ^LH → ^LG the base change homomorphism of Definition 2.8. Assume p is an odd good prime for Ĝ. Then there is a homomorphism ℨ_TV: ℨ(G) → ℨ(H) of Bernstein centers with coefficients in k such that, for every irreducible representation π of H(F_v) over k with character χ_π: ℨ(H) → k and every irreducible representation Π of G(F_v) over k on which ℨ(G) acts through χ_π ∘ ℨ_TV, the Genestier–Lafforgue parameters satisfy ρ_Π ≅ φ_BC ∘ ρ_π as semisimple L-parameters.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Theorem 1.4, p. 4; ℨ_TV is constructed in Definition 6.11 (p. 49) from Definition 6.8 (p. 48); its property is Corollary 6.15 with the 'Completion of the proof of Theorem 1.4', §6.4, pp. 49–51
items.note: A base change homomorphism of Bernstein centers in characteristic zero was sought by Haines and constructed in low depth; this is the first construction for general groups and depth, and the first with a proved relation to the local Langlands correspondence. Review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24), status check: missing is right; route 3 is the right owner. As written, the construction in §§6.2.3–6.4 needs a special vertex x of B(G/F_v) fixed by Gal(E_v/F_v), and such a vertex need not exist (new issue: H = SL_1(D)). The corrected Corollary 6.4 supplies the r > 0 double-coset input at any Gal-fixed x; it does not repair the distinct ramified global descent input (E58). This is retained as the published unrestricted main target. The counterexample E58 disproves the stated fixed-locus lemma at permitted ramified levels, not this existence/parameter target. Its quoted proof requires the ramified comparison repair identified at items 60–64 and in routes 2–3; do not claim the finite-étale correction supplies it automatically.
items.originalStatement: Assume p is an odd good prime for G-hat. Then there is a homomorphism Z_TV: Z(G) → Z(H) of Bernstein centers with k-coefficients such that for every irreducible H(F_v)-representation π, and every irreducible G(F_v)-representation Π on which Z(G) acts through χ_π ∘ Z_TV, one has ρ_Π ≅ φ_BC ∘ ρ_π.

items.name: Existence of global mod p cyclic base change (Theorem 1.6)
items.statement: Assume p is an odd good prime for G-hat. Let F be a global function field of characteristic ≠ p, H a reductive group over F, E/F cyclic of degree p and G = Res_{E/F}(H_E). If ρ: Gal(F^s/F) → ^LH(k) is automorphic, i.e. arises from Lafforgue–Xue's excursion action on compactly supported automorphic functions, then φ_BC ∘ ρ is automorphic.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Theorem 1.6; proved as Theorem 5.13
items.note: This is strong base change: it concerns the whole L-parameter, not only the Hecke eigensystem at almost all places. The two notions coincide for GL_n but not for general groups — Lafforgue's correspondence can assign different parameters to automorphic forms generating isomorphic representations, already for SL_n with n ≥ 3. This is retained as the published unrestricted main target. The counterexample E58 disproves the stated fixed-locus lemma at permitted ramified levels, not this existence/parameter target. Its quoted proof requires the ramified comparison repair identified at items 60–64 and in routes 2–3; do not claim the finite-étale correction supplies it automatically.
