items.name: The algebraic L-group
items.statement: For G reductive over a field F with separable closure F^s, the root datum Ψ(G) of G_{F^s} determines a pinning of the split reductive group G-hat over k, hence a splitting Out(G-hat) → Aut(G-hat) and an identification Aut(Ψ(G)) ≅ Out(G-hat); transporting the Gal(F^s/F)-action on Ψ(G) gives act^alg and ^LG^alg := G-hat ⋊_{act^alg} Gal(F^s/F), a pro-algebraic group over k since the action factors through a finite quotient. Over a local field the Weil form G-hat ⋊ Weil(F^s/F) is used instead.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, §2.1.1
items.note: ReductiveGroupsPartII:RG2.5 plans the pinned split dual group from the dual root datum together with the continuous finite-image action on its pinning and the semidirect L-group with its projection and action law. Review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24), status check: 'Planned' can stand with a caveat. ReductiveGroupsPartII:RG2.5 plans the pinned split dual group, the finite-image pinned action and the semidirect L-group, but its roadmap covers only G over a nonarchimedean local field E ('Use arbitrary nonarchimedean local fields E'). Theorem 1.6 and §5 need ^LG^alg for G over a global function field. GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands:GS.1 and GS.5 use that L-group ('descend nonsplit data via the L-group'; 'include the projection to the Galois group') but no layer constructs it. Since the construction does not depend on the field, the route-2 design should import RG2.5's construction for an arbitrary base field and say so.

items.name: The geometric L-group
items.statement: The Geometric Satake equivalence Perv_{L^+G_{F^s}}(Gr_{G,F^s};k) ≅ Rep_k(Ĝ), with fibre functor H^*(−), and the action of Gal(F^s/F) on Gr_{G,F^s} induce, by [RZ15, Lemma A.1], an action act^geom of Gal(F^s/F) on Ĝ_k. This action factors through a finite quotient, and ^LG^geom := Ĝ_k ⋊_{act^geom} Gal(F^s/F) is a pro-algebraic group. Rep_k(^LG^alg) := colim_{F'} Rep_k(Ĝ ⋊_{act^alg} Gal(F'/F)), the colimit over finite Galois F'/F splitting G. Rep_k(^LG^geom) := Rep_k(Ĝ)^{BGal(F^s/F),geom}: objects of Rep_k(Ĝ) with a continuous Gal(F^s/F)-equivariant structure for act^geom. Since k is algebraic over F_p, this category is colim_{F'/F} Rep_k(Ĝ)^{BGal(F'/F),geom}. Descent gives Perv_{L^+G}(Gr_G;k) ≅ Rep_k(Ĝ)^{BGal(F^s/F),geom} (2.2), with Gr_G over F. An isomorphism (2.1) induces an equivalence Rep_k(^LG^alg) ≃ Rep_k(Ĝ)^{BGal(F^s/F),geom}.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, §2.1.2; and §2.1.4
items.note: GeometricSatakeAndFusion:GS4 plans Tannakian reconstruction of the dual group from the Satake category together with the Weil action, and GS4:integral-dual-group the normalized functoriality; this is that construction in the equal-characteristic setting with k-coefficients. Review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24): status planned → missing: GeometricSatakeAndFusion:GS4:integral-dual-group builds the Tannakian dual group and its geometric Weil action only for the B_dR^+ affine Grassmannian over a nonarchimedean local field, and GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands:GS.1 plans equal-characteristic Satake only with rational ℓ-adic coefficients ('integral and modular Satake are further coefficient branches'). The paper's ^LG^geom uses the scheme-theoretic Gr_{G,F^s} over an arbitrary field F with k = F̄_p coefficients and the full Gal(F^s/F). Routed to route 2, which imports GS.1 and GS4:integral-dual-group as its models.
items.originalStatement: The Geometric Satake equivalence Perv_{L^+G_{F^s}}(Gr_{G,F^s};k) ≅ Rep_k(G-hat) carries the Gal(F^s/F)-action on Gr_{G,F^s} to an action act^geom on G-hat_k, and ^LG^geom := G-hat_k ⋊_{act^geom} Gal(F^s/F). The category Rep_k(^LG^geom) is the continuously Gal(F^s/F)-equivariant objects of Rep_k(G-hat) for act^geom, and descent gives Perv_{L^+G}(Gr_G;k) ≅ Rep_k(G-hat)^{BGal(F^s/F),geom}.

review.reason: Incomplete. It leaves out what §2.1.4 (which its locator cites) states. That section defines Rep_k(^LG^alg) as a colimit over finite forms, and notes that Rep_k(Ĝ)^{BGal,geom} is the colimit of its finite-level versions because k is algebraic over F_p. It also says an isomorphism (2.1) induces an equivalence Rep_k(^LG^alg) ≃ Rep_k(Ĝ)^{BGal(F^s/F),geom}. §5 uses that equivalence to feed representations of ^LG^alg into the Satake functor. The item also omits that act^geom factors through a finite quotient.

items.name: Comparison of the algebraic and geometric L-groups (Proposition 2.1)
items.statement: Let ρ̂ be half the sum of the positive coroots of Ĝ, viewed as a cocharacter G_m → Ĝ_ad. Let cyc_p: Gal(F^s/F) → F_p^× be the mod p cyclotomic character, and χ := ρ̂ ∘ cyc_p: Gal(F^s/F) → Ĝ_ad(k). Then act^geom(γ) = act^alg(γ) ∘ Ad_{χ(γ)} for all γ (Proposition 2.1). Consequently, let χ̃: Gal(F^s/F) → Ĝ(k) be a homomorphism lifting χ whose values are fixed by act^alg. For instance χ̃ = 2ρ̂ ∘ ε, where ε: Gal(F^s/F) → k^× is a square root of cyc_p and 2ρ̂, the sum of the positive coroots, is a cocharacter of Ĝ fixed by every pinned automorphism. For such χ̃, (g,γ) ↦ (g χ̃(γ^{−1}), γ) is an isomorphism ^LG^alg ≅ ^LG^geom. A square root ε exists whenever char F > 0.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Proposition 2.1
items.note: The ρ-shift between the L-algebraic and C-algebraic normalisations. In general the two L-groups need not be isomorphic, but over a function field they are. Review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24), status check: Missing is right for the global form (Γ = Gal(F^s/F), F a global function field, k-coefficients). But GeometricSatakeAndFusion:GS4:integral-dual-group explicitly plans the local-field form: 'distinguish the geometric Weil action from the standard pinned action, with the normalization isomorphism involving rho and the chosen sqrt(q)'. It does so via FS VI.9–VI.11, the paper's own proof of Proposition 2.1. The item should cite that stage, and the route-2 design should import it and add the global k-coefficient version. The extraction marks item 8 planned by GS4 but this item missing; the two statuses should be decided together.
items.originalStatement: Let ρ be the half sum of the positive coroots of G-hat, viewed as a cocharacter G_m → G-hat_ad, cyc_p: Gal(F^s/F) → F_p^× the mod p cyclotomic character and χ = ρ ∘ cyc_p: Gal(F^s/F) → G-hat_ad(k). Then act^geom = act^alg ∘ Ad_χ. Consequently a lift χ-tilde of χ to G-hat(k), for instance from a square root of the cyclotomic character, gives an isomorphism ^LG^alg ≅ ^LG^geom by (g,γ) ↦ (g χ-tilde(γ^{-1}), γ); such a square root exists whenever char F > 0.

review.reason: The consequence is stated for an arbitrary lift χ̃ of χ, as the paper states it on p. 9, but (2.1) is a homomorphism only when χ̃ is a homomorphism whose values are fixed by act^alg, as a square-root lift is. For other lifts it fails (new issue: lift in (2.1)). Proposition 2.1 itself is stated correctly.

items.name: L-parameters and semisimplicity
items.statement: For Γ a topological group with a quotient Γ-bar acting on G-hat, an L-parameter from Γ to G-hat(k) ⋊ Γ-bar is a G-hat(k)-conjugacy class of continuous homomorphisms ρ: Γ → G-hat(k) ⋊ Γ-bar lying over the given quotient; equivalently an element of H^1_cts(Γ, G-hat(k)). ρ is semisimple (completely reducible) if whenever it factors through a parabolic ^LP^alg(k) it factors through a Levi ^LM^alg(k) of it.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Definition 2.2
items.note: GS.5 plans the reconstruction of continuous semisimple L-group parameters, including the projection to the Galois group and the conjugacy convention for nonsplit G; ES0 plans the same in the local setting. Review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24): status planned kept, layers corrected: ExcursionOperatorsAndSpectralAction:ES0 constructs centres and excursion operators and does not define L-parameters. The definition (1-cocycles, twisted conjugation, sections of the L-group projection) and complete reducibility are planned by LanglandsParameterStacks:LP0 and LP2:semisimple-characters for Γ = W_v, and GS.5 uses them for Γ = Gal(F^s/F); the definition does not depend on the coefficients.

items.name: The excursion algebra, first presentation
items.statement: Exc(Γ, ^LG^alg) is the commutative k-algebra generated by symbols S_{I,f,(γ_i)} for I a finite set, f ∈ O(G-hat_k \ (^LG^alg_k)^I / G-hat_k) and γ_i ∈ Γ, subject to: S_{∅,f,*} = f(1); f ↦ S_{I,f,(γ_i)} is a k-algebra homomorphism; S_{J,f^ζ,(γ_j)} = S_{I,f,(γ_{ζ(i)})} for ζ: I → J; the triple relation S_{I⊔I⊔I, f-tilde, (γ)×(γ')×(γ'')} = S_{I,f,(γ_i(γ'_i)^{-1}γ''_i)}; and the inflation relation reducing a function pulled back from Γ^{I\J} to the index set J.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Definition 2.3; with the generators of §2.2.1 and the relations of §2.2.2
items.note: GS.5 plans excursion operators indexed by invariant functions and Galois tuples with their relations and commutativity; ES0 plans the same construction from a finite leg set, an invariant function, creation, the Weil tuple and annihilation, with linearity, multiplication, reindexing, unit insertion and composition relations. Review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24): status planned → missing: ES0 plans excursion operators on sheaves, not the presented algebra. The presented algebra for local Weil groups is LanglandsParameterStacks:LP2:excursion-presentation (FS's free-group-cocycle presentation; its comparison with this generators-and-relations presentation, FS Cor. VIII.4.3 and the paper's Remark 2.5, belongs there), and GS.5 fixes characteristic-zero ℓ-adic coefficients. The algebra over k = F̄_p for Γ = Gal(F^s/F) is not planned. Route 2 owns it and imports LP2:excursion-presentation for the local case.

items.name: Langlands parameters from characters of the excursion algebra (Proposition 2.4)
items.statement: For any character ν: Exc(Γ, ^LG^alg) → k there is a semisimple L-parameter ρ_ν: Γ → ^LG^alg(k), for the discrete topology on Γ and unique up to Ĝ(k)-conjugacy, characterised as follows. For all n ∈ N, all f ∈ O(Ĝ_k\(^LG^alg_k)^{n+1}/Ĝ_k) and all (γ_0,...,γ_n) ∈ Γ^{n+1}, ν(S_{{0,...,n},f,(γ_0,...,γ_n)}) = f(ρ_ν(γ_0), ρ_ν(γ_1), ..., ρ_ν(γ_n)). Equivalently, ν(S_{{0,...,n},f,(γ_0γ_n,...,γ_{n−1}γ_n,γ_n)}) = f(ρ_ν(γ_0γ_n), ..., ρ_ν(γ_{n−1}γ_n), ρ_ν(γ_n)).
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Proposition 2.4
items.note: Quoted from Lafforgue §13 and Böckle–Harris–Khare–Thorne Theorem 4.5. GS.5 plans exactly this reconstruction of semisimple parameters from characters of the excursion algebra. Review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24): status planned → missing: GS.5 fixes characteristic-zero ℓ-adic coefficients; this is the modular statement (k = F̄_p, from BHKT Theorem 4.5, which notes that positive characteristic needs modifications). For Γ = W_v it is planned by LanglandsParameterStacks:LP2:semisimple-characters (FS VIII.3.8, any algebraically closed coefficient field of characteristic different from the residue characteristic), which route 2 imports. For Γ = Gal(F^s/F) with k-coefficients it is missing.
items.originalStatement: For any character ν: Exc(Γ, ^LG^alg) → k there is a semisimple L-parameter ρ_ν: Γ → ^LG^alg(k) for the discrete topology on Γ, unique up to G-hat(k)-conjugacy, characterised by ν(S_{{0,...,n}, f, (γ_0,...,γ_n)}) = f(ρ_ν(γ_0γ_n), ..., ρ_ν(γ_{n-1}γ_n), ρ_ν(γ_n)) for all n, all invariant f and all tuples.

review.reason: The characterising formula copies the paper's (2.3), which is a misprint. As printed, Proposition 2.4 is false: it contradicts relations (ii) and (iii) of §2.2.2, and for split G its right-hand side does not depend on γ_n (new issue: (2.3)). The correct condition is ν(S_{{0..n},f,(γ_0,...,γ_n)}) = f(ρ_ν(γ_0),...,ρ_ν(γ_n)).

items.name: The excursion algebra, second presentation
items.statement: Exc(Γ, ^LG^alg) is presented by generators S_{I,W,x,ξ,(γ_i)} with W ∈ Rep_k((^LG^alg)^I), x ∈ W and ξ ∈ W^* invariant under the diagonal G-hat_k, subject to six families of relations: the empty-set evaluation, functoriality along morphisms of representations, multiplicativity for ☒ and additivity for ⊕ with k-linearity in x and ξ, restriction along ζ: I → J, the coevaluation/evaluation relation encoding γ(γ')^{-1}γ'', and inflation from a subset J. The two presentations agree via S_{I,W,x,ξ,(γ_i)} = S_{I,f_{x,ξ},(γ_i)} with f_{x,ξ}((g_i)) = ⟨ξ, (g_i)·x⟩.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, §2.4; generators in §2.4.1, relations in §2.4.2, comparison in §2.4.3
items.note: This is the presentation ES0 describes (creation by a coevaluation map, a tuple of Weil elements, annihilation by evaluation, independence of the representation realising the function, by the parameter algebra's presentation), and the one GS.5 needs to construct actions. Review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24): status planned → missing: ES0 plans the operator-level analogue on Bun_G for local Weil groups, including the independence of the representation realising a function (Lafforgue's Lemme 10.6, which §2.4.3 uses); the presented algebra for local Weil groups is LanglandsParameterStacks:LP2:excursion-presentation; GS.5 is characteristic zero. The second presentation over k for Γ = Gal(F^s/F), with its comparison with the first, is not planned. Route 2 owns it and imports LP2:excursion-presentation. Corrected domain contract: x and ξ are only diagonal-Ĝ-invariant. Do not strengthen them to diagonal-L-group-invariant. Their maps are applied through the geometric functors of item 56; the L-group representation supplies the separate descent structure and hence the middle Γ^I-action (E60).

beforeRedteamFix.note: This is the presentation ES0 describes (creation by a coevaluation map, a tuple of Weil elements, annihilation by evaluation, independence of the representation realising the function, by the parameter algebra's presentation), and the one GS.5 needs to construct actions. Review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24): status planned → missing: ES0 plans the operator-level analogue on Bun_G for local Weil groups, including the independence of the representation realising a function (Lafforgue's Lemme 10.6, which §2.4.3 uses); the presented algebra for local Weil groups is LanglandsParameterStacks:LP2:excursion-presentation; GS.5 is characteristic zero. The second presentation over k for Γ = Gal(F^s/F), with its comparison with the first, is not planned. Route 2 owns it and imports LP2:excursion-presentation.

unitTests.name: Feng.item13.quadraticCharacter
unitTests.statement: For split G_m, p=3, and the unramified quadratic character χ of Γ, W=k(χ) has trivial Ĝ-action. x=ξ=1 are permitted generators although x:1→W is not an L-group morphism. The corrected action must be χ(γ) id_M; for odd degree γ this is −id_M, not undefined and not a discarded generator.

items.name: Admissible homomorphisms of L-groups
items.statement: A homomorphism φ: ^LH^alg → ^LG^alg of pro-algebraic groups over k (H and G reductive over the same field F, Γ its Galois or Weil group) is admissible if it lies over the identity of Γ, i.e. the projections satisfy pr_G ∘ φ = pr_H.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, §2.5
items.note: RG2.5 plans the L-group with its projection to the Galois group, of which admissibility is the compatibility condition. Review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24): status planned → missing: ReductiveGroupsPartII:RG2.5 supplies ^LG and its projection to Γ, over local fields only. No layer defines homomorphisms of L-groups over Γ in general: ExcursionOperatorsAndSpectralAction:ES6:functoriality covers only isogenies, products and Weil restriction, and EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison:ET.0 only endoscopic L-morphisms. Routed to route 2 with items 15 and 16.
items.originalStatement: A homomorphism φ: ^LH^alg → ^LG^alg is admissible if it lies over the identity of Γ.

review.reason: The paper's 'homomorphism of L-groups' is a homomorphism of pro-algebraic groups over k, and Lemma 2.7 needs that for Res_φ: Rep_k(^LG^alg) → Rep_k(^LH^alg) to exist. The item's bare 'homomorphism' leaves it out.

items.name: Functoriality for excursion algebras (Lemma 2.7)
items.statement: Let φ: ^LH^alg → ^LG^alg be an admissible homomorphism of pro-algebraic groups over k. Then there is a k-algebra homomorphism φ^*: Exc(Γ,^LG^alg) → Exc(Γ,^LH^alg), given on generators by S_{I,V,x,ξ,(γ_i)} ↦ S_{I,Res_{φ^I}(V),x,ξ,(γ_i)}, equivalently S_{I,f,(γ_i)} ↦ S_{I,f∘φ^I,(γ_i)}. For every character ν of Exc(Γ,^LH^alg), the parameter ρ_{ν∘φ^*} is the semisimplification (φ∘ρ_ν)^{ss}: the unique semisimple parameter with the same excursion character as φ∘ρ_ν. It equals φ∘ρ_ν whenever φ∘ρ_ν is semisimple, in particular for φ = φ_BC.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Lemma 2.7
items.note: This is Langlands functoriality translated into the excursion algebra; it is what makes the whole strategy of the paper possible. No layer of the atlas plans functoriality of the excursion algebra along an L-homomorphism. Review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24), status check: Missing is right. ExcursionOperatorsAndSpectralAction:ES6:functoriality plans excursion comparisons only for isogenies, products and Weil restriction, in the local FS setting, and not along an arbitrary admissible φ.
items.originalStatement: For φ: ^LH^alg → ^LG^alg admissible there is a homomorphism φ^*: Exc(Γ, ^LG^alg) → Exc(Γ, ^LH^alg), given on generators by S_{I,V,x,ξ,(γ_i)} ↦ S_{I,Res_φ V, Res_φ x, Res_φ ξ, (γ_i)}, which on k-points of the corresponding spectra sends ρ ∈ H^1(Γ, H-hat(k)) to φ ∘ ρ ∈ H^1(Γ, G-hat(k)).

review.reason: The final clause is false for a general admissible φ. The k-points of Spec Exc are semisimple parameters (Proposition 2.4), and ν∘φ^* depends only on the semisimplification of φ∘ρ_ν, so the induced map sends ρ to (φ∘ρ)^{ss}. In characteristic p, φ∘ρ need not be semisimple (new issue: Lemma 2.7). For φ = φ_BC the composite is semisimple, but the paper does not prove it (new coverage item).

items.name: The base change homomorphism of L-groups φ_BC
items.statement: For H reductive over F and G = Res_{E/F}(H_E) with E/F cyclic of degree p, φ_BC: ^LH^alg → ^LG^alg is (h,γ) ↦ (Δ(h),γ) with Δ the diagonal H-hat → H-hat^p = G-hat; the same formula defines φ_BC^geom, and the two are compatible with the comparison isomorphism provided the same square root of the cyclotomic character is used for H and for G. φ_BC^*: Exc(Γ, ^LG^alg) → Exc(Γ, ^LH^alg) is the induced map.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Definition 2.8
items.note: The compatibility of φ_BC with both normalisations of the L-group is what lets the geometric argument (which produces the geometric L-group) be read as a statement about the algebraic one. Review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24), status check: Missing is right. ExcursionOperatorsAndSpectralAction:ES6:functoriality plans the Shapiro equivalence for Weil restriction in the local FS setting. The route-2 design can import it for the new semisimplicity lemma, but no layer plans φ_BC or its compatibility with the two L-groups. The statement matches Definition 2.8. The compatibility with (2.1) holds for square-root lifts, because 2ρ̂_G = Δ ∘ 2ρ̂_H.

items.name: Flat and perfect complexes over the group ring
items.statement: Let k be an algebraic closure of F_p, Λ ∈ {k, W(k)}, σ a generator of a cyclic group ⟨σ⟩ of order p and Λ[σ] its group ring. Let Y be a separated scheme locally of finite type over a field of characteristic ≠ p, and D^b_c(Y;Λ[σ]) ⊂ D^b(Y;Λ[σ]) the bounded constructible and bounded derived categories of étale Λ[σ]-sheaves (Λ-adic sheaves). Perf(Y;Λ[σ]) ⊂ D^b_c(Y;Λ[σ]) is the full subcategory of complexes whose stalks at all geometric points of Y are perfect over Λ[σ]. Flat^b(Y;Λ[σ]) ⊂ D^b(Y;Λ[σ]) is the full subcategory of bounded complexes whose stalks at all geometric points of Y are represented by bounded complexes of flat, not necessarily finitely generated, Λ[σ]-modules.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, §3.1, the paragraph before Definition 3.1 (Perf) and Definition 3.1 (Flat^b), p. 13
items.note: The enlargement from Perf to Flat^b is what makes the theory work for locally finite type schemes such as moduli of shtukas; see Remark 3.10.
items.originalStatement: For Y a separated locally finite type scheme over a field and Λ a p-adic coefficient ring, Perf(Y;Λ[σ]) ⊂ D^b_c(Y;Λ[σ]) is the full subcategory of complexes with perfect stalks, and Flat^b(Y;Λ[σ]) ⊂ D^b(Y;Λ[σ]) the full subcategory of bounded complexes whose stalks at geometric points are represented by bounded complexes of flat, not necessarily finite, Λ[σ]-modules.

review.reason: Missing hypothesis: the paper's standing assumptions of §3.1 are that the base field has characteristic ≠ p (so p is invertible and the Λ-adic étale formalism applies), that ⟨σ⟩ is cyclic of order p and that Λ ∈ {k, W(k)}; the item says only 'a separated locally finite type scheme over a field'. Also Perf(Y;Λ[σ]) is defined in the paragraph before Definition 3.1, not in it.

items.originalLocator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Definition 3.1

items.name: Flat^b is finite tor-amplitude (Lemma 3.2)
items.statement: Flat^b(Y;k[σ]) ⊂ D^b(Y;k[σ]) coincides with the full subcategory of objects which locally have finite tor-amplitude over k[σ].
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Lemma 3.2
items.note: Proved using that k[σ] is Artinian, so flat equals projective and the finitistic dimension is zero, whence a complex concentrated in degrees [a,b] with finite tor-amplitude has tor-amplitude in [a,b]. Not used essentially, but it identifies the subcategory.

items.name: The constructible and ind-constructible Tate categories
items.statement: The constructible Tate category of Y is the Verdier quotient D^b_c(Y;Λ[σ])/Perf(Y;Λ[σ]), written Perf(Y;T_Λ); the bounded ind-constructible Tate category is Shv(Y;T_Λ) := D^b(Y;Λ[σ])/Flat^b(Y;Λ[σ]). The projections are both written T^*, and the induced functor Perf(Y;T_Λ) → Shv(Y;T_Λ) is conservative.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Definition 3.3
items.note: Treumann's Tate category, extended from finite type to locally finite type. Nothing in the atlas plans Verdier quotients of equivariant derived categories by perfect or flat complexes. Review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24), status check: Status 'missing' is right for the sheaf-level Tate categories, but the note's 'nothing in the atlas plans Verdier quotients' should not lead the design job to rebuild the quotient: Mathlib at the pin has it (CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.IsTriangulated, ObjectProperty.trW with left and right calculus of fractions, MorphismProperty.Localization with the Pretriangulated/IsTriangulated instances of Triangulated.Localization), and the point case Perf(pt;T_k) = D^b(mod k[σ])/K^b(proj k[σ]) = D_sg(k[σ]) ≃ stmod-k[σ] is planned by tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/StablePeriodicCurved#layer-2-self-injective-modules-total-acyclicity-and-singularities (k[σ] is a finite-dimensional self-injective algebra). Cite both. The ind-constructible Shv(−;T_Λ) is used in the paper only with Λ = k outside §3, so the non-constructible W(k)-adic formalism is not needed downstream.

items.name: The shift-by-2 functor is the identity on the Tate category (Example 3.4)
items.statement: Let pt be the spectrum of a separably closed field of characteristic ≠ p; Shv(pt;T_Λ) = D^b(Λ[σ])/Flat^b(Λ[σ]). The shift functor [2] on Shv(pt;T_Λ) is isomorphic to the identity: for V ∈ D^b(Λ[σ]), represented by a bounded complex of Λ[σ]-modules flat over Λ, tensoring V over Λ (σ acting diagonally) with the exact sequence 0 → Λ →(N) Λ[σ] →(1−σ) Λ[σ] →(ε) Λ → 0 gives an exact complex 0 → V → V⊗_ΛΛ[σ] → V⊗_ΛΛ[σ] → V → 0, hence a natural map V → V[2] in D^b(Λ[σ]) whose cone lies in the triangulated subcategory generated by V⊗_ΛΛ[σ] ∈ Flat^b(Λ[σ]); so V ≅ V[2] naturally in the Tate category.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Example 3.4
items.note: This is why perverse sheaves cannot be seen in the Tate category and parity sheaves must replace them; it is the conceptual pivot of §4.
items.originalStatement: On the Tate category over a point — the spectrum of a separably closed field — which is D^b(Λ[σ])/Flat^b(Λ[σ]), the shift-by-2 functor is isomorphic to the identity functor, as the nullhomotopic complex 0 → V → V⊗Λ[σ] →(1-σ) V⊗Λ[σ] → V → 0 has its middle two terms projecting to 0.

review.reason: The item repeats the paper's word 'nullhomotopic': the complex 0 → V → V⊗Λ[σ] → V⊗Λ[σ] → V → 0 is exact (acyclic) but not nullhomotopic over Λ[σ] (for Λ = V = k a contraction would need a k[σ]-linear h: k[σ] → k with h∘N = id, but h(N) = p·h(1) = 0). Exactness is what the argument uses. The maps (norm, 1−σ, augmentation, tensored with V, σ acting diagonally) and the Λ-flatness of V needed for exactness when Λ = W(k) are unstated.

items.name: The Smith operation
items.statement: For Y a separated locally finite type scheme with an admissible σ-action, i: Y^σ ↪ Y the fixed locus and the identification D^b_σ(Y^σ;Λ) ≅ D^b(Y^σ;Λ[σ]), the Smith operation is Psm := T^* ∘ i^*, defined both as D^b_{c,σ}(Y;Λ) → Perf(Y^σ;T_Λ) and as D^b_σ(Y;Λ) → Shv(Y^σ;T_Λ); the two are compatible under Perf(Y^σ;T_Λ) → Shv(Y^σ;T_Λ).
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, §3.2, equations (3.2), (3.3), (3.4) and Remark 3.5, pp. 14–15
items.note: Treumann's functor, in the locally finite type generality the paper needs. Admissibility of the action is automatic when Y is exhausted by quasi-projective schemes over a field.
items.originalLocator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, §3.2; equations (3.3) and (3.4)

items.name: Pushforward along a free quotient is flat (Lemma 3.6)
items.statement: Let k be an algebraic closure of F_p, Λ ∈ {k, W(k)}, ⟨σ⟩ ≅ Z/pZ and Λ[σ] its group ring; all schemes are separated and locally of finite type over a field of characteristic ≠ p. Let Y carry a free admissible σ-action (SGA 1, Exposé V, Définition 1.7) and let q: Y → Y/σ be the quotient, on which σ acts trivially. For every F ∈ D^b_σ(Y;Λ), q_*F ∈ D^b_σ(Y/σ;Λ) ≅ D^b(Y/σ;Λ[σ]) lies in Flat^b(Y/σ;Λ[σ]); indeed for a geometric point ȳ of Y/σ and a lift x̄ to Y, (q_*F)_ȳ ≅ F_x̄ ⊗_Λ Λ[σ].
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Lemma 3.6
items.note: The stalk of q_*F at a geometric point is F_x-bar ⊗_Λ Λ[σ], visibly flat over Λ[σ].
items.originalStatement: If the σ-action on Y is free with quotient q: Y → Y/σ, then q_* F ∈ Flat^b(Y/σ;Λ[σ]) for every F ∈ D^b(Y;Λ[σ]).

review.reason: The item copies the paper's 'F ∈ D^b(Y;Λ[σ])', which is a misprint (see the new issue): σ acts freely, hence non-trivially, on Y, and in the paper D^b(Y;Λ[σ]) means non-equivariant sheaves of Λ[σ]-modules (compare (3.2)). Read literally the lemma is false: the constant sheaf Λ with trivial Λ[σ]-structure has q_*Λ with stalks Λ^p carrying the trivial σ-action, not flat over k[σ] when Λ = k. The intended F is a σ-equivariant complex, as the stalk formula (q_*F)_ȳ ≅ F_x̄ ⊗_Λ Λ[σ] and the use in Proposition 3.12 show. Admissibility, which gives the quotient, should be stated.

items.name: Nearby stalks along the fixed locus are flat (Lemma 3.7)
items.statement: Let k be an algebraic closure of F_p, Λ ∈ {k, W(k)}, ⟨σ⟩ ≅ Z/pZ and Λ[σ] its group ring; all schemes are separated and locally of finite type over a field of characteristic ≠ p. Let Y carry an admissible σ-action, U := Y ∖ Y^σ and j: U ↪ Y the open immersion. For every F ∈ D^b_σ(U;Λ) and every geometric point ȳ of Y^σ, the stalk (Rj_*F)_ȳ ∈ D^b_σ(ȳ;Λ) ≅ D^b(Λ[σ]) lies in Flat^b(ȳ;Λ[σ]).
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Lemma 3.7
items.note: Proved by total ramification of q at y-bar and the preservation of finite tor-amplitude by Rj-bar_*.
items.originalStatement: Let U := Y \ Y^σ with open immersion j. Then for any F ∈ D^b(U;Λ[σ]) and any geometric point y-bar of Y^σ, the stalk (Rj_* F)_{y-bar} lies in Flat^b(y-bar;Λ[σ]).

review.reason: Same misprint as Lemma 3.6: 'F ∈ D^b(U;Λ[σ])' must be F ∈ D^b_σ(U;Λ), since σ acts freely on U. Literally read, the lemma is false: for Y = A^1 with σ(x) = ζx and F the constant sheaf k with trivial k[σ]-structure, (Rj_*F)_0 has cohomology k in degrees 0 and 1 with trivial σ and is formal, so it is not in Flat^b(k[σ]); with the equivariant structure it is the perfect complex k[σ] →(1−σ) k[σ].

items.name: i^! and i^* agree in the Tate category (Lemma 3.8)
items.statement: Let k be an algebraic closure of F_p, Λ ∈ {k, W(k)}, ⟨σ⟩ ≅ Z/pZ and Λ[σ] its group ring; all schemes are separated and locally of finite type over a field of characteristic ≠ p. Let Y have bounded dimension and an admissible σ-action, and let i: Y^σ ↪ Y be the σ-fixed closed subscheme. For every F ∈ D^b_σ(Y;Λ), the cone of the natural map i^!F → i^*F in D^b_σ(Y^σ;Λ) ≅ D^b(Y^σ;Λ[σ]) lies in Flat^b(Y^σ;Λ[σ]); hence T^* i^!F ≅ T^* i^*F = Psm(F) in Shv(Y^σ;T_Λ).
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Lemma 3.8
items.note: This is the source of the good behaviour of Psm: in the Tate category the two restriction functors are identified. Proved for finite type schemes by Riche–Williamson, following Treumann in topology.
items.originalStatement: For i: Y^σ ↪ Y and any F ∈ D^b_σ(Y;Λ), the cone of i^! F → i^* F belongs to Flat^b(Y^σ;Λ[σ]).

review.reason: Missing hypothesis, inherited from the paper (new issue): Y must have bounded dimension (as in Lemma 3.9 and §3.3). Without it, i^!F and the cone i^*Rj_*j^*F need not be bounded. For Y = ⊔_{n≥1} A^n with σ acting by a primitive p-th root of unity and F = k, i^!F = ⊕_n k(−n)[−2n] on Y^σ = ⊔ {0}, so the cone is not in Flat^b ⊂ D^b. Every use (Appendix A §A.1, Proposition 4.15) is for varieties.

items.name: Proper pushforward preserves Flat^b (Lemma 3.9)
items.statement: If f: Y → S is a locally finite type separated σ-equivariant morphism of locally finite type schemes of bounded dimension, then Rf_!: D^b(Y;Λ[σ]) → D^b(S;Λ[σ]) carries Flat^b(Y;Λ[σ]) into Flat^b(S;Λ[σ]).
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Lemma 3.9; with Remark 3.10
items.note: Remark 3.10 records that the statement is false with Flat^b replaced by Perf, which is exactly why the ind-constructible Tate category is needed outside the finite type situation.

items.name: Pushforward from a free action lands in Flat^b (Corollary 3.11)
items.statement: Let k be an algebraic closure of F_p, Λ ∈ {k, W(k)}, ⟨σ⟩ ≅ Z/pZ and Λ[σ] its group ring; all schemes are separated and locally of finite type over a field of characteristic ≠ p. Let f: Y → S be a separated morphism, locally of finite type, of bounded dimension, with σ acting trivially on S and freely and admissibly on Y, and f σ-equivariant. Then Rf_!: D^b_σ(Y;Λ) → D^b_σ(S;Λ) ≅ D^b(S;Λ[σ]) lands in Flat^b(S;Λ[σ]). (Factor f = f̄∘q through q: Y → Y/σ; apply Lemma 3.6 to q_! = q_* and Lemma 3.9 to f̄_!.)
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Corollary 3.11
items.note: Factor f through Y/σ and combine Lemmas 3.6 and 3.9. This is the vanishing that makes equivariant localisation work.
items.originalStatement: If in addition σ acts trivially on S and freely on Y, then Rf_!: D^b(Y;Λ[σ]) → D^b(S;Λ[σ]) lands in Flat^b(S;Λ[σ]).

review.reason: Two misprints of the paper are handled inconsistently. The item silently corrects the target 'Flat^b(Y;Λ[σ])' to Flat^b(S;Λ[σ]), which is right but should be recorded (new issue). It copies the source 'D^b(Y;Λ[σ])', which must be D^b_σ(Y;Λ) because σ acts freely on Y. Literally, the constant sheaf Λ with trivial Λ[σ]-structure gives RΓ_c(Y;Λ) with trivial action, not flat. The proof applies Corollary 3.11 to j_!j^*F with F ∈ D^b_σ. Admissibility of the action on Y, needed to form Y/σ, is a standing assumption of §3.2 and should be stated.

items.name: The six operations on Tate categories
items.statement: (a) (§3.3.) Let k be an algebraic closure of F_p, Λ ∈ {k, W(k)}, ⟨σ⟩ ≅ Z/pZ and Λ[σ] its group ring; all schemes are separated and locally of finite type over a field of characteristic ≠ p. Let f: Y → S be σ-equivariant, locally of finite type, of bounded dimension, with admissible σ-actions, and f^σ: Y^σ → S^σ its restriction. The pullback (f^σ)^*: D^b(S^σ;Λ[σ]) → D^b(Y^σ;Λ[σ]) preserves stalks, hence Flat^b and Perf, and descends to f^*: Shv(S^σ;T_Λ) → Shv(Y^σ;T_Λ) and f^*: Perf(S^σ;T_Λ) → Perf(Y^σ;T_Λ). By Lemma 3.9, R(f^σ)_! descends to Rf_!: Shv(Y^σ;T_Λ) → Shv(S^σ;T_Λ), in general not to the constructible categories (Remark 3.10). (b) (§A.1.) If moreover Y and S are varieties (of finite type): f^* and Rf_! descend to functors between Perf(S^σ;T_Λ) and Perf(Y^σ;T_Λ); Verdier duality on D^b_{c,σ}(Y^σ;Λ) preserves Perf(Y^σ;Λ[σ]) and descends to D: Perf(Y^σ;T_Λ) → Perf(Y^σ;T_Λ); set f^! := D∘f^*∘D and Rf_* := D∘Rf_!∘D. Psm: D^b_{c,σ}(−;Λ) → Perf((−)^σ;T_Λ) commutes with f^* and f^! (§A.1.1, the second by Lemma 3.8) and with Rf_! and Rf_* (§A.1.2, as in Proposition 3.12, then by duality and Lemma 3.8).
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, §3.3.1 and §3.3.2, pp. 16–17; and Appendix A, §A.1 with §A.1.1 and §A.1.2, pp. 56–57
items.note: The slogan is that the Smith operation commutes with all operations; the compatibility with Rf_* follows from that with Rf_! by duality and Lemma 3.8.
items.originalStatement: For f: Y → S σ-equivariant, locally finite type, of bounded dimension: f^* descends to Shv(S^σ;T_Λ) → Shv(Y^σ;T_Λ) and to the constructible Tate categories since it preserves stalks; Rf_! descends by Lemma 3.9; and on the constructible Tate categories Verdier duality D descends, so f^! := D f^* D and Rf_* := D f_! D are defined. The Smith operation commutes with f^*, f^!, Rf_* and Rf_!.

review.reason: The item merges two settings the paper keeps apart. In §3.3 (locally finite type, bounded dimension) only f^* on Shv and Perf of the fixed loci and Rf_! on the ind-constructible Shv are defined, and only the commutation of Psm with Rf_! is proved (Proposition 3.12). Rf_! does not descend to the constructible Perf there (Remark 3.10). So 'on the constructible Tate categories ... Rf_* := D f_! D' and 'Psm commutes with f^*, f^!, Rf_*, Rf_!' do not hold in the item's locally-finite-type generality. They are §A.1's statements for f a σ-equivariant morphism of varieties (finite type) over a field of characteristic ℓ ≠ p, on the constructible categories Perf(−;T_Λ).

items.originalLocator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, §3.3; and Appendix A §A.1

items.name: The Smith operation commutes with proper pushforward (Proposition 3.12)
items.statement: Let k be an algebraic closure of F_p, Λ ∈ {k, W(k)}, ⟨σ⟩ ≅ Z/pZ and Λ[σ] its group ring; all schemes are separated and locally of finite type over a field of characteristic ≠ p. Let f: Y → S be σ-equivariant, locally of finite type, of bounded dimension, with admissible σ-actions on Y and S. Then Psm ∘ Rf_! ≅ Rf^σ_! ∘ Psm as functors D^b_σ(Y;Λ) → Shv(S^σ;T_Λ), where Rf^σ_!: Shv(Y^σ;T_Λ) → Shv(S^σ;T_Λ) is the descended proper pushforward along f|_{Y^σ}: Y^σ → S^σ (§3.3.2).
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Proposition 3.12, p. 17
items.note: This is the paper's form of equivariant localisation; the proof uses the triangle j_!j^*F → F → i_*i^*F and the vanishing of Rf_!j_!j^*F in the Tate category by Corollary 3.11.
items.originalStatement: For f: Y → S σ-equivariant locally finite type of bounded dimension, the square formed by Psm and Rf_! from D^b_σ(Y;Λ) and D^b_σ(S;Λ) to Shv(Y^σ;T_Λ) and Shv(S^σ;T_Λ) commutes.

review.reason: Missing hypotheses of the standing assumption of §3.3: Y and S are separated schemes, locally of finite type over a field of characteristic ≠ p, with admissible σ-actions. Admissibility is used, since the proof applies Corollary 3.11 to U = Y ∖ Y^σ, which needs the quotient U/σ. The item says only 'f σ-equivariant locally finite type of bounded dimension'.

items.originalLocator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Proposition 3.12

items.name: Tate cohomology of modules, complexes and sheaves
items.statement: For a Λ[σ]-module M, T^0(M) = M^σ/N·M and T^1(M) = ker(N: M → M)/(1−σ)·M, N = 1+σ+⋯+σ^{p−1}. The exact sequence 0 → Λ →(N) Λ[σ] →(1−σ) Λ[σ] →(ε) Λ → 0 gives a map Λ → Λ[2] in D^b(Λ[σ]) (3.5). For a bounded-below complex C of Λ[σ]-modules, T^i(C) := colim_n Hom_{D(Λ[σ])}(Λ, C[i+2n]) along (3.5); T^i is 2-periodic in i and descends to functors T^i: D^b(Λ[σ]) → Mod_{T^0(Λ)}. For Λ = k, flat k[σ]-modules are free, T^i kills Flat^b(k[σ]) and factors as T^i: Shv(pt;T_k) → Vect_k; for bounded C, T^i(C) ≅ Hom_{Shv(pt;T_k)}(k, T^*C[i]) (Remark 3.13). For S with trivial σ-action and F ∈ D^b(S;Λ[σ]), T^iF := colim_n Hom-sheaf_{D(S;Λ[σ])}(Λ, F[i+2n]) (transition maps from (3.5)) is an étale sheaf of T^0(Λ)-modules, and for Λ = k, T^iF ≅ Hom-sheaf_{Shv(S;T_k)}(k, T^*F[i]).
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, §3.4 (first display), §3.4.1 with Remark 3.13, and §3.4.2, pp. 17–18
items.note: The module-level T^0, T^1 are Tate cohomology of a finite cyclic group in degrees 0 and -1, which the libraries have; the complex-level and sheaf-level versions, with the colimit definition through the 2-periodicity map, are not. Review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24), status check: Status 'missing' is right. The point case can be built on the stable module category stmod-k[σ] planned by tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/StablePeriodicCurved#layer-2-self-injective-modules-total-acyclicity-and-singularities, and the module case on the library Tate cohomology of item 105.
items.originalStatement: For a Λ[σ]-module M, T^0(M) = M^σ/N·M and T^1(M) = ker(N)/(1-σ)M. For a bounded below complex C, T^i(C) = colim_n Hom_{D(Λ[σ])}(Λ, C[i+2n]) along the map Λ → Λ[2] induced by 0 → Λ → Λ[σ] →(1-σ) Λ[σ] → Λ → 0; it is 2-periodic in i, descends to D^b(Λ[σ]) and, for Λ = k, factors through the Tate category. For F ∈ D^b(S;Λ[σ]) with S carrying the trivial action, the Tate cohomology sheaves are T^i F = colim_n Hom-sheaf(Λ, F[i+2n]), and for Λ = k, T^i F ≅ Hom-sheaf_{Shv(S;T_k)}(k, T^* F[i]).

review.reason: Accurate, but it omits Remark 3.13, the point form of the Hom description that the sheaf form generalises and that §5 uses: for bounded C, T^i(C) ≅ Hom_{Shv(pt;T_k)}(k, T^*C[i]).

items.name: Tate cohomology of a trivial action (Lemma 3.14)
items.statement: If C ∈ D^b(k[σ]) is inflated from D^b(k), i.e. σ acts trivially, then T^* C ≅ H^*(C) ⊗ T^*(k) with k carrying the trivial σ-action.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Lemma 3.14, p. 18
items.note: This identity is what converts Tate cohomology of the shtuka stack for H back into ordinary cohomology, in equation (5.6) of the paper. Review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24): Statement exact. The note has the wrong cross-reference: the identity T^*(Sht_{H,D,I};F) ≅ H^*_c(Sht_{H,D,I}|_{η̄^I};F) ⊗ T^*(k) derived from Lemma 3.14 is equation (5.8), p. 36, not (5.6).
items.originalLocator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Lemma 3.14

items.name: Relative Tate cohomology and the long exact sequence
items.statement: Let k be an algebraic closure of F_p, Λ ∈ {k, W(k)}, ⟨σ⟩ ≅ Z/pZ and Λ[σ] its group ring; all schemes are separated and locally of finite type over a field of characteristic ≠ p. Let f: Y → S be as in §3.3 (σ-equivariant, locally of finite type, of bounded dimension, admissible actions) with σ acting trivially on S. For F ∈ D^b_σ(Y;k), Rf_!F ∈ D^b_σ(S;k) ≅ D^b(S;k[σ]), and its Tate cohomology sheaves T^iRf_!F (§3.4.2) are the relative Tate cohomology of F; if S is the spectrum of a separably closed field, T^i(Y;F) := T^i(Rf_!F). If σ also acts trivially on Y, F ↦ Rf_!F factors through Shv(Y;T_k) (Lemma 3.9), so T^iRf_! is a functor on Shv(Y;T_k) (Remark 3.15). A distinguished triangle F' → F → F'' in D^b_σ(Y;k) gives a 2-periodic long exact sequence ⋯ → T^{−1}Rf_!F'' → T^0Rf_!F' → T^0Rf_!F → T^0Rf_!F'' → T^1Rf_!F' → T^1Rf_!F → T^1Rf_!F'' → T^2Rf_!F' → ⋯.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, §3.4.3 with Remark 3.15, and §3.4.4, p. 18
items.note: The long exact sequence of Tate cohomology of a finite group is in the libraries at the level of modules; the relative version for a morphism of schemes is not.
items.originalStatement: For F ∈ D^b_σ(Y;k) and f: Y → S with S carrying the trivial σ-action, T^i Rf_! F is the relative Tate cohomology; when S is the spectrum of a separably closed field one writes T^i(Y;F). A distinguished triangle F' → F → F'' in D^b_σ(Y;k) gives a long exact sequence ··· → T^0 Rf_! F' → T^0 Rf_! F → T^0 Rf_! F'' → T^1 Rf_! F' → ···, 2-periodic.

review.reason: Accurate, but it omits Remark 3.15 (same subsection): when σ acts trivially on Y and on S, F ↦ Rf_!F factors through Shv(Y;T_k) by Lemma 3.9, so T^iRf_! is a functor on Shv(Y;T_k). This is the form used when (3.6) and (5.16) apply T^i to RΓ_c(Y^σ; Psm F).

items.originalLocator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, §3.4.3; and §3.4.4

items.name: Equivariant localisation for Tate cohomology
items.statement: Let k be an algebraic closure of F_p, Λ ∈ {k, W(k)}, ⟨σ⟩ ≅ Z/pZ and Λ[σ] its group ring; all schemes are separated and locally of finite type over a field of characteristic ≠ p. Let f: Y → S be σ-equivariant, locally of finite type, of bounded dimension, with admissible σ-actions. For F ∈ D^b_σ(Y;k), Proposition 3.12 gives Psm(Rf_!F) ≅ R(f|_{Y^σ})_! Psm(F) in Shv(S^σ;T_k). In particular, if S = L is the spectrum of a separably closed field with trivial σ-action, then T^*RΓ_c(Y;F) ≅ RΓ_c(Y^σ;Psm(F)) in Shv(L;T_k), where T^* is the projection D^b(L;k[σ]) → Shv(L;T_k); applying T^i gives T^i(Y;F) ≅ T^iRΓ_c(Y^σ;Psm(F)). This contains the classical localisation theorems of Smith theory, e.g. Quillen 1971, Theorem 4.2.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, §3.4.5, equation (3.6), p. 19
items.note: The statement that links this sheaf-theoretic formalism to classical Smith theory, and the form in which it is applied to shtukas.
items.originalStatement: Proposition 3.12 specialises to: for F ∈ D^b_σ(Y;k) and L the spectrum of a separably closed field with trivial σ-action, T^* RΓ_c(Y;F) ≅ RΓ_c(Y^σ; Psm(F)) in Shv(L;T_k). This encompasses the classical equivariant localisation theorems of Smith theory, for instance Quillen's Theorem 4.2.

review.reason: Wrong locator: the formula is equation (3.6) on p. 19 (in both the published version and arXiv v6); the paper has no equation (3.11). The statement also omits the hypotheses on Y. Y is a separated scheme, locally of finite type over L (the paper tacitly takes S = L), of bounded dimension, with admissible σ-action. The general form of Proposition 3.12 it specialises, over a base S, is also left out.

items.originalLocator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, §3.4.5; equation (3.11)

items.name: JMW stratifications, parity complexes and parity sheaves
items.statement: Let Λ be a complete local PID and Y a stratified variety over a separably closed field of characteristic ≠ p whose stratification S = {Y_λ} is JMW: Ext^i(L,L') between finite Λ-free local systems on a stratum is Λ-free and vanishes for i odd. Fix a pariversity †: S → Z/2Z, here always the dimension pariversity. F ∈ D^b_S(Y;Λ) is even if for every λ the cohomology sheaves of i_λ^*F and i_λ^!F are Λ-free and supported in degrees ≡ †(Y_λ) mod 2, odd analogously, and a parity complex is a direct sum of an even and an odd complex. A parity sheaf is an indecomposable parity complex whose restriction to the dense stratum of its support is L[dim Y_λ]; if it exists it is unique and written E(λ,L).
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, §4.1
items.note: Kac–Moody and in particular affine flag varieties over separably closed fields are JMW. Nothing in the atlas plans parity sheaves; EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves plans the perverse t-structure but parity is a different, mod 2 condition.

items.name: Structure of indecomposable parity complexes (Theorem 4.1)
items.statement: Let F be an indecomposable parity complex. Then its support is irreducible, hence of the form Y-bar_λ; i_λ^*F is a shifted Λ-free local system L[m]; and any indecomposable parity complex supported on Y-bar_λ extending L[m] is isomorphic to F.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Theorem 4.1
items.note: Juteau–Mautner–Williamson Theorem 2.12, the uniqueness statement that makes E(λ,L) well defined.

items.name: Tate-even, Tate-odd and Tate-parity complexes
items.statement: For F ∈ Perf_S(Y;T_O) with O = W(k) and a pariversity †: F is ?-Tate-even for ? ∈ {*,!} if T^{†(Y_λ)+1}(i_λ^? F) = 0 for every stratum, ?-Tate-odd if F[1] is ?-Tate-even, Tate-even (odd) if both * and !, and a Tate-parity complex if it is isomorphic in Perf_S(Y;T_O) to a direct sum of a Tate-even and a Tate-odd complex. A Tate-parity sheaf is an indecomposable Tate-parity complex whose restriction to the dense stratum of its support is T^*ε^*L[dim Y_λ] for an indecomposable O-free local system L; it is unique, written E_T(λ,L).
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Definition 4.2; and Definition 4.4
items.note: Leslie–Lonergan's notion. Integral coefficients are essential: Ext^*_{Perf(T_O)}(T^*O, T^*O) = ⊕_i k[2i] is supported in even degrees, which is what the JMW condition needs.

items.name: Structure of indecomposable Tate-parity complexes (Proposition 4.3)
items.statement: Let F be an indecomposable Tate-parity complex. Then its support is Y-bar_λ for a unique stratum, and two indecomposable Tate-parity complexes with the same support and isomorphic restriction to the dense stratum of that support are isomorphic.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Proposition 4.3
items.note: Leslie–Lonergan Theorem 5.5.6, proved by the argument of Juteau–Mautner–Williamson Theorem 2.12.

items.name: Modular reduction to the Tate category (Proposition 4.5)
items.statement: Let ε^*: D^b_c(Y;O) → D^b_c(Y;O[σ]) be inflation along the augmentation. (1) If F ∈ D^b_S(Y;O) is even (odd) then T^*ε^*F is Tate-even (Tate-odd). (2) If the parity sheaf E = E(λ,L) exists and Hom_{D^b_S(Y;O)}(E,E[n]) = 0 for all n < 0 — for instance if E is perverse — then E_T(λ,L) exists and T^*ε^*E(λ,L) ≅ E_T(λ,L).
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Proposition 4.5
items.note: The proof uses Hom_{Perf(Y;T_O)}(T^*ε^*F, T^*ε^*G) ≅ ⊕_{i∈Z} Hom_{D^b_S(Y;k)}(F F, F G[2i]). The slogan is: if all parity sheaves exist with vanishing negative self-Exts then T^*∘ε^* is a bijection from parity sheaves to Tate-parity sheaves.

items.name: Normalized parity sheaves and the lifting functor
items.statement: A normalized (Tate-)parity complex is a direct sum of (Tate-)parity sheaves with no shifts, giving Parity^0_S(Y;O), Parity^0_S(Y;k) and Parity^0_S(Y;T_O). Assuming all parity sheaves exist with vanishing negative self-Exts there is a lifting functor L: Parity^0_S(Y;T_O) → Parity^0_S(Y;k) sending E_T(λ,L) to E(λ,L⊗_O k) and, on morphisms, projecting to the i = 0 summand; it satisfies L ∘ T^*ε^* = F, the modular reduction.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Definition 4.7; and the discussion of §4.4
items.note: Leslie–Lonergan Theorem 5.6.6. The lifting functor is what converts the output of the Smith operation, which lives in a Tate category, back into honest sheaves with k-coefficients.

items.name: Parity sheaves on the affine Grassmannian are tilting modules (Theorem 4.8)
items.statement: If p is good for G then the Geometric Satake equivalence restricts to an equivalence Parity^0_{L^+G}(Gr_G;k) ≅ Tilt_k(G-hat) between normalized parity sheaves for the stratification by L^+G-orbits and tilting modules for the dual group.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Theorem 4.8
items.note: Mautner–Riche Corollary 1.6, adapted from the complex affine Grassmannian to Gr_G over a separably closed field F. Goodness of p also gives that all parity sheaves exist and all normalized ones are perverse.

items.name: Tilting modules generate the derived category (Proposition 4.10)
items.statement: The natural projection K^b(Tilt_k(G-hat)) → D^b(Rep_k(G-hat)) from the bounded homotopy category of tilting modules is an equivalence.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Proposition 4.10
items.note: Riche Proposition 7.17, valid in any highest weight category. It is what lets a functor defined only on tilting modules determine the restriction functor on all representations.

items.name: The affine Grassmannian of H is the σ-fixed locus (Lemma 4.11)
items.statement: For G = H^p with σ acting by cyclic rotation, the diagonal map induces an isomorphism Gr_H ≅ Gr_G^σ of subfunctors of Gr_G.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Lemma 4.11
items.note: The geometric input that makes the Smith operation available in the base change setting; it is the local counterpart of Lemma 5.7 for shtukas.

items.name: The norm functor Nm on the Satake category (Definition 4.12)
items.statement: For F ∈ Perv_{L^+G}(Gr_G;Λ), Nm(F) := F ⋆ {}^σF ⋆ ··· ⋆ {}^{σ^{p-1}}F, made σ-equivariant by the commutativity constraint of the convolution product; it is constructed first as a σ-equivariant perverse sheaf and then pushed through the realization functor into D_{L^+G⋊σ}(Gr_G;Λ).
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Definition 4.12
items.note: The categorification of the p-fold convolution h * ··· * h appearing in the normalized Brauer homomorphism of Treumann–Venkatesh. Constructing the equivariant structure at the perverse level rather than the derived level is essential.

items.name: Stalks of Nm have filtrations by trivial and free modules (Lemma 4.14)
items.statement: Let i: Gr_H ≅ Gr_G^σ ↪ Gr_G and F ∈ Perv_{L^+G}(Gr_G;O) with O-free stalks and costalks of its cohomology sheaves. Then the stalks of the cohomology sheaves of i^*Nm(F) and the costalks of those of i^!Nm(F) each carry an O[σ]-stable filtration whose associated graded is a direct sum of trivial and free O[σ]-modules.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Lemma 4.14
items.note: The hypothesis (*) that makes Proposition 4.15 apply to Nm(F).

items.name: The Smith operation preserves parity (Proposition 4.15)
items.statement: Let F be a separably closed field of characteristic ≠ p, Y a variety over F with an admissible σ-action, Z = Y^σ, and S a σ-stable stratification of Y satisfying the JMW condition whose strata Y_λ are all smooth. Let E ∈ D^b_{S,σ}(Y;O) be a parity complex satisfying (*): for every fixed point y ∈ Z, with y ∈ Y_λ, the stalks at y of the cohomology sheaves of (i^Y_λ)^*E and of (i^Y_λ)^!E carry an O[σ]-stable filtration whose associated graded is a direct sum of O-free modules with trivial σ-action and free O[σ]-modules. Then Psm(E) = T^* i^* E ∈ Perf_S(Z;T_O) is a Tate-parity complex for the induced stratification Z_λ = Y_λ ∩ Z and the induced pariversity †_Z(λ) := †_Y(λ); if E is even (odd) then Psm(E) is Tate-even (Tate-odd).
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Proposition 4.15
items.note: A variant of Leslie–Lonergan Theorem 6.1.1. This is the technical heart of §4: it reconciles the Smith operation with a notion of t-structure-like constraint.
items.originalStatement: Assume each stratum Y_λ is smooth and let E ∈ D^b_{S,σ}(Y;O) be a parity complex satisfying (*): all * and ! stalks of its cohomology sheaves at fixed points have an O[σ]-stable filtration with associated graded a direct sum of trivial or free O[σ]-modules. Then Psm(E) ∈ Perf_S(Z;T_O) is Tate-parity for the induced stratification Z_λ = Y_λ ∩ Z and the induced pariversity.

review.reason: The item omits the standing hypotheses of §4.6.2 under which Proposition 4.15 is stated (F separably closed, admissible σ-action, Z = Y^σ, S σ-stable and JMW), omits the formula for the induced pariversity, and should say that the 'trivial' graded pieces are O-free with trivial σ-action (O-torsion pieces would have nonzero odd Tate cohomology).

items.name: Base change of coefficients for equivariant parity sheaves (Lemma 4.16)
items.statement: Let Y be a variety over a separably closed field of characteristic ≠ p with a JMW stratification S whose strata are all simply connected, and assume all parity sheaves E(λ,L) exist (with O- and hence, by Remark 4.6, k-coefficients). Then the modular reduction F = k ⊗^L_O (−) induces an equivalence Parity^0_S(Y;O) ⊗_O k ≅ Parity^0_S(Y;k), where C ⊗_O k := C ⊗_{O-Mod} (k-Mod) for an O-linear category C with O-free Hom modules [JMW14, Remark 2.7 and (2.39)]. A σ-equivariant version holds only on a restricted subcategory: on a full subcategory P ⊂ Parity^0_{S,σ}(Y;O) of perverse objects, closed under summands, whose Hom-lattices M satisfy H^1(⟨σ⟩, M) = 0 (then Hom_σ(X,Y) ⊗ k ≅ Hom_σ(FX,FY), since (M^σ) ⊗ k → (M ⊗ k)^σ has cokernel H^1(⟨σ⟩,M)), reduction is fully faithful onto its essential image; the additive closure of the image of Nm on Gr_G, whose Hom-lattices are permutation lattices, is such a subcategory.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Lemma 4.16
items.note: Needed to descend the construction from integral to k-coefficients, and to make the categorical Frobenius twist of Construction 4.17 available.
items.originalStatement: If all strata Y_λ are simply connected and all parity sheaves E(λ,L) exist, then Parity^0_{S,σ}(Y;O) ⊗_O k → Parity^0_{S,σ}(Y;k) is an equivalence.

review.reason: The item copies Lemma 4.16 as printed, for σ-equivariant categories Parity^0_{S,σ}. In that form the lemma is false (issue below: at a point with trivial σ-action the reduction functor is not full, and for p ≥ 5 not essentially surjective), and its proof uses that local systems on simply connected strata are trivial, which fails for σ-equivariant local systems on σ-stable strata. The use in §4.6.3 (definition of BC^(p)) needs only the non-equivariant case, which is true.

items.name: Frobenius twist of a k-linear category (Construction 4.17)
items.statement: For a k-linear category C, C^{(p)} := C ⊗_{k,Frob} k has the same objects and Hom_{C^{(p)}}(x,y) = Hom_C(x,y) ⊗_{k,Frob} k; the tautological Frob-semilinear equivalence Frob_C: C → C^{(p)} is universal among Frob-semilinear functors out of C. A presentation C ≅ C_0 ⊗_{F_p} k induces a further k-linear equivalence C ≅ C^{(p)}, hence a Frob-semilinear self-equivalence Frob_{F_0} of C.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Construction 4.17
items.note: The categorification of the linearisation step in the normalized Brauer homomorphism; the algebra version is Construction 5.17.

items.name: The base change functor BC on the Satake category (Definition 4.18)
items.statement: Assume H is a reductive group over a separably closed field F of characteristic ≠ p, G = H^p with σ acting by cyclic rotation of the factors (the ith factor to the (i+1)st mod p), p is odd and good for Ĝ (equivalently for Ĥ), k is an algebraic closure of F_p and O = W(k). For F ∈ Parity^0_{L^+G}(Gr_G;O), Psm(Nm(F)) lies in Parity^0_{(L^+H)}(Gr_H;T_O). The functor L ∘ Psm ∘ Nm: Parity^0_{L^+G}(Gr_G;O) → Parity^0_{L^+H}(Gr_H;k) is additive, satisfies L Psm Nm(a·f) = ā^p · L Psm Nm(f) for a ∈ O, and so factors, uniquely up to unique isomorphism, through the modular reduction F: Parity^0_{L^+G}(Gr_G;O) → Parity^0_{L^+G}(Gr_G;k) ≅ Parity^0_{L^+G}(Gr_G;O) ⊗_O k (non-equivariant Lemma 4.16) as a Frob-semilinear functor BC^(p): Parity^0_{L^+G}(Gr_G;k) → Parity^0_{L^+H}(Gr_H;k) with BC^(p) ∘ F ≅ L ∘ Psm ∘ Nm (diagram (4.7)). Let Frob_p be the Frob-semilinear self-equivalence of Parity^0_{L^+G}(Gr_G;k) induced (Construction 4.17) by the F_p-structure F_0: Parity^0_{L^+G}(Gr_G;k) ≅ Parity^0_{L^+G}(Gr_G;F_p) ⊗_{F_p} k coming from D(Gr_G;k) ≅ D(Gr_G;F_p) ⊗_{F_p} k. The base change functor is the k-linear functor BC := BC^(p) ∘ Frob_p^{-1}: Parity^0_{L^+G}(Gr_G;k) → Parity^0_{L^+H}(Gr_H;k).
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Definition 4.18
items.note: The categorification of the normalized Brauer homomorphism of Treumann–Venkatesh §4.3, and the analogue of Leslie–Lonergan's functor LL describing the Frobenius contraction functor.
items.originalStatement: BC^{(p)}: Parity^0_{L^+G}(Gr_G;k) → Parity^0_{L^+H}(Gr_H;k) is the unique functor filling in the square whose top row is Psm ∘ Nm from Parity^0_{L^+G}(Gr_G;O) to Parity^0_{(L^+H)}(Gr_H;T_O), whose left column is the modular reduction F and whose right column is the lifting functor L. Since BC^{(p)} is Frob-semilinear, one sets BC := BC^{(p)} ∘ Frob_p^{-1}, where Frob_p is the semilinear self-equivalence induced by the F_p-structure Parity^0_{L^+G}(Gr_G;k) ≅ Parity^0_{L^+G}(Gr_G;F_p) ⊗_{F_p} k.

review.reason: The item omits the standing hypotheses (§4.6.1, the sentence after Lemma 4.11, §4.6.3) and does not record that the factorisation through F requires L ∘ Psm ∘ Nm to be additive and Frob-semilinear on morphisms, which the paper asserts without proof (issue below; proposed new coverage item).

items.name: The base change functor is restriction along the diagonal (Theorem 4.20)
items.statement: Assume H is a reductive group over a separably closed field F of characteristic ≠ p, G = H^p with σ acting by cyclic rotation of the factors (the ith factor to the (i+1)st mod p), p is odd and good for Ĝ (equivalently for Ĥ), k is an algebraic closure of F_p and O = W(k). Let Res_BC: Rep_k(Ĝ) → Rep_k(Ĥ) be restriction along the diagonal embedding Ĥ → Ĥ^p = Ĝ; it maps Tilt_k(Ĝ) into Tilt_k(Ĥ), since tensor products of tilting modules are tilting. Let Sat_G: Parity^0_{L^+G}(Gr_G;k) ≅ Tilt_k(Ĝ) and Sat_H: Parity^0_{L^+H}(Gr_H;k) ≅ Tilt_k(Ĥ) be the equivalences of Theorem 4.8. Then there is a natural isomorphism Sat_H ∘ BC ≅ Res_BC ∘ Sat_G of functors Parity^0_{L^+G}(Gr_G;k) → Tilt_k(Ĥ).
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Theorem 4.20; proved in Appendix A
items.note: The main theorem of §4 and of the appendix with Gus Lonergan: the base change functor realises Langlands functoriality on the geometric side. That Res_BC preserves tilting rests on the theorem that tensor products of tilting modules are tilting.
items.originalStatement: Let Res_BC: Rep_k(G-hat) → Rep_k(H-hat) be restriction along the diagonal embedding H-hat → G-hat = H-hat^p, which preserves tilting modules. Then the square formed by BC on normalized parity sheaves, Res_BC on tilting modules and the two Geometric Satake equivalences of Theorem 4.8 commutes.

review.reason: A main theorem stated without its hypotheses: the item omits that F is separably closed of characteristic ≠ p, that G = H^p with σ the cyclic rotation, that p is odd and good for Ĝ (the route-1 brief also drops 'odd'), and that Res_BC preserves tilting modules because tensor products of tilting modules are tilting (footnote 11). The proof in Appendix A has a gap in the reduction to a torus (issue below).

items.name: Exactness of the composite Psm ∘ Nm ∘ Sat (Lemma 4.21)
items.statement: Assume H is a reductive group over a separably closed field F of characteristic ≠ p, G = H^p with σ acting by cyclic rotation of the factors (the ith factor to the (i+1)st mod p), p is odd and good for Ĝ (equivalently for Ĥ), k is an algebraic closure of F_p and O = W(k), and let i: Gr_H ≅ Gr_G^σ ↪ Gr_G. The composite Φ: Rep_k(Ĝ) →(Frob_p^{-1}) Rep_k(Ĝ) →(Sat) Perv_{L^+G}(Gr_G;k) →(Nm) Perv_{L^+G⋊σ}(Gr_G;k) →(Psm) Perf_{(L^+H)}(Gr_H;T_k) is exact in the following sense: for every short exact sequence 0 → A → B → C → 0 in Rep_k(Ĝ), writing A' = Nm Sat Frob_p^{-1}(A) and similarly B', C', the induced map Cone(i^*A' → i^*B') → i^*C' in D^b_{c,L^+H}(Gr_H;k[σ]) projects to an isomorphism in Perf_{(L^+H)}(Gr_H;T_k). (A sequence 𝒜 → ℬ → 𝒞 in the Tate category is called exact when the map from the cone of 𝒜 → ℬ, formed in D_{L^+H}(Gr_H;k[σ]), to 𝒞 becomes an isomorphism in Perf_{(L^+H)}(Gr_H;T_k).)
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Lemma 4.21; proved in Appendix A §A.6
items.note: Exactness is what allows the functor, defined on tilting modules, to be extended to all of Rep_k(G-hat) through Proposition 4.10.
items.originalStatement: The composite Rep_k(G-hat) →(Frob_p^{-1}) Rep_k(G-hat) →(Sat) Perv_{L^+G}(Gr_G;k) →(Nm) Perv_{L^+G⋊σ}(Gr_G;k) →(Psm) Perf_{(L^+H)}(Gr_H;T_k) is exact, i.e. sends exact sequences to exact sequences in the appropriate sense.

review.reason: 'Exact in the appropriate sense' is not a statement: the lemma uses the specific notion defined just before it on p. 28 (cones computed in the equivariant derived category with k[σ]-coefficients), and the hypotheses of Theorem 4.20 are omitted.

items.name: Galois equivariance of the base change functor (Lemma 4.22 and Corollary 4.23)
items.statement: Let F be a separably closed field of characteristic ≠ p containing a subfield F_0, H_0 a reductive group over F_0 with H = H_{0,F}, E_0/F_0 a Galois extension with group Z/pZ and G_0 = Res_{E_0/F_0}(H_{0,E_0}), so that G = G_{0,F} ≅ H^p with a generator σ of Gal(E_0/F_0) rotating the factors; assume p odd and good for Ĝ, and let Aut(F/F_0) act on H, G, Gr_H, Gr_G. (a) (Lemma 4.22) BC: Parity^0_{L^+G}(Gr_{G,F};k) → Parity^0_{L^+H}(Gr_{H,F};k) is Aut(F/F_0)-equivariant. (b) (Corollary 4.23) Put Parity^0_{L^+G}(Gr_{G,F_0};k) := Parity^0_{L^+G}(Gr_{G,F};k)^{BAut(F/F_0)} (equivariantization [DGNO10]) and similarly for H, and let Tilt_k(^LG^geom) be the full subcategory of Rep_k(^LG^geom) of representations whose restriction to Ĝ is tilting, so that Tilt_k(^LG^geom) ≅ Tilt_k(Ĝ)^{Aut(F/F_0),geom}, similarly for ^LH. Then the square formed by BC^{BAut(F/F_0)}: Parity^0_{L^+G}(Gr_{G,F_0};k) → Parity^0_{L^+H}(Gr_{H,F_0};k), Res_BC: Tilt_k(^LG^geom) → Tilt_k(^LH^geom) and the two equivariantized Satake equivalences commutes.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Lemma 4.22; and Corollary 4.23
items.note: This is what makes the construction descend from the separably closed field to the ground field and hence apply to the geometric L-group, which is the form in which it enters Lafforgue's machine.
items.originalStatement: BC: Parity^0_{L^+G}(Gr_{G,F};k) → Parity^0_{L^+H}(Gr_{H,F};k) is equivariant for the action of Aut(F/F_0); consequently, after equivariantization, the square formed by BC^{BAut(F/F_0)} on parity sheaves over F_0, Res_BC on Tilt_k(^LG^geom) and Tilt_k(^LH^geom), and the two Satake equivalences, commutes.

review.reason: The item omits the setting of §4.6.4 in which both statements are made (H defined over a subfield F_0 ⊂ F, G = Res_{E_0/F_0}(H_{E_0}) for a Z/pZ-Galois extension E_0/F_0) and the definitions of Parity^0(Gr_{G,F_0};k) by equivariantization and of Tilt_k(^LG^geom).

items.name: The integral compatibility cube (Lemma 4.24)
items.statement: Assume H is a reductive group over a separably closed field F of characteristic ≠ p, G = H^p with σ acting by cyclic rotation of the factors (the ith factor to the (i+1)st mod p), p is odd and good for Ĝ (equivalently for Ĥ), k is an algebraic closure of F_p and O = W(k). Let P ⊂ Parity^0_{L^+G⋊σ}(Gr_G;O) be the additive closure of the image of Nm, and P_k its reduction, so that F: P ⊗_O k ≅ P_k and Psm maps P into Parity^0_{(L^+H)}(Gr_H;T_O); let Φ: P_k → Parity^0_{L^+H}(Gr_H;k) be the functor with Φ ∘ F ≅ L ∘ Psm (so that Φ ∘ Nm = BC^(p)). In the cube (4.8) with these categories: the left face (F commutes with the inclusions), the front face (Psm restricted to parity objects), the bottom face (F ∘ Psm ≅ Psm ∘ F from D^b_{c,L^+G⋊σ}(Gr_G;O) to Perf_{(L^+H)}(Gr_H;T_k)) and the top face (by definition of Φ) commute as functors. The right face T^*ε^* ∘ L ≅ F ∘ incl holds on objects of Parity^0_{(L^+H)}(Gr_H;T_O) and on morphisms in the image of T^*ε^*: Parity^0_{L^+H}(Gr_H;O) → Parity^0_{(L^+H)}(Gr_H;T_O), but not on all morphisms. Consequently the back face holds on objects: T^*ε^*(Φ(E)) ≅ Psm(E) in Perf_{(L^+H)}(Gr_H;T_k) for every E in P_k. It holds as a natural isomorphism of functors on P_k provided Psm(f̃) has zero components of index i ≠ 0 in the decomposition (4.2) for every morphism f̃ of P, which the paper does not prove.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Lemma 4.24
items.note: It says that the a priori mysterious top arrow has, after projecting to the Tate category, the simple description Psm; this is used when Tate cohomology is taken with coefficients in these parity sheaves.
items.originalStatement: The cube whose two horizontal faces are Psm from equivariant parity sheaves with O- and with k-coefficients, whose vertical arrows are the inclusions of parity categories into the constructible derived and Tate categories, whose diagonals are the modular reduction F and the lifting functor L, commutes; the unlabeled arrow on the top face is the one making that face commute.

review.reason: Two problems. (1) The description of the cube is inaccurate: the right-hand vertical arrow of the back face is T^*ε^*: Parity^0_{L^+H}(Gr_H;k) → Perf_{(L^+H)}(Gr_H;T_k), not an inclusion, and the bottom face is F ∘ Psm ≅ Psm ∘ F between the equivariant derived and Tate categories. (2) As printed, Lemma 4.24 is false and its proof has two faulty steps (issues below): the right face T^*ε^* ∘ L ≅ F ∘ incl does not commute as functors, because L discards the summands of index i ≠ 0 in (4.2) that F retains; and the unlabeled arrow's existence uses the σ-equivariant Lemma 4.16, which is false on all of Parity^0_{L^+G⋊σ}(Gr_G;O). The item should carry what is provable, and flag that the back face as a natural isomorphism (used in the proof of Proposition 5.12) is not established by the paper's argument.

items.name: Moduli stacks of shtukas with legs
items.statement: Fix a smooth projective curve X over a finite field F_ℓ whose characteristic is not p, and a smooth algebraic group scheme G over X which is generically reductive; let X° ⊂ X be the open locus over which G is reductive. For a finite set I, Sht_{G,I} sends an F_ℓ-scheme S to the groupoid of triples ((x_i)_{i∈I} ∈ X^I(S), an étale G-torsor E over X×S, an isomorphism φ: E|_{X×S−∪_{i∈I}Γ_{x_i}} ≅ ^τE|_{X×S−∪_{i∈I}Γ_{x_i}}), where τ is Frob_ℓ on the factor S and ^τE = (1×τ)^*E. Geometrically Sht_{G,I} has a Schubert stratification whose strata are Deligne–Mumford stacks locally of finite type, and it is regarded as an ind-(locally finite type) Deligne–Mumford stack. The map π_I: Sht_{G,I} → X^I records the legs, and Sht°_{G,I} := Sht_{G,I} ×_{X^I} (X°)^I.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, §5.1.1
items.note: GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands:GS.2 plans multi-leg global shtukas as successive modifications with an isomorphism to the Frobenius pullback, with bounds, level, partial Frobenius and Harder–Narasimhan truncations, and the representability statements. Review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24), status check: Planned status confirmed: GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands:GS.2 plans multi-leg shtukas (successive modifications with an isomorphism to the Frobenius pullback, direction specified) with the representability/Deligne–Mumford statements, and GS.0 works with the chosen smooth model. This part of the construction is independent of the coefficients.
items.originalStatement: For X a smooth projective curve over F_ℓ with ℓ ≠ p and G a smooth generically reductive group scheme over X, Sht_{G,I} sends an F_ℓ-scheme S to the groupoid of tuples ((x_i)_{i∈I} ∈ X^I(S), an étale G-torsor E on X×S, and an isomorphism φ of E with its Frobenius twist away from the graphs of the legs). It is an ind-(locally finite type) Deligne–Mumford stack with a Schubert stratification, and π_I: Sht_{G,I} → X^I records the legs.

review.reason: Two hypotheses are imprecise. (1) The paper fixes X over 'a finite field F_ℓ of characteristic ≠ p'; the item's 'ℓ ≠ p' is weaker if ℓ denotes the order of the field (ℓ = p² would satisfy it). (2) The item omits the reductive locus X° ⊂ X and Sht°_{G,I} := Sht_{G,I} ×_{X^I} (X°)^I, which the paper introduces here and on which Sat (item 53) is defined.

items.name: The Hecke stack and the Satake functor on shtukas
items.statement: Hk_{G,I} sends S to ((x_i)_{i∈I} ∈ X^I(S), étale G-torsors E, E' over X×S, an isomorphism φ: E|_{X×S−∪Γ_{x_i}} ≅ E'|_{X×S−∪Γ_{x_i}}); let Hk°_{G,I} := Hk_{G,I} ×_{X^I} (X°)^I. Geometric Satake gives a functor Rep_k((^LG)^I) → D(Hk°_{G,I};k), normalised as in [Laf18, Théorème 0.9]. Pulling back along Sht_{G,I} → Hk_{G,I}, ((x_i),E,φ) ↦ ((x_i),E,^τE,φ), gives Sat^geom: Rep_k(Ĝ^I)^{B Gal(F^s/F),geom} → D^b(Sht°_{G,I};k), and composing with the identification Rep_k((^LG^alg)^I) ≅ Rep_k(Ĝ^I)^{B Gal(F^s/F),geom} of §2.1.4 gives Sat: Rep_k((^LG^alg)^I) → D^b(Sht°_{G,I};k) (cf. [Laf18, Théorème 0.11]). The Schubert stratification of Sht°_{G,I} is defined by the supports of the sheaves in the image of Sat, with closure relations given by the Bruhat order; Sat lands in complexes constructible for it.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, §5.1.2; and §5.1.3
items.note: GS.1 plans global Hecke stacks and classical geometric Satake, and GS.2 the local-model maps to bounded Grassmannians defining the Schubert stratification. Review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24): status planned → missing: GS.1 plans the global Hecke stack and geometric Satake with rational ℓ-adic intersection complexes and says that 'integral and modular Satake are further coefficient branches'; GS.2 plans the map Sht → Hk. The functor Sat with coefficients in k = F̄_p is the modular branch GS.1 leaves out. The Hecke stack and the map from shtukas stay planned by GS.1 and GS.2, and route 2 imports them; the k-coefficient Satake functor on Hk°_{G,I} and Sht°_{G,I} is missing, and route 2 builds it from the local modular Satake category that route 1 takes from GeometricSatakeAndFusion. Creation and annihilation in the excursion instance are geometric Rep_k(Ĝ^I) morphisms evaluated before Galois descent; the Γ-action is supplied separately as in corrected item 56. Full-L-group invariance of x or ξ is not assumed (E59–E60).
items.originalStatement: Hk_{G,I} classifies two torsors with an isomorphism away from the legs; Geometric Satake gives Rep_k((^LG)^I) → D(Hk_{G,I};k), and pulling back along Sht_{G,I} → Hk_{G,I} gives Sat: Rep_k((^LG^alg)^I) → D^b(Sht_{G,I};k), normalized as in Lafforgue. The Schubert stratification is the support stratification of the image of Sat.

review.reason: The Satake functors live over the reductive locus: Geometric Satake gives Rep_k((^LG)^I) → D(Hk°_{G,I};k) with Hk°_{G,I} := Hk_{G,I} ×_{X^I} (X°)^I, and Sat takes values in D^b(Sht°_{G,I};k), not D^b(Sht_{G,I};k). The item also skips the intermediate functor Sat^geom and the identification of §2.1.4 through which Rep_k((^LG^alg)^I) is reached.
