items.name: Level structures, iterated shtukas and the partial Frobenius
items.statement: For D ⊂ X a closed finite subscheme, Sht_{G,D,I} → Sht_{G,I}|_{(X\D)^I} adds a trivialisation of E over D×S compatible with τ and φ. For a partition I = I_1 ⊔ ··· ⊔ I_r, the iterated stack Sht^{(I_1,...,I_r)}_{G,D,I} classifies a chain of torsors with modifications at the legs of each block and an isomorphism E_r ≅ {}^τE_0; the map ν to Sht_{G,D,I} is stratified small. The partial Frobenius F_{I_1} rotates the chain and applies τ to the legs indexed by I_1, lying over Frob_{I_1} on X^I.
items.note: GS.2 plans level, partial Frobenius and truncations; GS.4 plans the partial Frobenius action and Drinfeld's lemma with the verification that partial Frobenii commute with Hecke operators. Review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24), status check: Planned status confirmed: GS.2 plans level, partial Frobenius and HN truncations for multi-leg (iterated) shtukas, and GS.4 plans the partial Frobenius action. The sheaf-level partial Frobenius isomorphisms F^*_{I_1}Sat^{(I_1,…,I_r)}(V) ≅ Sat^{(I_2,…,I_r,I_1)}(V) and Rν_!Sat^{(I_1,…,I_r)}(V) ≅ Sat(V) of §5.2.3 depend on the coefficients. With k-coefficients they belong to the new §5.2.2–5.2.3 item proposed under coverage.

items.name: The base change setup for shtukas
items.statement: Let F be the function field of X, H_F reductive over F with a chosen parahoric extension H over X; let E/F be cyclic of degree p, corresponding to a smooth projective curve X', and set G := Res_{X'/X}(H_{X'}), a group scheme over X with generic fibre Res_{E/F}(H_E) and an action of ⟨σ⟩ = Aut(X'/X).
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, §5.1.7
items.note: The global setting of the paper; the σ-action on the whole shtuka tower is what Smith theory is applied to. Review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24), status check: Missing status confirmed: no stage plans the cyclic Weil restriction G = Res_{X'/X}(H_{X'}) with its σ-action. It is correctly routed to route 2. The map φ_*: ker¹(F,H) → ker¹(F,G) of §5.6 (p. 42), which Theorem 5.13 uses, belongs with this setup (see the coverage row for (5.6)/(5.19)).

items.name: Coefficient-linear geometric families with Galois transport and excursion actions
items.statement: Use the coefficient, geometric-domain, transport, fusion, unit and inflation contracts in functorContract. For W∈Rep_k((^LG)^I), let V=W|_{Ĝ^I}, ζ:I→{0}, x∈V^{ΔĜ}, ξ∈(V*)^{ΔĜ}, and γ=(γ_i)∈Γ^I. On M≅F_{ {0} }(1), define S_{I,W,x,ξ,γ}=F_{ {0} }(ξ) χ_ζ^{-1} D^W_γ χ_ζ F_{ {0} }(x), where D^W_γ=F_I(r_γ)a_{γ,V}. Every outer arrow is now in the geometric functor domain. The six relations of item 13 follow from k-linearity, natural coherent fusion, the transport group law and duality diagrams, unit normalization and the stated forgotten-leg/inflation compatibility, as proved finding by finding in the fixes report. Thus these operators define a k-algebra map Exc(Γ,^LG)→End_A(M). Fusion and composition alone, for arbitrary ordinary functors, do not suffice (E59); applying a functor on Rep_k(^LG) directly to x or ξ is generally ill typed (E60).
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Definition 5.1; and Construction 5.2
items.note: Route 2 retains ownership of the modular abstract mechanism. This corrected abstraction surrounds the geometric Satake/cohomology operations, rather than applying the printed full-L-group functor to geometric-only arrows. Item rev-20 supplies the ordinary cohomology instance; item 58 the partial-Weil-to-Weil descent needed for the Tate instance. The six proof arguments and negative/positive specifications are in RT-PAPER-FENG-24.fixes.md. The earlier E35 index repair is retained, but does not repair E59 or E60.
items.originalStatement: A family H_I: Rep_k((^LG)^I) → Mod_A(Γ^I) over finite sets I is admissible if it is compatible with fusion, i.e. carries natural isomorphisms χ_ζ between H_I ∘ Res_ζ and Res_ζ ∘ H_J for every ζ: I → J, and with composition, χ_{ζζ'} = χ_ζ ∘ χ_{ζ'}. Given such a family, the composite H_{{0}}(1) → H_{{0}}(W^ζ) → H_I(W) →((γ_i)) H_I(W) → H_{{0}}(W^ζ) → H_{{0}}(1) defines the image of the generator S_{I,W,x,ξ,(γ_i)}, giving an A-linear action of Exc(Γ,^LG) on H_{{0}}(1).

review.reason: Compatibility with fusion is printed with I and J swapped, and the item copies the slip: for ζ: I → J the restriction Res_ζ goes from Rep_k((^LG)^I) to Rep_k((^LG)^J) (diagram (5.2); in Construction 5.2, W^ζ = Res_ζ W and χ_ζ: H_{{0}}(W^ζ) ≅ H_I(W)), so H_I ∘ Res_ζ is not composable. The isomorphism is χ_ζ: H_J ∘ Res_ζ ≅ Res_ζ ∘ H_I. The item also omits A (a not necessarily commutative ring), the allowed empty I, the requirement that ζ: I → {0} in Construction 5.2, and Remark 5.3.

beforeRedteamFix.name: Admissible families of functors and the excursion action they carry
beforeRedteamFix.statement: Let A be a (not necessarily commutative) ring. A family of functors H_I: Rep_k((^LG)^I) → Mod_A(Γ^I), I running over (possibly empty) finite sets, is admissible if (1) (fusion) for every map ζ: I → J there is a natural isomorphism χ_ζ: H_J ∘ Res_ζ ≅ Res_ζ ∘ H_I of functors Rep_k((^LG)^I) → Mod_A(Γ^J), where Res_ζ restricts along (^LG)^J → (^LG)^I and along Γ^J → Γ^I, (g_j)_j ↦ (g_{ζ(i)})_i; and (2) (composition) χ_{ζ∘ζ'} = χ_ζ ∘ χ_{ζ'} for I' →ζ' I →ζ J. Given an admissible family, for a tuple (I, W, x, ξ, (γ_i)_{i∈I}) with W ∈ Rep_k((^LG)^I), x ∈ W^{Δ(Ĝ)}, ξ ∈ (W^*)^{Δ(Ĝ)}, γ_i ∈ Γ, and ζ: I → {0}, the composite H_{{0}}(1) →[H_{{0}}(x)] H_{{0}}(W^ζ) →[χ_ζ] H_I(W) →[(γ_i)] H_I(W) →[χ_ζ^{-1}] H_{{0}}(W^ζ) →[H_{{0}}(ξ)] H_{{0}}(1) is the image of S_{I,W,x,ξ,(γ_i)}. These endomorphisms satisfy the relations of §2.4.2 and so define an A-linear action of Exc(Γ,^LG) on H_{{0}}(1). By admissibility (χ for ∅ → I) the A-module underlying H_I(1) is identified with H_∅(1) for every I (Remark 5.3).
beforeRedteamFix.note: Feng's axiomatisation of Lafforgue's mechanism: this is the device by which an excursion action is constructed on any object built functorially out of the Satake category, and it is what he applies to Tate cohomology rather than cohomology. Review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24), status check: Missing status confirmed. The same creation / Weil-tuple / annihilation mechanism is planned in specific settings by GS.5 (shtuka cohomology, characteristic-zero) and ExcursionOperatorsAndSpectralAction:ES0 (Fargues–Scholze categories). Neither plans the abstract admissible-family formalism, so route 2 is the right owner.

functorContract.coefficients: A is a unital, possibly noncommutative k-algebra with k acting centrally. Mod_A and all Hom spaces use this k-action. For every finite I, including ∅, F_I: Rep_k(Ĝ^I) → Mod_A is a k-linear additive functor. Thus F_I(0)=0 on morphisms and finite biproducts are preserved; no exactness or strong monoidality of F_I is assumed.
functorContract.geometricDomain: Creation and annihilation are geometric morphisms x:1→V^ζ and ξ:V^ζ→1, for ζ:I→{0}. Here V is W restricted to Ĝ^I, and W may be any allowed representation of (^LG)^I. The geometric/algebraic L-group identification uses the compatible normalization of item 8. Neither x nor ξ is required to be Γ-invariant.
functorContract.transport: Let T_γV be V with action g↦ρ_V(γ^{-1}gγ), for γ∈Γ^I. Equip F with A-linear natural isomorphisms a_{γ,V}:F_I(V)→F_I(T_γV). Require a_{1,V}=id and a_{γδ,V}=a_{γ,T_δV} a_{δ,V}, under T_γT_δ=T_{γδ}. The full L-group representation gives r_γ:T_γV→V, v↦W(γ)v, with r_{γδ}=r_γ T_γ(r_δ). Its action on F_I(V) is D^W_γ=F_I(r_γ)a_{γ,V}. Naturality proves D^W_γ D^W_δ=D^W_{γδ}.
functorContract.fusion: For every ζ:I→J, χ_ζ:F_J(V^ζ)≅F_I(V), natural in all geometric representation morphisms. Require identity and composition coherence. The χ_ζ square intertwines a_{δ,V^ζ} with a_{δ^ζ,V}, where δ^ζ=(δ_{ζ(i)})_i, and hence intertwines the D-actions for descended W. Use this same naturality for external products, their canonical permutations, evaluation and coevaluation after coalescing paired legs. These are compatibility diagrams for the actual geometric morphisms, not a tensor product identification F(V⊗V′)=F(V)⊗F(V′).
functorContract.unit: Writing M=F_∅(k), χ_{∅→I} identifies F_I(1) with M. Transport-compatible fusion for ∅→I forces identity transport on unit objects, since the source has no Γ-coordinates. At I=∅, k-linearity gives the canonical F_∅(U)≅M⊗_k U for finite-dimensional U, so ξx acts by ⟨ξ,x⟩ id_M. This records the empty-set and scalar normalizations as consequences of the coherent geometric contract.
functorContract.inflation: If V is inflated from Ĝ^J for J⊂I, χ for J↪I identifies F_I(V) with F_J(V|_{Ĝ^J}). For δ∈Γ^{I minus J}, its pullback to Γ^J is the identity tuple. The transport-compatible χ square therefore gives a_{(1_J,δ),V}=id under this identification. For full-L-group W inflated from (^LG)^J×Γ^{I minus J}, the remaining action D^W_{(1_J,δ)} is F_J(W(1_J,δ)), moving x to W(1_J,δ)x as the inflation relation requires. This is a consequence of geometric transport-compatible fusion, not of the two printed ordinary-functor axioms. The geometric cohomology instance must verify that compatibility.

unitTests.name: Feng.item56.constantFunctorExcluded
unitTests.statement: The ordinary functor taking every representation to k and every map to id satisfies the two printed fusion conditions. For W=1 and x=0 its composite is id, contrary to excursion linearity. It is excluded by F_I(0)=0 in the coefficient-linear contract.

unitTests.name: Feng.item56.linearCreation
unitTests.statement: For fixed W, ξ and γ, S_{x+x′}=S_x+S_{x′}, S_{λx}=λ S_x and S_0=0; the same identities hold in ξ. Check biproduct additivity, external-product composition and the empty-set scalar ⟨ξ,x⟩ separately.

unitTests.name: Feng.item56.fullLGroupInflation
unitTests.statement: For W=k(χ) with Ĝ acting trivially and χ a quadratic Γ-character in characteristic 3, creation x=1 and annihilation ξ=1 are geometric morphisms. Inflation to J=∅ gives S_{W,1,1,γ}=χ(γ) id_M. This validates a generator forbidden by the old ill-typed construction.

unitTests.name: Feng.item56.tripleTuple
unitTests.statement: With coevaluation δ_W and evaluation ev_W, the operator on W⊠W*⊠W at (γ,γ′,γ″), creation δ_W⊠x and annihilation ξ⊠ev_W, equals S_{W,x,ξ,γ(γ′)^{-1}γ″}. Check the two paired-leg transport squares and the duality triangle, not just fusion on objects.

items.name: Automorphic L-parameters after Lafforgue and Xue
items.statement: An L-parameter ρ ∈ H^1(Gal(F^s/F), G-hat(k)) arises from C_c^∞(Bun_{G,D}(F_ℓ);k) if it arises through Proposition 2.4 from the Exc(Γ,^LG)-action on some irreducible Hecke subquotient, equivalently if the corresponding maximal ideal lies in the support of that space as an Exc(Γ,^LG)-module; ρ is automorphic if this holds for some D.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Definition 5.5 (p. 35); with the discussion of §5.2.4 (p. 35). There is no §5.2.5: §5.2 ends with §5.2.4, 'Xue's generalization', which contains Definition 5.5 and to which Theorem 5.13 refers ('in the sense of §5.2.4').
items.note: Lafforgue defined the action on the finite-dimensional cuspidal subspace; Xue extended it to all compactly supported functions, where no finite-dimensional subspace is stable, so the notion of arising has to be phrased through supports. Review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24), status check: Missing status confirmed (GS.5 plans only the characteristic-zero decomposition of the cuspidal space). The item's wording drops the alternative characterisation in the second sentence: m_ρ lies in the support of C_c^∞(G_α(F)\G_α(A_F);k) for some α. That is harmless, since the item keeps 'for some D'. The second sentence is misprinted ('We say will be called automorphic'); see E6.
items.originalLocator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Definition 5.5; with the discussion of §5.2.5

items.name: The partial Weil group acts through its quotient on Tate cohomology (Proposition 5.6)
items.statement: For any G, D, I and V, the FWeil(η^I, η^I-bar)-action on T^j(Sht_{G,D,I};V) factors through the surjection FWeil(η^I,η^I-bar) ↠ Weil(η,η-bar)^I.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Proposition 5.6; proved in Appendix B
items.note: This is Drinfeld's lemma for Tate cohomology, and it is what makes the excursion formalism applicable to T^*(Sht_{G,D,I};V). GS.4 plans Drinfeld's lemma for the Hecke-finite sector of ordinary cohomology, not for Tate cohomology. Review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24), status check: Missing status confirmed: GS.4 plans Drinfeld's lemma and its use for ordinary cohomology on the Hecke-finite sector (ℓ-adic coefficients), not for Tate cohomology with k-coefficients. Locator: Proposition 5.6 is on p. 36, and its proof is in Appendix B, pp. 61–64. The concluding step and Lemma B.5 are on p. 64, beyond the pp. 61–63 given for Appendix B.

items.name: Tate cohomology of moduli of shtukas
items.statement: For V ∈ Rep_k((^LG^alg)^I)^σ-equivariant, the σ-equivariance of Sat and of π_I makes RΓ_c(Sht_{G,D,I}|_{η^I-bar};Sat(V)) a σ-equivariant complex, and one sets T^j(Sht_{G,D,I};V) := T^j(RΓ_c(Sht_{G,D,I}|_{η^I-bar};Sat(V))), a module over T^0(H_G)[Weil(η,η-bar)^I] by Proposition 5.6. When σ acts trivially, Lemma 3.14 gives T^*(Sht_{H,D,I};F) ≅ H_c^*(Sht_{H,D,I}|_{η^I-bar};F) ⊗ T^*(k).
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, §5.3.1
items.note: Passing from cohomology to Tate cohomology is Feng's solution to the problem that the natural map between Sht_H and Sht_G is not Hecke-equivariant. Review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24), status check: Missing status confirmed: no stage plans Tate cohomology of shtukas. Identity (5.8) is correctly attributed to Lemma 3.14. (Item 30's note calls it equation (5.6); it is (5.8).)

items.name: Étale-cover fixed-locus identification for shtukas (qualified Lemma 5.7)
items.statement: Assume additionally that π:X′→X is finite étale (hence a C_p-torsor). In the base change setup (§5.1.7), let x_0 ∈ X be a closed point, D ⊂ X a closed finite subscheme, (I_1,…,I_r) a partition of the finite set I, μ a coweight of H and μ̃ the induced coweight of G. If n is large enough that Sht^{(I_1,…,I_r),≤μ}_{H,D+nx_0,I} and Sht^{(I_1,…,I_r),≤μ̃}_{G,D+nx_0,I} are representable by schemes, then the map induced by the diagonal H → G is an isomorphism Sht^{(I_1,…,I_r),≤μ}_{H,D+nx_0,I} ≅ (Sht^{(I_1,…,I_r),≤μ̃}_{G,D+nx_0,I})^σ onto the σ-fixed locus.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Lemma 5.7
items.note: The whole-fixed-locus assertion is qualified to finite étale covers. Automorphism-freeness gives the unique cocycle; π being a C_p-torsor identifies that cocycle with an effective fppf descent datum. Descend the torsors, level, modifications and Frobenius, then use the separately routed HN comparison rev-25. This is natural for every test scheme and the iterated partitions, hence gives the scheme isomorphism. For ramified π, the same uniqueness only gives a linearization and need not give effective descent: E58 supplies a framed G_m counterexample at every depth. No claim of a ramified trivial-inertia criterion or of sufficient branch level is made by this qualified lemma.
items.originalStatement: If n is large enough that Sht^{(I_1,...,I_r),≤μ}_{H,D+nx_0,I} and Sht^{(I_1,...,I_r),≤μ-tilde}_{G,D+nx_0,I} are representable by schemes, then the diagonal map H → G induces an isomorphism from the former onto the σ-fixed locus of the latter.

review.reason: The item does not introduce μ, μ̃, x_0 or D. μ is a coweight of H and μ̃ the induced coweight of G, fixed just before (5.11). The statement concerns the iterated stacks for a partition (I_1,…,I_r) of I, although the proof treats only the non-iterated case ('the general case is essentially the same').

beforeRedteamFix.name: The shtuka stack for H is the σ-fixed locus (Lemma 5.7)
beforeRedteamFix.statement: In the base change setup (§5.1.7), let x_0 ∈ X be a closed point, D ⊂ X a closed finite subscheme, (I_1,…,I_r) a partition of the finite set I, μ a coweight of H and μ̃ the induced coweight of G. If n is large enough that Sht^{(I_1,…,I_r),≤μ}_{H,D+nx_0,I} and Sht^{(I_1,…,I_r),≤μ̃}_{G,D+nx_0,I} are representable by schemes, then the map induced by the diagonal H → G is an isomorphism Sht^{(I_1,…,I_r),≤μ}_{H,D+nx_0,I} ≅ (Sht^{(I_1,…,I_r),≤μ̃}_{G,D+nx_0,I})^σ onto the σ-fixed locus.
beforeRedteamFix.note: The global analogue of Lemma 4.11 and the geometric input to equivariant localisation; the passage to representable truncations is what avoids Smith theory for stacks. Review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24), status check: Missing status confirmed. The proof uses the Cartesian squares (5.11): Bun_H^{≤μ} = Bun_H ×_{Bun_G} Bun_G^{≤μ̃} and its shtuka analogue. The paper asserts them without proof and no item covers them (see coverage).

proofOutline: For a fixed S-point, representability removes its automorphisms, so the fixed-point isomorphism is unique and its p-fold composite is identity.

For finite étale π, X′_S×_{X_S}X′_S≅C_p×X′_S. The unique cocycle is therefore an actual fppf descent datum on the full relation, not merely on separate graphs. Effective descent of affine H-torsors and full faithfulness descend the morphisms, Frobenius and level.

Apply this to every torsor and modification in an iterated shtuka. Pullback and descent are inverse and commute with S-base change. Use rev-25 for the truncation pullback square (5.11), rather than assuming its separate HN claim is formal.

unitTests.name: Feng.item60.ramifiedFrame
unitTests.statement: Over F_7 let t=u³, σ(u)=2u, H=G_m, no legs and frame u modulo (u³−1)^n at x_0=(t=1). Multiplication by 4 identifies the changed frame, and 4³=1. Framed automorphisms vanish, but inertia at u=0 acts by 4. No pulled-back degree-zero framed line bundle produces this point, for any n≥1. Therefore deep level at x_0 does not repair a ramified whole-fixed-locus theorem.

unitTests.name: Feng.item60.etaleRelation
unitTests.statement: For a finite étale C_p-torsor π, test the isomorphism C_p×X′_S→X′_S×_{X_S}X′_S and descent over each S. For the ramified t=u³ cover, the graphs meet at u=0, so the same decomposition is false there. A set-level generic-fibre check is insufficient.

items.name: Cohomology and Tate cohomology at infinite level (Definitions 5.8 and 5.10)
items.statement: Fix a closed point x_0 ∈ X. For V ∈ Rep_k((^LH^alg)^I), RΓ_c(Sht_{H,D+∞x_0,I}|_{η̄^I};Sat(V)) := colim_{n,μ} RΓ_c(Sht^{≤μ}_{H,D+nx_0,I}|_{η̄^I};Sat(V)). The transition maps in μ are the covariant maps induced by the open embeddings, and those in n are the contravariant maps induced by pullback along the change-of-level maps. The colimit is filtered, and the indices (n,μ) for which Sht^{≤μ}_{H,D+nx_0,I} is a scheme are cofinal, so the colimit may be taken over them (Remark 5.9). The colimit is a bounded complex, since the dimension of the support of Sat(V) on Sht^{≤μ}_{H,D+nx_0,I}|_{η̄^I} is bounded uniformly in n and μ. For V ∈ Rep_k((^LH^alg)^I)^{Bσ}, T^j(Sht_{H,D+∞x_0,I};V) := T^j(RΓ_c(Sht_{H,D+∞x_0,I}|_{η̄^I};Sat(V))). The same definitions are made for G, with the colimit over n and the induced HN polygons μ̃, which form a cofinal system for G; this gives RΓ_c(Sht_{G,D+∞x_0,I}|_{η̄^I};Sat(V)) and, for V ∈ Rep_k((^LG^alg)^I)^{Bσ}, T^j(Sht_{G,D+∞x_0,I};V).
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Definition 5.8; and Definition 5.10, with Remark 5.9
items.note: Necessary because the excursion action does not stabilise the pieces of cohomology cut out by bounding the Harder–Narasimhan polygon, so both n and μ must go to infinity.
items.originalStatement: Fix a closed point x_0 ∈ X. RΓ_c(Sht_{H,D+∞x_0,I}|_{η^I-bar};Sat(V)) := colim_{n,μ} RΓ_c(Sht^{≤μ}_{H,D+nx_0,I}|_{η^I-bar};Sat(V)), the colimit being over the covariant maps in μ and the contravariant pullback maps in n, a filtered colimit; and T^j(Sht_{H,D+∞x_0,I};V) is its Tate cohomology. The indices for which the truncation is a scheme are cofinal.

review.reason: The item defines the infinite-level objects only for H, and does not say which V are allowed. Theorem 5.11 and Proposition 5.12 use the G-versions, which the paper defines 'analogously' along the induced polygons μ̃, noting that these are cofinal for G. The item also omits the boundedness of the colimit, which the paper notes and which makes Tate cohomology commute with the filtered colimit.

items.name: Equivariant localisation identifies excursion operators (Theorem 5.11)
items.statement: Assume additionally that π:X′→X is finite étale (hence a C_p-torsor). Standing hypotheses (not repeated in the printed statement): the base change setup of §5.1.7 (X smooth projective over a finite field F_ℓ of characteristic ≠ p, H a parahoric model over X of a reductive H_F, E/F cyclic of degree p with curve X', G = Res_{X'/X}(H_{X'}) with its action of ⟨σ⟩ = Aut(X'/X)), and p odd and good for Ĝ, which the paper assumes from p. 24 on ('Henceforth, we assume that p is odd and good for Ĝ', after Lemma 4.11) and which the proof uses through Theorem 4.20 and Proposition 4.10. Fix a closed point x_0 ∈ X and a closed finite subscheme D ⊂ X. Let I be a finite set, V ∈ Rep_k((^LG)^I), x ∈ V^{Δ(Ĝ)}, ξ ∈ (V^*)^{Δ(Ĝ)} and (γ_i)_{i∈I} ∈ Γ^I. (i) For each j ∈ {0,1}, consider the isomorphism T^j(Sht_{G,D+∞x_0,∅};1) ≅ T^j(Sht_{H,D+∞x_0,∅};1) = H^0_c(Sht_{H,D+∞x_0,∅};1) induced by Lemma 5.7 (through equivariant localisation (3.6) and (5.8)). Under it, the action of S_{I,Nm^{(p^{-1})}(V),Nm^{(p^{-1})}(x),Nm^{(p^{-1})}(ξ),(γ_i)} ∈ Exc(Γ,^LG)^σ on the left is identified with the action of S_{I,Res_BC(V),x,ξ,(γ_i)} ∈ Exc(Γ,^LH) on the right, where Res_BC is restriction along φ_BC. (ii) For each j ∈ {0,1}, S_{I,N·V,(N·x)∘Δ_p,∇_p∘(N·ξ),(γ_i)} ∈ Exc(Γ,^LG)^σ acts by 0 on T^j(Sht_{G,D+∞x_0,∅};1).
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Theorem 5.11
items.note: The fixed-locus input is the qualified item 60, so this working comparison assumes finite étale π. Smith localization still applies to the entire fixed scheme in general, but at ramified level it cannot be identified with Sht_H by Lemma 5.7. Its comparison with Sht_H requires a separate ramified descent/localization repair in route 2 (E58). Use the corrected item-56 contract for creation and annihilation; retain the original norm-element vanishing target. The central global theorem: it converts the geometric identity BC = Res_BC of Theorem 4.20 into an identity between excursion operators for G and for H. Part (ii) is what makes the character extension of Lemma 5.15 applicable. Review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24), status check: Missing status confirmed. Nm^{(p^{-1})}, N·V, N·x, Δ_p and ∇_p are defined at the start of §5.5 (p. 38), which no item covers (see coverage). The Exc(Γ,^LG)^σ-action on T^j is §5.3.2, also uncovered.
items.originalStatement: Fix a closed point x_0 ∈ X and a closed finite subscheme D. (i) For j ∈ {0,1}, under the isomorphism T^j(Sht_{G,D+∞x_0,∅};1) ≅ H^j_c(Sht_{H,D+∞x_0,∅};1) induced by Lemma 5.7, the action of S_{I,Nm^{(p^{-1})}(V),Nm^{(p^{-1})}(x),Nm^{(p^{-1})}(ξ),(γ_i)} ∈ Exc(Γ,^LG)^σ is identified with the action of S_{I,Res_BC(V),x,ξ,(γ_i)} ∈ Exc(Γ,^LH). (ii) For j ∈ {0,1}, the action of S_{I, N·V, (N·x)∘Δ_p, ∇_p∘(N·ξ), (γ_i)} ∈ Exc(Γ,^LG)^σ on T^j(Sht_{G,D+∞x_0,∅};1) is zero.

review.reason: (1) The item copies a misprint. Part (i) is taken 'with respect to the isomorphism T^j(Sht_{G,D+∞x_0,∅};1) ≅ H^j_c(Sht_{H,D+∞x_0,∅};1)', but for j = 1 the right side is 0: with no legs, Sht_{H,D+nx_0,∅}^{≤μ} is, for large n, a finite discrete set of points. Meanwhile T^1(Sht_G;1) ≅ T^1(Sht_H;1) = H^0_c ⊗ T^1(k) ≅ H^0_c by (3.6) and (5.8). The same sentence ends with 'T^j(Sht_{H,D+∞x_0,∅};1) = H^0_c(Sht_{H,D+∞x_0,∅};1)', and (5.21) uses H^0_c. The target is H^0_c (see new issue). (2) The standing hypotheses are missing: the base change setup, and p odd and good for Ĝ. (3) The quantifiers over (I, V, x, ξ, (γ_i)) are not stated.

items.statement: Assume additionally that π:X′→X is finite étale (hence a C_p-torsor). items.name: The Tate diagonal homomorphism (Definition 5.14)
items.statement: For a commutative ring A of characteristic p with an action of σ (of order p), N·A := {(1+σ+…+σ^{p−1})a : a ∈ A} is an ideal of A^σ. The map Nm: A → A^σ, a ↦ a·σ(a)···σ^{p−1}(a), is multiplicative but not additive, and its composite with A^σ ↠ A^σ/N·A = T^0(A) is a ring homomorphism Δ^p: A → T^0(A), the Tate diagonal. When A is a k-algebra and σ is k-linear, Δ^p is Frobenius-semilinear: Δ^p(λa) = λ^pΔ^p(a) for λ ∈ k.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Definition 5.14
items.note: The algebraic mechanism behind the normalized Brauer homomorphism of Treumann–Venkatesh, isolated here as a general statement. Review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24): route: moved from route 2 to route 1. PAPER-TREUMANN-VENKATESH-16/26 (TV §3.4), routed to that paper's proposed Part II SmithTheoryAndModPFunctoriality, states a special case; Feng's version (any perfect κ, any subring A′ ⊂ A^σ containing Nm(A) and N·A) is the general one. By PROTOCOL §15 it is planned once, in the most foundational roadmap that needs it: route 1, which owns Tate cohomology of Λ[σ]-modules and complexes. Route 2 and SmithTheoryAndModPFunctoriality import it.
items.originalStatement: For A a commutative algebra in characteristic p with a σ-action, N·A is an ideal of A^σ and Nm: A → A^σ, a ↦ a·σ(a)···σ^{p-1}(a), is multiplicative but not additive; its composite with A^σ ↠ A^σ/N·A = T^0(A) is an algebra homomorphism Δ^p: A → T^0(A), the Tate diagonal.

review.reason: Clarification. 'Algebra homomorphism' must be read as a ring (F_p-algebra) homomorphism. For a k-algebra A with k-linear σ, Nm(λa) = λ^p Nm(a), so Δ^p is Frobenius-semilinear, not k-linear. That is why Construction 5.17 linearises it. The item should say so, or a formaliser will state a false k-linearity.

items.name: Unique extension of characters through the Tate diagonal (Lemma 5.15)
items.statement: Let A be a commutative F_p-algebra with a σ-action, κ a perfect field over F_p, and A' ⊂ A^σ a subring containing Nm(A) and N·A. Then any character χ: A' → κ factoring through A'/N·A extends uniquely to a character χ-tilde: A → κ, given by χ-tilde(a) = χ(Nm(a))^{1/p}.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Lemma 5.15
items.note: The engine of every character-matching argument in the paper, both globally in Theorem 5.13 and locally in Theorems 6.21 and 6.26. It is the excursion-algebra analogue of Treumann–Venkatesh §3.4. Review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24): route: moved from route 2 to route 1 with item 65, for the same reason. PAPER-TREUMANN-VENKATESH-16/26 is the special case.

items.name: Norm and norm-element formulas in the excursion algebra (Lemma 5.16)
items.statement: In Exc(Γ,^LG), Nm(S_{I,V,x,ξ,(γ_i)}) = S_{I,Nm(V),Nm(x),Nm(ξ),(γ_i)} and N·S_{I,V,x,ξ,(γ_i)} = S_{I, N·V, (N·x)∘Δ_p, ∇_p∘(N·ξ), (γ_i)}.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Lemma 5.16
items.note: Identifies the multiplicative norm and the additive norm element of the σ-action on the excursion algebra in terms of its generators, so that the subalgebra of Definition 5.19 can be described explicitly. Review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24), status check: Missing status confirmed; the statement matches the page (proof by the relations (2.5)–(2.7) and (5.9)).

items.name: Frobenius twist and linearization of algebras (Construction 5.17)
items.statement: For a k-algebra A, A^{(p)} := A ⊗_{k,Frob} k with the k-semilinear isomorphism a ↦ a ⊗ 1, universal among Frob-semilinear homomorphisms out of A. An F_p-structure φ_0: A ≅ A_0 ⊗_{F_p} k gives a k-linear isomorphism A ≅ A^{(p)} and hence a Frob-semilinear self-isomorphism Frob_{φ_0} of A which is the identity on A_0; precomposing a Frob-semilinear f: A → B with its inverse is the linearization of f. Exc(Γ,^LG) has such an F_p-structure because ^LG is defined over F_p.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Construction 5.17; with Example 5.18
items.note: The algebra counterpart of Construction 4.17, and the step that turns Br^p into a k-linear homomorphism. Review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24): route: moved from route 2 to route 1, which already owns the Frobenius twist of a k-linear category (item 46, Construction 4.17); this is its algebra form. PAPER-TREUMANN-VENKATESH-16/2 (Frobenius twist of a k-vector space) is a special case; SmithTheoryAndModPFunctoriality imports it from here.

items.name: The subalgebra Exc(Γ,^LG)' (Definition 5.19)
items.statement: Exc(Γ,^LG)' ⊂ Exc(Γ,^LG) is the k-subalgebra generated by N·Exc(Γ,^LG) and all elements Nm(S_{I,V,x,ξ,(γ_i)}) = S_{I,Nm(V),Nm(x),Nm(ξ),(γ_i)}; its local analogue Exc(W_v,^LG)' is Definition 6.22.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Definition 5.19; and Definition 6.22
items.note: The subring A' of Lemma 5.15 in the case at hand: a character of it has a unique extension to the full excursion algebra, which is how the base change parameter is pinned down. Review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24), status check: Missing status confirmed. Exc(Γ,^LG)' satisfies the hypotheses of Lemma 5.15. It lies in Exc^σ, and it contains Nm(a) for every a, not only for generators: Nm is multiplicative, Nm(λS) = λ^p Nm(S), and Nm(a+b) − Nm(a) − Nm(b) ∈ N·Exc. It also makes Exc integral over Exc' (the elementary symmetric functions of the σ^i(a) are N·(…) or Nm(a)), which is the lying-over step used in the proof of Theorem 5.13.

items.name: Hecke algebras, their centers and the Bernstein center in characteristic p
items.statement: For K ⊂ G_v an open compact subgroup of prime-to-p pro-order, H(G,K;Λ) := C_c(K\G_v/K;Λ) under convolution normalized so that 1_K is the unit, and Z(G,K;Λ) is its center; for K ⊂ K' convolution with 1_{K'} gives Z(G,K;Λ) → Z(G,K';Λ), and the Bernstein center is Z(G;Λ) := lim_K Z(G,K;Λ) over such K. It is the ring of endomorphisms of the identity functor on smooth k-representations of G_v, so every irreducible admissible Π gives a character χ_Π of Z(G).
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, §6.1.1
items.note: SR.1 plans Hecke algebras over rings with the normalized idempotents e_U defined exactly when the index denominators are units, and the corner description of U-biinvariant Hecke algebras; SR.3 plans the Bernstein center as natural endomorphisms of the identity, though in the complex case. The characteristic-p case is the one the paper needs. Review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24): status planned kept, layers corrected: SR.3 plans the Bernstein centre only for complex coefficients. SR.1 plans H(G,K;Λ) when the pro-order of K is invertible in Λ, with the normalised idempotents and U-biinvariant corners, building on the Hecke ring already in the libraries (mathlib:HeckeRing, definitions; tauceti:instRingHeckeRing, the ring structure). ExcursionOperatorsAndSpectralAction:ES0 plans the centre of the smooth category as natural endomorphisms of the identity over SR.0's coefficients. The mod p Bernstein centre as the inverse limit lim_K ℨ(G,K;k), with its transition maps and its identification with End(id), is not planned: it is split off as a new missing item for route 3.

items.name: The Genestier–Lafforgue correspondence
items.statement: For F_v a local function field of residue characteristic ℓ ≠ p and G reductive over F_v, Genestier–Lafforgue construct Z_G: Exc(W_v,^LG) → Z(G); composing the character of Z(G) attached to an irreducible admissible Π with Z_G and applying Proposition 2.4 gives the semisimple L-parameter ρ_Π: W_v → ^LG(k). Writing Z_{G,r} for the composite with the projection to Z(G,K_r), K_r := G(F_v)_{x,r}, the map is characterised by local-global compatibility.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, §6.1.2; and §6.1.3
items.note: The semisimplified local Langlands correspondence over function fields, for all reductive groups and all irreducible representations. GS.7 plans a local–global comparison at a chosen place beginning from unramified Satake and GL_n, not this construction. Review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24), status check: missing confirmed. ExcursionOperatorsAndSpectralAction:ES5 plans the Fargues–Scholze parameter, not the Genestier–Lafforgue map Z_G; no stage plans GL. GS.7 does not plan it either.

items.name: Local-global compatibility of the excursion action (Proposition 6.1)
items.statement: Let F_v be a local function field of residue characteristic ℓ ≠ p, G reductive over F_v, x ∈ B(G/F_v) and K_r := G(F_v)_{x,r}. Choose a smooth projective curve X over F_ℓ and v ∈ X with X_v = Spec O_v; an extension of G to a reductive group over the generic point of X and then to a parahoric group scheme over X whose restriction to O_v is the parahoric group scheme of x; and an embedding W_v ⊂ Weil(η, η̄). Let r ≥ 0 be an integer and D := rv + D^v a closed finite subscheme of X with D^v supported away from v. Then for every excursion datum (I, f, (γ_i)_{i∈I}) with (γ_i)_{i∈I} ∈ W_v^I, the excursion operator S_{I,f,(γ_i)} acts on H^0_c(Sht_{G,D,∅}; 1) as convolution by Z_{G,r}(S_{I,f,(γ_i)}) ∈ ℨ(G,K_r).
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Proposition 6.1; with Remark 6.2
items.note: Genestier–Lafforgue Proposition 1.3. For D^v large enough the action is faithful, so this characterises Z_G; the independence of the auxiliary global data is proved in their paper by a purely local construction with restricted shtukas, and is used here as a black box.
items.originalStatement: Let r ≥ 0 and D := rv + D^v with D^v supported away from v. For (γ_i)_{i∈I} ⊂ W_v^I, the excursion operator S_{I,f,(γ_i)} acts on H^0_c(Sht_{G,D,∅};1) as convolution by Z_{G,r}(S_{I,f,(γ_i)}) ∈ Z(G,K_r).

review.reason: The item omits the global data the proposition depends on (§6.1.3): a smooth projective curve X over F_ℓ with a point v such that X_v = Spec O_v; an extension of G to a parahoric group scheme over X whose fibre over O_v is the parahoric group scheme of x; and an embedding W_v ⊂ Weil(η, η̄). It also omits that r is an integer (D = rv). The faithfulness in Remark 6.2, which the locator cites, is used in §6.4.1 and Corollary 6.14 but is not stated; see the coverage row for Remark 6.2.

items.name: Bruhat–Tits buildings, parahorics and the Moy–Prasad filtration
items.statement: For H reductive over a local field F_v, B(H/F_v) is the Bruhat–Tits building; to x ∈ B(H/F_v) are attached the parahoric H(F_v)_{x,0} and its decreasing filtration H(F_v)_{x,r}, r ≥ 0, with H(F_v)_{x,0+} = ∪_{s>0} H(F_v)_{x,s} pro-ℓ. If E_v/F_v is unramified then H(E_v)_{x,r}^{Gal(E_v/F_v)} = H(F_v)_{x,r}, and if tamely ramified then the fixed points contain H(F_v)_{x,r}.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, §6.2.2
items.note: ReductiveGroupsPartII:RG2.2 plans buildings with the group action and RG2.3 parahoric and congruence group schemes; the Moy–Prasad filtration in that generality and its Galois descent are the specific content used here. Review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24), status check: 'planned' is only partly right. ReductiveGroupsPartII:RG2.2 plans buildings and the group action. RG2.3 plans parahoric group schemes and 'pro-p congruence subgroups'. No atlas stage mentions the Moy–Prasad filtration G(F_v)_{x,r} for real r ≥ 0, or the pro-ℓ property of G(F_v)_{x,0+}. PAPER-FINTZEN-21/7 routes the Moy–Prasad filtration to RG2.1–RG2.3 as a source route, but only for groups split over a tame extension with the residue characteristic not dividing |W|, which does not cover the arbitrary reductive groups over local function fields used here. No stage plans the Galois descent statements (H(E_v)_{x,r}^{Gal} = H(F_v)_{x,r} for unramified E_v/F_v and ⊃ for tame; B(H/F_v) = B(G/F_v)^{Gal}). Split the item. Buildings and parahorics are planned by RG2.2 and RG2.3. The general Moy–Prasad filtration is planned only if the Fintzen source route is accepted and widened; otherwise it is missing. The descent statements are missing; see the coverage row proposing them as a new item for route 3.

items.name: The Cartan decomposition at a special vertex
items.statement: Let S be a maximal F_v-split torus of H, Z = Z_H(S), and Z := {z ∈ Z(F_v) : α(ω_Z(z)) ≥ 0 for all α ∈ Φ^+}. For a special vertex x in the apartment of S, H(F_v) = H(F_v)_{x,0}·Z·H(F_v)_{x,0}, and for z,z' ∈ Z the double cosets H(F_v)_{x,0} z H(F_v)_{x,0} and H(F_v)_{x,0} z' H(F_v)_{x,0} coincide if and only if z'z^{-1} ∈ Z(F_v)^0, the kernel of the Kottwitz homomorphism.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, §6.2.2; quoted from Kaletha–Prasad Theorem 5.2.1
items.note: ReductiveGroupsPartII:RG2.4 plans the Cartan and Iwahori–Bruhat decompositions in their exact generality with the correct relative cocharacter lattice, dominance conditions and stabilizers. Review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24), status check: planned by ReductiveGroupsPartII:RG2.4 confirmed: it plans 'the Cartan and Iwahori–Bruhat decompositions in their exact generality, with the correct relative cocharacter lattice, dominance conditions and stabilizers'. Z(F_v)^0 is the kernel of the Kottwitz homomorphism on Z(F_v). That is not the κ of BunGAndNewtonStrata:BG1, which is defined on B(G), so RG2.4 must supply it.

items.name: Injectivity of the map of double coset spaces (Proposition 6.3)
items.statement: Let F_v be a local field of residue characteristic ℓ ≠ p, E_v/F_v a finite Galois extension whose degree is prime to ℓ, H a connected reductive group over F_v, G := Res_{E_v/F_v}(H_{E_v}), H_v = H(F_v) ⊂ G_v = G(F_v) = H(E_v). Let x ∈ B(G/F_v) be fixed by Gal(E_v/F_v) (for instance a point of B(H/F_v)), let r > 0, K_r := G(F_v)_{x,r} and U_r := K_r^{Gal(E_v/F_v)} = K_r ∩ H_v. Then the natural map U_r\H_v/U_r → K_r\G_v/K_r is injective. The paper's case r = 0, with x a special vertex of B(G/F_v), is false in general and is not used later.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Proposition 6.3
items.note: For r = 0 this is the Cartan decomposition; for r > 0 it uses that Gal(E_v/F_v) has order prime to ℓ while K_r is pro-ℓ, so that H^1(Gal(E_v/F_v); Stab_{K_r}(b)) vanishes. The referee suggested the simplification of the proof.
items.originalStatement: Let E_v/F_v be a finite Galois extension whose group has order coprime to ℓ, G = Res_{E_v/F_v}(H_{E_v}), x a special vertex in the apartment of a maximal F_v-split torus of G, K_r := G(F_v)_{x,r} and U_r := K_r^{Gal(E_v/F_v)}. Then for r ≥ 0 the map U_r\H_v/U_r → K_r\G_v/K_r is injective.

review.reason: The item copies Proposition 6.3, which is false at r = 0 under its stated hypotheses. Counterexample: H = SL_2, E_v/F_v totally (tamely) ramified, x a vertex of the tree of SL_2(E_v) lying inside an edge of the tree of SL_2(F_v); see the new issue. The r > 0 argument never uses that x is special. It uses only that x is fixed by Gal(E_v/F_v), which makes K_r Gal-stable, and that K_r is pro-ℓ. The item also leaves implicit that x must be Gal-fixed. The paper presupposes this when it writes U_r ⊃ H(F_v)_{x,r} and lets Gal act on H(G,K_r;Λ).

items.name: Surjectivity of restriction of Hecke algebras (Corollary 6.4)
items.statement: In the setting of the corrected Proposition 6.3 (x ∈ B(G/F_v) fixed by Gal(E_v/F_v), r > 0), for every coefficient ring Λ the restriction map H(G,K_r;Λ)^{Gal(E_v/F_v)} → H(H,U_r;Λ) is surjective: for h ∈ H_v the Gal-invariant function 1_{K_r h K_r} restricts to 1_{U_r h U_r}.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Corollary 6.4
items.note: The only consequence of §6.2 used later: it makes the Brauer homomorphism surjective and hence induces a map on centers.
items.originalStatement: For r ≥ 0 the restriction map H(G,K_r;Λ)^{Gal(E_v/F_v)} → H(H,U_r;Λ) is surjective.

review.reason: False at r = 0 as stated, by the same counterexample: every K_0-biinvariant function takes the same value at t = diag(ϖ_F, ϖ_F^{-1}) and at t^{-1}, so 1_{U_0 t U_0} is not a restriction. It holds for every r > 0 and every Gal-fixed x, special or not.

items.name: Plain subgroups
items.statement: Let K ⊂ G_v be a σ-stable open compact subgroup and U := K^σ = K ∩ H_v, so that H_v/U ⊂ (G_v/K)^σ. K is plain if (G_v/K)^σ = H_v/U. Equivalently (proof of Lemma 6.6), the map H^1(⟨σ⟩; K) → H^1(⟨σ⟩; G_v) has trivial fibre over the trivial class.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, §6.3.2
items.note: This is the σ-plainness condition of Treumann–Venkatesh §4.1, in the base change setting where the second condition of that definition is automatic. The same notion is routed by PAPER-TREUMANN-VENKATESH-16; the two routes must not both plan it.
items.originalStatement: For K ⊂ G_v open compact with U := K^σ ⊂ H_v, K is a plain subgroup if (G_v/K)^σ = H_v/U.

review.reason: The paper leaves implicit that K is σ-stable, which is needed for σ to act on G_v/K. It is harmless, but a formal definition must include it.

items.name: The Brauer homomorphism (Lemma 6.5)
items.statement: If K ⊂ G_v is plain, the restriction map from H(G,K)^σ = Fun_{G_v,c}((G_v/K)×(G_v/K),k)^σ to Fun_{H_v,c}((H_v/U)×(H_v/U),k) = H(H_v,U) is an algebra homomorphism, written Br.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Lemma 6.5
items.note: Introduced in Treumann–Venkatesh §4; the proof is that the terms of the convolution indexed by y ∉ H_v/U come in free σ-orbits, so contribute multiples of p. Also routed by PAPER-TREUMANN-VENKATESH-16.

items.name: Deep congruence subgroups are plain (Lemma 6.6)
items.statement: If K ⊂ G(F_v)_{x,0+} for some x ∈ B(G/F_v) then K is plain.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Lemma 6.6
items.note: Because G(F_v)_{x,0+} is pro-ℓ and σ has order p, all its subgroups have vanishing H^1(⟨σ⟩,-), so the fibre of H^1(σ,K) → H^1(σ,G_v) over the trivial class is trivial. This is what supplies plainness at every sufficiently deep Moy–Prasad level.

items.name: The Brauer homomorphism computes the action on Tate cohomology (Lemma 6.7)
items.statement: Let K ⊂ G_v be a plain subgroup, U := K^σ, and Π a smooth representation of G_v ⋊ ⟨σ⟩ over k (for example an irreducible admissible σ-fixed representation with the σ-action of Lemma 6.16). Then the map T^*(Π^K) → T^*(Π) induced by Π^K ⊂ Π lands in T^*(Π)^U. For every h ∈ H(G,K)^σ, the square whose rows are this map T^*(Π^K) → T^*(Π)^U, whose left column is the action of T^0h ∈ T^0(H(G,K)) and whose right column is the action of Br(h) ∈ H(H,U) commutes.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Lemma 6.7
items.note: Treumann–Venkatesh §6.2. Also routed by PAPER-TREUMANN-VENKATESH-16, where it appears as the compatibility diagram (6.1).
items.originalStatement: Assume K ⊂ G_v is plain and Π is a σ-fixed representation of G_v. Then T^*(Π^K) → T^*(Π) lands in the U-invariants, and for every h ∈ H(G,K)^σ the square with vertical maps T^0h and Br(h) commutes.

review.reason: 'σ-fixed representation' is used before it is defined. §6.5.2 defines it only for irreducible admissible Π, as Π ≅ Π^σ. What Tate cohomology needs is an action of G_v ⋊ ⟨σ⟩, which Lemma 6.16 supplies for irreducible admissible σ-fixed Π.

items.name: The Treumann–Venkatesh homomorphism at level r (Definition 6.8)
items.statement: Let r > 0, x ∈ B(G/F_v) be σ-fixed (for example x ∈ B(H/F_v)), K_r := G(F_v)_{x,r} and U_r := K_r^σ. By Lemma 6.6, K_r is plain. By Lemma 6.5 and the corrected Corollary 6.4, Br: H(G,K_r)^σ → H(H,U_r) is a surjective algebra homomorphism. It therefore induces Z(Br): Z(H(G,K_r)^σ) → ℨ(H,U_r), which factors through Z(H(G,K_r)^σ)/N·ℨ(G,K_r). Since ℨ(G,K_r)^σ ⊂ Z(H(G,K_r)^σ), composing the Tate diagonal Δ^p: ℨ(G,K_r) → T^0(ℨ(G,K_r)) of Definition 5.14 with Z(Br) gives a Frob-semilinear ring homomorphism, that is, a k-linear Z′: ℨ(G,K_r)^{(p)} → ℨ(H,U_r). ℨ_{TV,r}: ℨ(G,K_r) → ℨ(H,U_r) is the linearization of Z′ (Construction 5.17) with respect to the F_p-structure ℨ(G,K_r) ≅ ℨ(G,K_r;F_p) ⊗_{F_p} k, i.e. Z′ precomposed with the k-linear isomorphism ℨ(G,K_r) ≅ ℨ(G,K_r)^{(p)} of (6.8).
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Definition 6.8; with Remark 6.9
items.note: Not in Treumann–Venkatesh, but inspired by their normalized Brauer homomorphism: this is the extension of that construction from spherical Hecke algebras to the centers of Hecke algebras at arbitrary Moy–Prasad level.
items.originalStatement: With K = K_r as in Corollary 6.4, Br: H(G,K_r)^σ → H(H,U_r) is a surjective algebra homomorphism, hence induces Z(Br) on centers, which factors through Z(H(G,K_r)^σ)/N·Z(G,K_r). Composing the Tate diagonal Δ^p: Z(G,K_r) → T^0(Z(G,K_r)) with Z(Br) gives a Frob-semilinear map, and Z_{TV,r}: Z(G,K_r) → Z(H,U_r) is its linearization with respect to the F_p-structure Z(G,K_r) ≅ Z(G,K_r;F_p) ⊗_{F_p} k.

review.reason: No level restriction is stated. Br is an algebra homomorphism only for plain K_r, which Lemma 6.6 guarantees for r > 0 (K_0 need not be plain). Surjectivity comes from Corollary 6.4, whose r = 0 case fails. The construction must therefore be stated for r > 0, at a Gal-fixed x.

items.name: Compatibility of Z_{TV,r} with change of level (Lemma 6.10)
items.statement: In the setting of item 81 (x σ-fixed), for 0 < r < s let e_G^{s→r}: ℨ(G,K_s) → ℨ(G,K_r) and e_H^{s→r}: ℨ(H,U_s) → ℨ(H,U_r) be convolution with the normalized idempotents 1_{K_r} and 1_{U_r}; these exist because K_r and U_r are pro-ℓ. Then e_H^{s→r} ∘ ℨ_{TV,s} = ℨ_{TV,r} ∘ e_G^{s→r}.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Lemma 6.10
items.note: The compatibility that lets the maps at each level be assembled into a map of Bernstein centers.
items.originalStatement: For s > r the square formed by Z_{TV,s}, Z_{TV,r} and the maps e_G^{s→r}: Z(G,K_s) → Z(G,K_r) and e_H^{s→r}: Z(H,U_s) → Z(H,U_r) given by convolution with the appropriate indicator functions commutes.

review.reason: The item omits the hypotheses of §6.4. K_r must have prime-to-p pro-order, so that the normalized idempotent 1_{K_r} exists in H(G,K_s). Also r > 0 (with s > r), so that ℨ_{TV,r} is defined.

items.name: The base change homomorphism for Bernstein centers (Definition 6.11)
items.statement: Z_TV: Z(G) → Z(H) is the inverse limit over r of the Z_{TV,r}: Z(G,K_r) → Z(H,U_r). It is defined over any local field of residue characteristic ℓ ≠ p; its properties are proved here only for local function fields.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Definition 6.11
items.note: This realises, in characteristic p, the base change homomorphism of Bernstein centers envisaged by Haines, for general groups and arbitrary depth. Review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24): Minor. The limit is over r > 0 at a fixed σ-fixed x. It is a map ℨ(G) → ℨ(H) because {K_r} and {U_r = K_r ∩ H_v} are cofinal among the open compact subgroups of prime-to-p pro-order.

items.name: The Brauer homomorphism on permutation modules (Lemma 6.12)
items.statement: Let S̃ be a set with an action of G_v ⋊ ⟨σ⟩ on which a σ-stable open compact subgroup K ⊂ G_v acts freely. Let S := S̃/K, U := K^σ, and let k[T] denote the k-valued functions on a set T. H(G,K) = End_{G_v}(k[G_v/K]) acts on k[S] = Hom_{G_v}(k[G_v/K], k[S̃]). This induces an action of T^0(H(G,K)) on T^0(k[S]) ≅ k[S^σ] and, by inflation, of H(G,K)^σ on k[S^σ]. In the same way H(H,U) acts on k[S̃^σ/U]. If K is plain, then k[S̃^σ/U] is an H(G,K)^σ-stable direct summand of k[S^σ], and for every h ∈ H(G,K)^σ the action of h on k[S̃^σ/U] equals that of Br(h) ∈ H(H,U).
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Lemma 6.12
items.note: The function-level counterpart of Lemma 6.7, used to transport the excursion action through the identification of Tate cohomology of shtukas.
items.originalStatement: Assume K ⊂ G_v is plain. Then k[S-tilde^σ/U] is an H(G,K)^σ-direct summand of k[S^σ], and for all h ∈ H(G,K)^σ the action of h on k[S-tilde^σ/U] agrees with the action of Br(h) ∈ H(H,U).

review.reason: The item uses S̃, S and the Hecke action on k[S] without their definitions (§6.4.3).

items.name: Tate cohomology of shtukas intertwines the two center actions (Corollary 6.13)
items.statement: Working comparison hypothesis: the local data admit a compatible global model with π:X′→X finite étale, the qualified global comparisons of items 62–63, and the large auxiliary level needed for faithful local-global comparison. In the setting of §6.4.1 (X, v, a closed point x_0 ≠ v, D := rv + ∞x_0 as in §5.4.2, the parahoric model at v attached to a σ-fixed x), for every integer r ≥ 1 and every z ∈ T^0ℨ(G,K_r), the action of z on T^0(Sht_{G,D,∅}; 1) agrees with the action of Z(Br)(z) ∈ ℨ(H,U_r) on T^0(Sht_{H,D,∅}; 1), under the identification T^0(Sht_{G,D,∅}; 1) ≅ T^0(Sht_{H,D,∅}; 1) of §3.4.5. That is, the square in (6.9) commutes.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Corollary 6.13
items.note: The bridge between the global identity of Theorem 5.11 and the purely local statement of Corollary 6.14. The unrestricted ramified local formula remains the published target, recorded in sourceTarget. A finite étale global cover has unramified completion at v, so this working hypothesis supplies no ramified local theorem. Route 3 imports the required ramified global repair from route 2; extra level at x_0, or the local r > 0 correction alone, does not establish it (E58).
items.originalStatement: For all r ≥ 1 the action of z ∈ T^0 Z(G,K_r) on T^0(Sht_{G,D,∅};1) agrees with the action of Z(Br)(z) on T^0(Sht_{H,D,∅};1) under the identification of the two Tate cohomologies coming from equivariant localisation.

review.reason: The global setting is omitted: a closed point x_0 ≠ v of X, D := rv + ∞x_0 interpreted as in §5.4.2, and the parahoric model at v attached to x. Z(Br) requires the corrected Corollary 6.4 (r ≥ 1, x σ-fixed).

That is, the square in (6.9) commutes.

items.name: Unique σ-action on a σ-fixed representation (Lemma 6.16)
items.statement: Let Π be an irreducible admissible representation of G_v over k and Π^σ := Π ∘ σ. Π is σ-fixed if Π ≅ Π^σ as G_v-representations. If Π is σ-fixed, the G_v-action on Π extends uniquely to an action of G_v ⋊ ⟨σ⟩.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Lemma 6.16
items.note: Treumann–Venkatesh Proposition 6.1; it makes T^0(Π) and T^1(Π) well defined, with their H_v = G_v^σ-actions. Also routed by PAPER-TREUMANN-VENKATESH-16.
items.originalStatement: If Π is an irreducible admissible σ-fixed representation of G_v, then the G_v-action on Π extends uniquely to an action of G_v ⋊ ⟨σ⟩.

review.reason: 'σ-fixed' is not defined in the item.

items.name: Linkage (Definition 6.17)
items.statement: An irreducible admissible representation π of H_v is linked with an irreducible admissible representation Π of G_v if the Frobenius twist π^{(p)} := π ⊗_{k,Frob} k appears in T^0(Π) or T^1(Π).
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Definition 6.17; with Example 6.19
items.note: Treumann–Venkatesh Definition 6.2. The motivating example G = H^p with σ acting by cyclic permutation gives T^0(π^{⊠p}) ≅ π^{(p)}, which is why the Frobenius twist is there. Also routed by PAPER-TREUMANN-VENKATESH-16.

items.name: The Treumann–Venkatesh conjecture (Conjecture 6.18)
items.statement: Conjecture: if π is linked to Π then π base changes to Π, i.e. ρ_Π ≅ φ_BC ∘ ρ_π.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Conjecture 6.18
items.note: Treumann–Venkatesh Conjecture 6.3, formulated here precisely using the Genestier–Lafforgue correspondence, which did not exist when it was stated. Theorem 6.21 proves it in the form stated there. Also routed by PAPER-TREUMANN-VENKATESH-16, where it is the second conjecture of §6.3.

items.name: Tate cohomology realises base change, local form (Theorem 6.21)
items.statement: Working comparison hypothesis: the local data admit a compatible global model with π:X′→X finite étale, the qualified global comparisons of items 62–63, and the large auxiliary level needed for faithful local-global comparison. Let F_v be a local function field of residue characteristic ℓ ≠ p, E_v/F_v cyclic of degree p, σ a generator of its Galois group, G := Res_{E_v/F_v}(H_{E_v}), and assume p is an odd good prime for Ĝ. Let Π be an irreducible admissible σ-fixed representation of G_v over k, with the action of G_v ⋊ ⟨σ⟩ from Lemma 6.16. Let χ_{Π^{(p)}}: Exc(W_v, ^LG) → k be the character attached to the Frobenius twist Π^{(p)}. Regard T^*(Π) := T^*(⟨σ⟩, Π) as a smooth H_v-representation. Then for every character χ: Exc(W_v, ^LH) → k occurring in the action of Exc(W_v, ^LH) on T^*(Π) through Z_H: Exc(W_v, ^LH) → ℨ(H) (in particular χ = χ_π for every irreducible subquotient π of T^0(Π) or T^1(Π)), χ ∘ φ_BC^* = χ_{Π^{(p)}}.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Theorem 6.21; which implies Theorem 1.2
items.note: Proved by combining the compatibility (6.4) of Br with the action on T^*(Π), the identification of excursion operators of Corollary 6.14, the vanishing of Theorem 5.11(ii), and the uniqueness of character extensions of Lemma 5.15. The unrestricted ramified local formula remains the published target, recorded in sourceTarget. A finite étale global cover has unramified completion at v, so this working hypothesis supplies no ramified local theorem. Route 3 imports the required ramified global repair from route 2; extra level at x_0, or the local r > 0 correction alone, does not establish it (E58).
items.originalStatement: Assume p is an odd good prime for G-hat. Let Π be an irreducible admissible representation of G_v and χ_{Π^{(p)}}: Exc(W_v,^LG) → k the character of its Frobenius twist. Form T^*(Π) as a smooth H_v-representation. Then for any irreducible character χ: Exc(W_v,^LH) → k appearing in the action on T^*(Π) through Z_H, the composite χ ∘ φ_BC^* agrees with χ_{Π^{(p)}}.

review.reason: Π must be σ-fixed, as in Theorem 1.2, because T^*(⟨σ⟩, Π) needs the σ-action of Lemma 6.16. The printed Theorem 6.21 omits this too (recorded as a new misprint). The standing setting of §6.5.1 is also omitted.

items.name: Base change of representations (Definition 6.23)
items.statement: For π irreducible admissible of H_v and Π of G_v over k, π base changes to Π if ρ_Π ≅ φ_BC ∘ ρ_π in H^1(W_v, G-hat(k)). The fibres of the Genestier–Lafforgue correspondence are used as a substitute for L-packets, which are not available for general groups and representations.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Definition 6.23
items.note: The precise notion of local base change proved to exist in Theorem 6.26.

items.name: Hecke algebras are finite over their centers (Theorem 6.24)
items.statement: For every x ∈ B(G/F_v), every r ≥ 0 and K_r := G(F_v)_{x,r}, the Hecke algebra H(G,K_r) with k-coefficients is finite over its center Z(G,K_r), which is itself a finitely generated k-algebra.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Theorem 6.24; with Remark 6.25
items.note: Quoted from Dat–Helm–Kurinczuk–Moss, who prove it over an arbitrary Z_p-algebra. The characteristic-zero statement is Bernstein's; the banal case was known to experts from Vignéras's work. This finiteness plus the Artin–Tate lemma and Nakayama is what produces the base change representation. Review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24): status missing → planned: SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups:SR.6 follows Dat–Helm–Kurinczuk–Moss, Theorems 1.1–1.2: Hecke algebras with coefficients in a noetherian Z_ℓ-algebra, ℓ different from the residue characteristic, are finite over their centres, which are finitely generated. k = F̄_p with p ≠ ℓ is such a ring, so route 3 imports SR.6.

items.name: Existence of local base change with level control (Theorem 6.26)
items.statement: Working comparison hypothesis: the local data admit a compatible global model with π:X′→X finite étale, the qualified global comparisons of items 62–63, and the large auxiliary level needed for faithful local-global comparison. Suppose p is an odd good prime for G-hat. Let r > 0 and fix x ∈ B(H/F_v), K_r := G(F_v)_{x,r} and U_r := K_r^σ. Let π be an irreducible representation of H_v over k with non-zero U_r-fixed vectors and L-parameter ρ_π. Then there is an irreducible representation Π of G_v over k with non-zero K_r-fixed vectors such that ρ_Π ≅ φ_BC ∘ ρ_π.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Theorem 6.26; which implies Theorem 1.1
items.note: At r > 0 the corrected double-coset and plain-subgroup inputs apply at any σ-fixed x. The proof still needs Corollary 6.14, whose global fixed-locus input must meet the stated working hypothesis or be replaced by the ramified comparison. The prior E48–E51 level/building issues and r=0 boundary are retained. The unrestricted ramified local formula remains the published target, recorded in sourceTarget. A finite étale global cover has unramified completion at v, so this working hypothesis supplies no ramified local theorem. Route 3 imports the required ramified global repair from route 2; extra level at x_0, or the local r > 0 correction alone, does not establish it (E58).

beforeRedteamFix.note: The proof produces a maximal ideal m_π' of Exc(W_v,^LG)' whose unique extension is χ_π ∘ φ_BC^*, then uses the finiteness of Theorem 6.24 to find an irreducible H(G,K_r)-subquotient of H(G,K_r)/H(G,K_r)n_π on which the excursion algebra acts through it. Because x need not be a special vertex, Corollary 6.4 is not available and Br need not induce a map of centers. Review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24), status check: missing is right; route 3. The note repeats footnote 13's claim that Br need not be surjective when x is not special. That claim is unnecessary for r > 0: the corrected Corollary 6.4 holds at every σ-fixed x, including every x ∈ B(H/F_v). The proof as printed applies Corollary 6.14 outside the setting in which the paper proves it, and asserts the case r = 0 as 'classical' without argument; both are recorded as new issues (gaps affecting the proof).

items.name: Depth estimate for the base change (Remark 6.27)
items.statement: Working comparison hypothesis: the local data admit a compatible global model with π:X′→X finite étale, the qualified global comparisons of items 62–63, and the large auxiliary level needed for faithful local-global comparison. Let π be an irreducible representation of H_v over k of depth r, that is, r is the least real number ≥ 0 with π^{H(F_v)_{y,r+}} ≠ 0 for some y ∈ B(H/F_v), with the Moy–Prasad filtration normalized so that F_v^× has value group Z. Let x ∈ B(H/F_v) with π^{H(F_v)_{x,r+}} ≠ 0. Since E_v/F_v is cyclic of degree p ≠ ℓ, it is unramified or tamely ramified. Hence B(H/F_v) = B(G/F_v)^{Gal(E_v/F_v)} and (G(F_v)_{x,r+})^{Gal(E_v/F_v)} = H(F_v)_{x,r+}. The proof of Theorem 6.26, run at the level G(F_v)_{x,r+}, therefore gives a base change Π of π with Π^{G(F_v)_{x,r+}} ≠ 0, so depth(Π) ≤ depth(π). If E_v/F_v is ramified and Π is regarded as a representation of H(E_v), with the filtration normalized so that E_v^× has value group Z, then H(E_v)_{x,pr} = G(F_v)_{x,r} and the estimate reads depth(Π) ≤ p·depth(π).
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Remark 6.27
items.note: The inequalities are expected to be optimal. The proof of the depth estimate uses neither Corollary 6.4 nor the Treumann–Venkatesh homomorphism. The unrestricted ramified local formula remains the published target, recorded in sourceTarget. A finite étale global cover has unramified completion at v, so this working hypothesis supplies no ramified local theorem. Route 3 imports the required ramified global repair from route 2; extra level at x_0, or the local r > 0 correction alone, does not establish it (E58).
items.originalStatement: Let π be irreducible of depth r, with x ∈ B(H/F_v) such that π^{H(F_v)_{x,r+}} ≠ 0. If E_v/F_v is unramified, or tamely ramified, then B(H/F_v) = B(G/F_v)^{Gal(E_v/F_v)} and (G(F_v)_{x,r+})^{Gal(E_v/F_v)} = H(F_v)_{x,r+}, so the proof of Theorem 6.26 produces a base change Π with Π^{G(F_v)_{x,r+}} ≠ 0 and hence depth(Π) ≤ depth(π); in the normalisation where H(E_v)_{x,pr} = G(F_v)_{x,r} the estimate reads depth(Π) ≤ p·depth(π).

review.reason: The paper states the normalization caveat H(E_v)_{x,pr} = G(F_v)_{x,r}, which gives depth(Π) ≤ p·depth(π), only for the ramified case. For unramified E_v/F_v the two normalizations agree, and the estimate is depth(Π) ≤ depth(π) in both. The item also uses 'depth' without defining it.

items.name: Hyperbolic localisation and the constant term functor
items.statement: Let H be reductive over a separably closed field F of characteristic ≠ p, G = H^p, and fix a regular σ-equivariant cocharacter κ: G_m → H; its centraliser in G is a maximal torus T ⊂ G and T_H := T ∩ H is a maximal torus of H. The fixed points of G_m acting on Gr_G by left translation through κ are the t^ν, ν ∈ X_*(T); the attracting locus of t^ν is the semi-infinite orbit S_ν, with inclusion i_ν: S_ν → Gr_G (a locally closed embedding of ind-schemes) and projection p_ν: S_ν → t^ν ∈ Gr_T. The constant term (hyperbolic localisation) functor is CT_G := ⊕_ν Rp_{ν!} i_ν^*: D^b_c(Gr_G;Λ)^{G_m-mon} → D^b_c(Gr_T;Λ)^{G_m-mon}, and CT_G[deg_G] := ⊕_ν Rp_{ν!} i_ν^*[⟨2ρ_G, ν⟩]; similarly CT_H[deg_H] for H and T_H. Both are t-exact on L^+-equivariant objects (equivariance implies monodromicity) and, under Geometric Satake, CT_G[deg_G] corresponds to Res^Ĝ_T̂: Rep_Λ(Ĝ) → Rep_Λ(T̂) and CT_H[deg_H] to Res^Ĥ_{T̂_H} (diagram (A.1); Remark A.1: for the scheme-theoretic Gr_G in equal characteristic with modular étale coefficients this is not fully documented, cf. [BR18, p. 66], [FS, p. 233]).
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, §A.4
items.note: GeometricSatakeAndFusion:GS1 plans semi-infinite geometry and constructibility, which is where hyperbolic localisation and the constant-term functor live; Remark A.1 notes that the displayed commutative diagram is not completely documented in the literature in this generality. Review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24): status planned → missing: GeometricSatakeAndFusion:GS1 plans semi-infinite orbits and hyperbolic localisation for the Fargues–Scholze B_dR^+ (and Witt-vector) Grassmannians over Div^1, and GS4:integral-dual-group the naturality of the constant term for Levi restriction, again for that Grassmannian. The paper needs the scheme-theoretic equal-characteristic Gr_G over a separably closed field with k- and O-coefficients, which GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands:GS.1 does not plan beyond rational ℓ-adic coefficients; Remark A.1 notes that (A.1) is undocumented in this generality. Route 1 owns it, with GS1 and GS4:integral-dual-group as the models to transport.
items.originalStatement: Fix a regular σ-equivariant cocharacter κ: G_m → H with centraliser a maximal torus T ⊂ G such that T_H := T ∩ H is maximal in H. The G_m-fixed points on Gr_G are the t^ν for ν ∈ X_*(T), with attracting semi-infinite orbits S_ν; CT_G := ⊕_ν Rp_{ν!} i_ν^* on monodromic complexes, and CT_G[deg_G] with deg_G(ν) = ⟨2ρ_G,ν⟩ is t-exact and is intertwined by Geometric Satake with restriction along T-hat → G-hat.

review.reason: Only the G-half of (A.1) is recorded; the paper uses both squares of (A.1) (for G with T and for H with T_H) and applies CT_H also on the σ-equivariant categories D^b_{c,σ}(Gr_H)^{G_m-mon}. The coefficient ring Λ is arbitrary (used for Λ = k, O).

items.name: Compatibility of BC with the constant term functor (Lemma A.2)
items.statement: Assume H is a reductive group over a separably closed field F of characteristic ≠ p, G = H^p with σ acting by cyclic rotation of the factors (the ith factor to the (i+1)st mod p), p is odd and good for Ĝ (equivalently for Ĥ), k is an algebraic closure of F_p and O = W(k), and let κ, T = T_H^p, T_H be as in §A.4. Consider the cube (A.3) whose top face is the square of Theorem 4.20 (Parity^0_{L^+G}(Gr_G;k) →BC Parity^0_{L^+H}(Gr_H;k), Tilt_k(Ĝ) →Res_BC Tilt_k(Ĥ), the diagonals being the Satake equivalences of Theorem 4.8), whose bottom face is the same square for the tori (Parity^0_{L^+T}(Gr_T;k) →BC Parity^0_{L^+T_H}(Gr_{T_H};k), Tilt_k(T̂) →Res_BC Tilt_k(T̂_H)), and whose vertical arrows are CT_G[deg_G], CT_H[deg_H], Res^Ĝ_T̂ and Res^Ĥ_{T̂_H}. Then the back face (Res^Ĥ_{T̂_H} ∘ Res_BC ≅ Res_BC ∘ Res^Ĝ_T̂), the front face (CT_H[deg_H] ∘ BC ≅ BC ∘ CT_G[deg_G]), and the left and right faces ((A.1) for G and for H) commute.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Lemma A.2
items.note: The reduction of Theorem 4.20 to the case of a torus: once the four side faces commute and CT is conservative, commutativity of the top follows from that of the bottom.
items.originalStatement: In the cube whose top face is Res_BC on Tilt_k(G-hat) and Tilt_k(H-hat), whose bottom face is Res_BC on Tilt_k(T-hat) and Tilt_k(T-hat_H), whose middle faces are BC on normalized parity sheaves for Gr_G, Gr_H, Gr_T and Gr_{T_H}, and whose vertical arrows are the restriction functors and CT_G[deg_G], CT_H[deg_H], the back, front, left and right faces commute.

review.reason: The cube is described wrongly. In (A.3) the top face is the square of Theorem 4.20 (Tilt_k(Ĝ), Tilt_k(Ĥ), Parity^0_{L^+G}(Gr_G;k), Parity^0_{L^+H}(Gr_H;k)); the bottom face is its torus analogue; the back face is the square of restriction functors between tilting categories; the front face is BC with the CT functors; the left and right faces are (A.1). The note's account of the reduction is also wrong: the paper uses that Res^Ĥ_{T̂_H} is faithful and that tilting modules are determined by their characters [Don93, p. 46], not conservativity of CT (Lemma A.3, used only for Lemma 4.21); and that reduction step has a gap (issue below).

items.name: Conservativity of the constant term functor on the Tate category (Lemma A.3)
items.statement: The functor CT: Perf_{(L^+H)}(Gr_H;T_k) → Perf_{(L^+T_H)}(Gr_{T_H};T_k) is conservative.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Lemma A.3
items.note: This is what makes the reduction to a torus legitimate in the Tate category.

items.name: Additivity of the base change functor
items.statement: BC(F ⊕ F') ≅ BC(F) ⊕ BC(F'): indeed Nm(F ⊕ F') ≅ Nm(F) ⊕ Nm(F') ⊕ (a direct sum of free σ-orbits), so the restrictions to the fixed locus differ by a perfect complex of O[σ]-modules and agree in the Tate category; the lifting functor L and Frob_p^{-1} are additive, and F is essentially surjective.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, §A.3
items.note: The first step of the proof of Theorem 4.20, and the reason the multiplicative norm Nm becomes additive after the Smith operation — the categorical shadow of the Tate diagonal.

items.name: Xue's Eichler–Shimura relation (Proposition B.1)
items.statement: [Xue, Proposition 7.2.6] Let v be a closed point of X° ∖ D, of degree deg v. For any finite set I = Ĩ ⊔ {0} and any V ∈ Rep_k(Ĝ^I) there exists W ∈ Rep_k(Ĝ) such that Σ_{α=0}^{dim W} (−1)^α S_{∧^{dim W−α}W,v}(F^{deg v}_{{0}})^α = 0 in End_{D^c((X°∖D)^Ĩ×v;k)}(R^jπ_{I!}(Sht°_{G,D,I}|_{(X°∖D)^Ĩ×v};Sat(V))). Here S_{W',v} is Lafforgue's operator [Laf18, §6] and F_{{0}} is the partial Frobenius at the leg 0.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Proposition B.1
items.note: Quoted from Xue Proposition 7.2.6. It is the input that lets Drinfeld's lemma be applied, by making the partial Frobenius act integrally over a finitely generated algebra. Review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24), status check: Missing status confirmed. GS.4 follows Lafforgue's route (Drinfeld's lemma on the Hecke-finite sector) and does not plan an Eichler–Shimura relation. Xue's integral/torsion-coefficient version needs route 2.
items.originalStatement: Let v be a closed point of the open locus, of degree deg v. For any finite set I = I-tilde ⊔ {0} and any V ∈ Rep_k(G-hat^I) there is W ∈ Rep_k(G-hat) such that Σ_{α=0}^{dim W} (-1)^α S_{∧^{dim W - α}W, v}(F_{{0}}^{deg v})^α = 0 as an endomorphism of R^jπ_{I!} of the Satake sheaf restricted over v.

review.reason: The item's v must lie in X° ∖ D, not just in the open locus X°: the relation lives on (X°∖D)^Ĩ × v, which lies in (X°∖D)^I only if v ∉ D (the legs avoid D). The paper writes v ∈ X° (see new issue on Lemma B.3).

items.name: The S = T theorem (Theorem B.2)
items.statement: S_{W,v} agrees with the Hecke operator T_{W,v} after restricting to (X \ (D ∪ v))^I.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Theorem B.2
items.note: The identification of the excursion-type operator with the classical Hecke operator away from the point v, needed to run the Eichler–Shimura argument in Tate cohomology. Review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24), status check: Missing status is right for the form used here, but it should cite what is planned. GS.5's 'unramified Satake compatibility' is Lafforgue's characteristic-zero S = T theorem ([Laf18, §6]). What the paper needs is the integral-coefficient version (Xiao–Zhu Theorem 6.0.1(2), written integrally in Yu22, Theorem 5.1 and Corollary 5.5), which holds at the level of cohomological correspondences and hence for Tate cohomology. That version is not planned. Route 2 should own it and import the characteristic-zero statement's set-up from GS.5. The operator S_{W,v} itself is defined by no item (see coverage).

items.name: Eichler–Shimura in Tate cohomology (Lemma B.3)
items.statement: With v and I as in Proposition B.1, for any V ∈ Rep_k(G-hat^I) there is W ∈ Rep_k(G-hat) with Σ_{α=0}^{dim W}(-1)^α S_{∧^{dim W-α}W,v}(F_{{0}}^{deg v})^α = 0 as an endomorphism of T^j Rπ_{I!} of the Satake sheaf restricted over v.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Lemma B.3
items.note: The Tate cohomology version of Proposition B.1, obtained from the long exact sequence for Tate cohomology. Review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24), status check: Missing status confirmed; the statement matches the page (with v ∈ X°∖D as in item 100, correcting the printed 'v ∈ X'; see new issue).

items.name: The finite-type filtration on Tate cohomology (Lemma B.4)
items.statement: Let 𝔗 := T^jRπ_{I!}(Sht_{G,D,I}|_{(X°∖D)^I};Sat(V)) and 𝔗^μ := T^jRπ_{I!}(Sht^{≤μ}_{G,D,I}|_{(X°∖D)^I};Sat(V)) be the j-th Tate cohomology sheaves, 𝔗^μ being constructible, so that T^j(Sht_{G,D,I};V) ≅ 𝔗|_{η̄^I} by proper base change. Let Ω ⊂ (X°∖D)^I be a dense open subscheme on which 𝔗^μ is lisse, v ∈ Ω a closed point, v_i := pr_i(v) (i ∈ I), and A^μ := ⊗_{i∈I} H_{G,v_i}, the tensor product of the local Hecke algebras at the v_i (a k-algebra of finite type). Set M^μ := Σ_{(n_i)∈N^I} A^μ·∏_{i∈I}F^{n_i}_{{i}}(∏_{i∈I}(Frob^{n_i}_{{i}})^* Im(𝔗^μ|_{η̄^I} → 𝔗|_{η̄^I})). Then M^μ ⊂ 𝔗|_{η̄^I} is stable under the partial Frobenii F_{{i}} and is an A^μ-module of finite type; and T^j(Sht_{G,D,I};V) = ∪_μ M^μ.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Lemma B.4
items.note: Following Xue §1: the filtration by Harder–Narasimhan truncation is what supplies the finiteness hypothesis in Drinfeld's lemma. Review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24), status check: Missing status confirmed. The printed lemma asserts stability only under F_{{i}}; Lemma B.5 needs stability under all of FWeil, including F_{{i}}^{-1} (see the new gap issue).
items.originalStatement: The submodule M^μ ⊂ T|_{η^I-bar} ≅ T^j(Sht_{G,D,I};V) is stable under the partial Frobenii F_{{i}} and of finite type over A^μ.

review.reason: The statement is not self-contained. 𝔗, M^μ and A^μ are used but not defined, and the item omits the conclusion T^j(Sht_{G,D,I};V) = ∪_μ M^μ, which the application of Lemma B.5 needs. As printed, 𝔗 is Rπ_{I!}(…) (a complex), but the isomorphism T^j(Sht_{G,D,I};V) ≅ 𝔗|_{η̄^I} and 'M^μ … finite-dimensional' need the j-th Tate cohomology sheaf (see new issue).

items.name: Drinfeld's lemma applied to Tate cohomology (Lemma B.5)
items.statement: [Xue, Lemma 7.4.2] Let A be a finitely generated k-algebra and M an A-module of finite type. Then any continuous A[FWeil(η^I,η̄^I)]-action on M factors through the surjection FWeil(η^I,η̄^I) ↠ Weil(η,η̄)^I. Applied to each M^μ of Lemma B.4, this gives Proposition 5.6 (p. 64).
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Lemma B.5, §B.3 (p. 64); the proof of Proposition 5.6 follows it on p. 64.
items.note: GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands:GS.4 plans Drinfeld's lemma in the lisse/finite-rank setting and its justification on the Hecke-finite sector, together with the continuous action of a product of global Galois groups; the application here is to Tate cohomology rather than cohomology. Review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24): status planned → missing: GS.4 plans Drinfeld's lemma in the lisse, finite-rank setting and its use on the Hecke-finite sector, with characteristic-zero ℓ-adic coefficients. Lemma B.5 concerns modules of finite type over a finitely generated algebra (not of finite rank over the coefficient field) with discrete k = F̄_p coefficients. Route 2, which already owns Proposition 5.6 and Lemmas B.1–B.4, owns it and imports GS.4's Drinfeld's lemma.
items.originalStatement: Drinfeld's lemma, in Xue's form (Lemma 7.4.2 of Xue), applied to the filtration of Lemma B.4 shows that the FWeil(η^I,η^I-bar)-action on T^j(Sht_{G,D,I};V) factors through Weil(η,η-bar)^I, which is Proposition 5.6.

review.reason: The statement is not Lemma B.5. It paraphrases the proof of Proposition 5.6 (item 58), so Lemma B.5 is stated nowhere in the extraction. Lemma B.5 is Xue's form of Drinfeld's lemma for finite-type modules over a finitely generated k-algebra.

items.originalLocator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Lemma B.5; concluding the proof of Proposition 5.6

items.name: Tate cohomology of a module over a cyclic group of order p
items.statement: For a Λ[σ]-module M with σ of order p, T^0(M) = M^σ/N·M and T^1(M) = ker(N: M → M)/(1-σ)·M, where N = 1 + σ + ··· + σ^{p-1}; these are 2-periodic in the index and a short exact sequence of σ-modules induces a six-term exact sequence.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, §3.4; the first display
items.note: Mathlib has the Tate complex and Tate cohomology of a finite group with the connecting map and the long exact sequence; Tau Ceti identifies degree 0 with M^G/NM and degree -1 with ker N/I_G M and proves 2-periodicity for a cyclic group, so T^0 and T^1 here are Tate cohomology in degrees 0 and -1 of ⟨σ⟩. Review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24), status check: Library status confirmed. Mathlib 082e2d3 (RepresentationTheory/Homological/TateCohomology/Basic.lean) has tateCohomology, Rep.tateNorm, and TateCohomology.δ, exact₁ and exact₃ (the ℤ-indexed long exact sequence for a finite group). Tau Ceti f790474 has TauCeti.TateCohomology.H0IsoNormQuotient (Ĥ^0 ≅ M^G/N·M) and HNegOneIsoNormKernelQuotient (Ĥ^{−1} ≅ ker N / I_G·M, with I_G·M = (1−σ)M for G = ⟨σ⟩), and Rep.FiniteCyclicGroup.periodicIso (Ĥ^m ≅ Ĥ^n for m ≡ n mod 2, [IsCyclic G]). So T^0 = Ĥ^0 and T^1 = Ĥ^{−1} ≅ Ĥ^1. One caveat: periodicIso has no naturality lemma in M at the pin, and folding the ℤ-indexed sequence into the six-term sequence the item states needs one. That lemma is small and missing, but the paper itself uses only the ℤ-indexed sequence (§3.4.4).

items.name: Witt vectors of an algebraic closure of F_p as coefficient ring
items.statement: O := W(k) is the ring of p-typical Witt vectors of k, an algebraic closure of F_p; it is a p-adically complete discrete valuation ring with maximal ideal pO and residue field O/pO ≅ k.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, §4.1, p. 19 (definition O := W(k)); used from §4.2, p. 20
items.note: Mathlib has Witt vectors of a commutative ring of characteristic p with the ring structure, Frobenius, the Teichmüller lift and the discrete-valuation-ring statement for a perfect field. Review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24), status check: Library status confirmed at 082e2d3: WittVector (Defs.lean), WittVector.isDiscreteValuationRing (DiscreteValuationRing.lean, for k a perfect field of characteristic p). For 'complete with residue field k' cite also WittVector.isAdicCompleteIdealSpanP (Complete.lean) and WittVector.quotientPEquiv (W(k)/p ≅ k, Complete.lean). WittVector.frobenius and WittVector.teichmuller exist but are not used by the paper.
items.originalStatement: O := W(k) is the ring of Witt vectors of the algebraically closed field k of characteristic p, a complete discrete valuation ring with residue field k; it is the integral coefficient ring for which the Tate category has Ext^* supported in even degrees and hence Tate-parity sheaves behave well.

review.reason: The second clause ('the integral coefficient ring for which the Tate category has Ext^* supported in even degrees') is not part of the definition and is not a library fact: it is (4.1), [LL21, Proposition 4.6.1], proposed below as a new item. The statement should stop at the Witt-vector facts. Locator: O := W(k) is introduced in §4.1, p. 19.

items.name: The group ring of a cyclic group of order p and its flat modules
items.statement: Λ[σ] is the group ring of ⟨σ⟩ ≅ Z/pZ over the p-adic coefficient ring Λ; for Λ = k a field of characteristic p it is Artinian local, so a module over it is flat if and only if it is free if and only if it is projective.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, §3.1; and §3.4.1
items.note: Mathlib has group algebras, their module theory, and the equivalence of flat, projective and free over an Artinian local ring; Feng's argument for Lemma 3.2 is exactly the chain of Stacks Project references for these facts. Review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24): status library → missing: mathlib:Module.free_of_flat_of_isLocalRing requires [Module.Finite R P], but the paper needs arbitrary flat k[σ]-modules (Definition 3.1: 'not necessarily finite'; §3.4.1 cites Stacks 051E, flat ⇔ projective ⇔ free over a local ring with nilpotent maximal ideal). That lemma is not at the pin, and neither library has IsLocalRing for k[Z/p] ≅ k[x]/(x^p). mathlib:MonoidAlgebra and mathlib:Module.Flat are in the library and route 1 builds on them.

items.name: Bounded constructible and ind-constructible derived categories on locally finite type stacks
items.statement: Let Y be a locally finite type stack and Λ a coefficient ring in which the characteristic of Y is invertible. D^b_c(Y;Λ) is the category of complexes of étale Λ-sheaves whose restriction to every quasi-compact open substack U ⊂ Y lies in the bounded constructible derived category D^b_c(U;Λ). D(Y;Λ) is the cocomplete derived category of ind-constructible étale Λ-sheaves, and D^b(Y;Λ) ⊂ D(Y;Λ) is its full subcategory of bounded objects. For a stratification S = {Y_λ} of Y, D^b_S(Y;Λ) ⊂ D^b(Y;Λ) is the full subcategory of complexes constructible with respect to S. If a (pro-)algebraic group Σ acts on Y, D^b_{c,Σ}(Y;Λ) = D^b_c(Y;Λ)^{BΣ} and D^b_Σ(Y;Λ) = D^b(Y;Λ)^{BΣ} are the Σ-equivariant versions. For Λ = k the coefficient ring is omitted from the notation, and f_!, f_*, f^!, f^* always denote derived functors.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, §1.5 (Notation), p. 7
items.note: Added by the review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24): Definitions 3.1 and 3.3 (items 17 and 19) are Verdier quotients of D^b_c(Y;Λ[σ]) and D^b(Y;Λ[σ]) for locally finite type Y (moduli of shtukas), and §4 uses the equivariant versions on Gr.
