These categories are presupposed but no item defines them. EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves:EDC.0 imports only the bounded constructible category, and the atlas has no stage matching 'ind-constructible' or equivariant derived categories.

items.name: The base change homomorphism preserves semisimplicity
items.statement: Let F be a global field or a local field, H a connected reductive group over F, E/F a cyclic extension of degree p, and G = Res_{E/F}(H_E). Let Γ = Gal(F^s/F), or the Weil group of F when F is local, and let φ_BC: ^LH^alg → ^LG^alg be as in Definition 2.8. If ρ: Γ → ^LH^alg(k) is semisimple, then φ_BC ∘ ρ: Γ → ^LG^alg(k) is semisimple. Consequently, for every character ν of Exc(Γ,^LH^alg), the parameter ρ_{ν∘φ_BC^*} is φ_BC ∘ ρ_ν itself, not merely its semisimplification.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Supplement to Lemma 2.7 (p. 12) and Definition 2.8 (p. 13), added by this review
items.note: Added by the review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24): The proofs yield equalities of excursion characters, which by Proposition 2.4 identify ρ_Π with the semisimplification (φ_BC∘ρ_π)^{ss}. The theorems assert ρ_Π ≅ φ_BC∘ρ_π, and Theorem 1.6 asserts that φ_BC∘ρ is automorphic, hence semisimple. That needs φ_BC to preserve semisimplicity, which the paper never states, and which fails for a general admissible φ in characteristic p (new issue: Lemma 2.7). Proof sketch. ρ(Γ_E) is normal in ρ(Γ), so it is completely reducible (Bate–Martin–Röhrle 2005, Theorem 3.10). Suppose ψ := φ_BC∘ρ lies in an R-parabolic P_λ of ^LG, where λ = (λ_s)_{s∈Hom_F(E,F^s)}. Then ρ(Γ_E) ⊂ P_{λ_{s_0}}, so it lies in a Levi L_0 of P_{λ_{s_0}}. Transport L_0 to s by ρ(γ) for any γ with γs_0 = s; the result does not depend on γ because ρ(Γ_E) ⊂ L_0. This gives a Levi of P_λ containing ψ(Γ): Shapiro's lemma in parabolic form.

items.name: Admissible σ-actions, the quotient Y/σ and the σ-fixed subscheme
items.statement: Let Y be a separated scheme locally of finite type over a field of characteristic ≠ p with an action of ⟨σ⟩ ≅ Z/pZ. The action is admissible (SGA 1, Exposé V, Définition 1.7) if every orbit lies in an affine open subscheme (equivalently in a σ-stable affine open). This holds if Y is a union of σ-stable quasi-projective opens (Riche–Williamson, Remark 2.2). For an admissible action the quotient q: Y → Y/σ exists as a scheme, glued from Spec(A^σ) over σ-stable affine opens Spec A. It is finite and surjective, Y/σ is separated and locally of finite type, geometric fibres of q are σ-orbits, and its formation commutes with restriction to σ-stable opens. The fixed subscheme Y^σ ⊂ Y is the equaliser of id and σ, a closed subscheme on which σ acts trivially, and q is totally ramified along it: q^{-1}(q(ȳ)) = {ȳ} for ȳ ∈ Y^σ. The action on U := Y ∖ Y^σ is free (trivial stabilisers of geometric points) and again admissible, and for a free action every geometric fibre of q is a σ-torsor.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, §3.2, p. 14; Lemma 3.6 and Lemma 3.7, p. 15
items.note: Added by the review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24): The σ-fixed subscheme Y^σ, admissibility, the scheme quotient Y/σ and free actions are used by every statement of §§3.2–3.4 (Psm = T^*i^*, Lemmas 3.6–3.8, Corollary 3.11 via Y/σ, and Proposition 3.12 via freeness and admissibility of U = Y∖Y^σ). No item defines them. tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ModularCurves#0c-finite-quotients-and-torsors plans affine quotients by finite groups, and glued quotients only for free actions with an invariant affine cover; this item extends that to admissible non-free actions and cites it.

items.name: σ-equivariant derived categories and the trivial-action identification
items.statement: For Y as in §3.2 with σ-action, let Sh_σ(Y;Λ) be the abelian category of σ-equivariant étale sheaves of Λ-modules (for Λ = W(k), Λ-adic sheaves), D^b_σ(Y;Λ) its bounded derived category, and D^b_{c,σ}(Y;Λ) ⊂ D^b_σ(Y;Λ) the full subcategory of objects whose underlying complex is constructible. For σ-equivariant morphisms, f^*, Rf_*, Rf_!, f^!, ⊗ and RHom lift to these categories, compatibly with forgetting the equivariance. If σ acts trivially on Z, a σ-equivariant sheaf is the same as a sheaf of Λ[σ]-modules, giving equivalences D^b_σ(Z;Λ) ≅ D^b(Z;Λ[σ]) and D^b_{c,σ}(Z;Λ) ≅ D^b_c(Z;Λ[σ]) (3.2). This applies in particular to Z = Y^σ, and also to Y/σ and S in Lemma 3.6 and Corollary 3.11.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, §3.2, equation (3.2), p. 15
items.note: Added by the review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24): D^b_σ(Y;Λ), its constructible subcategory and the identification (3.2) for the trivial action are the domain of Psm and of Lemmas 3.8 and Proposition 3.12. As the new issue on Lemmas 3.6, 3.7 and Corollary 3.11 shows, the distinction between D^b_σ(Y;Λ) and D^b(Y;Λ[σ]) is exactly where the text slips. No item defines them, and the atlas plans no equivariant derived category of étale sheaves for a finite group action. EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E5:presentability plans only abstract ∞-categorical group actions and homotopy fixed points.

items.name: Tor-amplitude over Λ[σ]: flat resolutions, stalkwise criterion and the Artinian case
items.statement: (i) For a commutative ring A and K ∈ D(A), K has tor-amplitude in [a,b] if and only if K is represented by a complex of flat A-modules concentrated in degrees [a,b] (Stacks 08G1). (ii) For K ∈ D(Y_ét;A), K has tor-amplitude in [a,b] if and only if every stalk at a geometric point does (Stacks 0DJJ). (iii) Over a commutative Artinian local ring such as k[σ], a complex of finite tor-amplitude has finite projective dimension (Stacks 0A5M), a module of finite projective dimension is projective (finitistic dimension zero), and hence a complex with cohomology in [a,b] and finite tor-amplitude has tor-amplitude in [a,b]. (iv) For Noetherian A (for example Λ[σ]), a pseudo-coherent complex of finite tor-amplitude is perfect, so Perf(Y;Λ[σ]) = D^b_c(Y;Λ[σ]) ∩ Flat^b(Y;Λ[σ]), and Flat^b is a thick triangulated subcategory. Consequently Perf(Y;T_Λ) → Shv(Y;T_Λ) is conservative.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, proof of Lemma 3.2, pp. 13–14, and the paragraph after Definition 3.3 (equation (3.1)), p. 14
items.note: Added by the review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24): Lemma 3.2, the conservativity of Perf(Y;T_Λ) → Shv(Y;T_Λ), and Lemmas 3.7 and 3.9 all rest on the theory of tor-amplitude for complexes of modules and of sheaves, quoted from Stacks 08G1, 0DJJ, 0A5M and 051E. DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:P7 plans Tor-amplitude only for bounded complexes of finite projective modules over complete Noetherian local rings. The stalkwise criterion on the étale site, the non-finite flat modules of Definition 3.1, and the finitistic-dimension step are not planned. Item 107 covers only flat = free.

items.name: Separate finite tor-amplitude preservation for Rf_! and Rj_*
items.statement: Let f:X→Y be separated of finite type between schemes of finite type over a field of characteristic ℓ≠p, with geometric fibres of dimension ≤d. Use étale p-primary torsion coefficients A=Λ[C_p] with Λ=k or Λ=W(k)/p^m, m≥1, and bounded complexes of sheaves of A-modules. For an input of tor-amplitude [a,b], the compactly supported pushforward Rf_! has tor-amplitude in [a,b+2d], by fibrewise compact-support cohomological dimension and the projection formula. For a quasi-compact open immersion j:U↪Y of such schemes, Rj_* preserves finite tor-amplitude, with its finite cohomological-dimension bound depending on the ambient local geometry; there is no bound by twice j's relative dimension and no claim of t-exactness. In the constructible setting where the usual finiteness hypotheses apply these operations preserve perfect-stalk complexes. In particular they supply the finite-Tor inputs needed for Flat^b. For Λ=W(k), apply the torsion statements to a compatible adic system with a uniform bound and justify its completed projection-formula/limit passage; it is not an automatic consequence of the torsion statement alone.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, proofs of Lemma 3.7 and Lemma 3.9, p. 16
items.note: Route 1 keeps ownership of the missing group-ring finite-Tor preservation theorem and imports the relevant Rf_! operations/cohomological-dimension foundations from EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves:EDC.0. Feng p.16 invokes preservation of finiteness for Rj_*, not a relative-dimension numerical estimate. The false estimate was introduced by review-added rev-6; neither Feng nor Stacks 0F10 states it. The k-coefficient case is the present negative test. Stacks 0F10 is a finite cohomological-dimension input for higher direct images, and 03PK supplies the Kummer calculation; neither is quoted as proving tor preservation on its own.

beforeRedteamFix.name: Rf_! and Rj_* preserve finite tor-amplitude
beforeRedteamFix.statement: Let f: X → Y be a separated morphism of finite type between schemes of finite type over a field of characteristic ≠ p, j a quasi-compact open immersion of such schemes, and A = Λ[σ]. Then Rf_!, and Rj_*, have finite cohomological dimension (Stacks 0F10). They carry objects of D^b(X;A) of tor-amplitude in [a,b] to objects of tor-amplitude in [a, b+c], with c bounded by twice the relative dimension, and they carry Perf to Perf in the constructible case (SGA 4, Exposé XVII, Théorèmes 5.2.10 and 5.2.11, via the projection formula). In particular they preserve locally finite tor-amplitude, hence Flat^b.
beforeRedteamFix.note: Added by the review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24): The only non-formal input to Lemmas 3.7 and 3.9 is the quoted fact that proper pushforward and pushforward along quasi-compact open immersions preserve finite tor-amplitude and perfectness: Stacks 0F10 (finite cohomological dimension for finite type morphisms over a field) combined with SGA 4, Exposé XVII, Théorèmes 5.2.10 and 5.2.11. EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves:EDC.0 imports the finite cohomological-dimension bounds for Rf_!, but no stage plans the tor-amplitude statement.

unitTests.name: Feng.rev6.puncturedLine
unitTests.statement: Take j:G_m→A¹ over Fbar_7 and A=Fbar_3[C_3]. The constant free A-sheaf has tor-amplitude [0,0]. On the punctured strict henselian trait at 0, z³=t is a nontrivial étale Kummer torsor, since v(t)=1 is not divisible by 3. Thus (R¹j_*A)_0≠0, despite relative dimension zero. Rj_*A does not have tor-amplitude [0,0]; only finite amplitude is asserted.

unitTests.name: Feng.rev6.compactSupport
unitTests.statement: For f:A¹→Spec(Fbar_7), the constant free k[C_3]-sheaf has compactly supported cohomology k[C_3](-1) in degree 2. This reaches the Rf_! bound [0,2] for d=1. An open immersion j_! is exact, whereas Rj_* may have a degree-one stalk: keep the functors distinct.

items.name: Compactly supported pushforward for locally finite type morphisms of bounded dimension
items.statement: Let f: Y → S be a separated morphism, locally of finite type, between schemes locally of finite type over a field of characteristic ≠ p, with Y of bounded dimension, and A = Λ[σ]. Write Y as the filtered union of its finite-type open subschemes j_α: Y_α ↪ Y, and for F ∈ D^b(Y;A) set Rf_!F := colim_α R(f∘j_α)_!(F|_{Y_α}). This is well defined, lies in D^b(S;A) (uniform cohomological-dimension bound), agrees with the usual Rf_! when f is of finite type, and is compatible with composition, arbitrary base change and the projection formula. It lifts to D^b_σ for σ-equivariant f, and it preserves Flat^b (Lemma 3.9), via the filtered-colimit stability of flatness with a uniform bound on tor-amplitude.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, proof of Lemma 3.9, p. 16; used in §3.3.2 and Proposition 3.12, p. 17, and §3.4.3, p. 18
items.note: Added by the review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24): The whole point of §3 is to allow locally finite type schemes. The paper takes Rf_! for a separated locally finite type morphism of bounded dimension to be the filtered colimit over finite-type opens, and uses its boundedness, proper base change (the reduction to S = S^σ in Proposition 3.12) and the projection formula. EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves:EDC.0 plans Rf_! for compactifiable (finite type) morphisms. GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands:GS.3 plans only the colimit over shtuka truncations. The general construction is planned nowhere.

items.name: Parity sheaves on the affine Grassmannian: existence, equivariance and perversity
items.statement: Let F be a separably closed field of characteristic ≠ p, G a reductive group over F and Gr_G its affine Grassmannian with the stratification by L^+G-orbits, and Λ ∈ {k, O}. (a) The stratification is JMW (Gr_G is a partial affine flag variety of Kac–Moody type) [JMW14, §4.1]. (b) For every orbit Gr^λ_G and every Λ-free local system L on it the parity sheaf E(λ,L) exists, and it admits an L^+G-equivariant structure if p is not a torsion prime for G [JMW16, Theorem 1.4]. (c) If p is good for Ĝ, every normalized parity sheaf on Gr_G (with k- or O-coefficients) is perverse [MR18, Corollary 1.6].
items.note: Added by the review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24): Existence, equivariance and perversity of parity sheaves on Gr_G are used throughout (e.g. 'F is essentially surjective as all parity sheaves exist' in §A.3, perversity of normalized parity sheaves in §4.6.3); item 39 has them only in its note.

items.name: The S-constructible integral Tate category
items.statement: For a stratification S of Y, Perf_S(Y;T_O) ⊂ Perf(Y;T_O) is the full subcategory generated by the images of objects of D^b_S(Y;O[σ]). With Perf_S(Y;O[σ]) ⊂ Perf(Y;O[σ]) the full thick subcategory of S-constructible objects, the natural functor D^b_S(Y;O[σ])/Perf_S(Y;O[σ]) → Perf_S(Y;T_O) is an equivalence [LL21, Corollary 4.5.2]. When S is the orbit stratification of a group K one writes Perf_{(K)}(Y;T_O), and similarly Parity_{(K)}.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, §4.2, p. 20
items.note: Added by the review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24): Items 35–38 use Perf_S(Y;T_O) and Parity_S(Y;T_O) but no item defines the S-constructible Tate category or records the Verdier-quotient description [LL21, Corollary 4.5.2].

items.name: Morphisms between inflated objects of the integral Tate category
items.statement: (a) Ext^*_{Perf(T_O)}(T^*O, T^*O) ≅ ⊕_{i∈Z} k[2i]: the Tate cohomology of Z/pZ with coefficients O is k in even degrees and 0 in odd degrees. (b) For F, G ∈ D^b_S(Y;O), Hom_{Perf(Y;T_O)}(T^*ε^*F, T^*ε^*G) ≅ ⊕_{i∈Z} Hom_{D^b_S(Y;k)}(FF, FG[2i]), where F = k ⊗^L_O (−) [LL21, Proposition 4.6.1]. (c) Parity_S(Y;T_O) is a Krull–Remak–Schmidt category [LL21, Proposition 5.5.2].
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, (4.1), p. 20; (4.2) and the proof of Proposition 4.5, p. 22
items.note: Added by the review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24): The Hom formula (4.2) is what defines the lifting functor L on morphisms (item 38) and drives Propositions 4.5 and Lemma A.2; it is only quoted in the note of item 37.

items.name: Modular reduction of parity sheaves
items.statement: Let Y carry a JMW stratification S and F = k ⊗^L_O (−): D^b_S(Y;O) → D^b_S(Y;k). (1) E ∈ D^b_S(Y;O) is a parity sheaf if and only if F(E) is a parity sheaf. (2) If E(λ,L) exists then E(λ,FL) exists and FE(λ,L) ≅ E(λ,FL). (3) For parity complexes E, E', Hom_{D^b_S(Y;O)}(E,E') is a free O-module and k ⊗_O Hom_{D^b_S(Y;O)}(E,E') → Hom_{D^b_S(Y;k)}(FE,FE') is an isomorphism [JMW14, §2.5].
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Remark 4.6, p. 21
items.note: Added by the review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24): Modular reduction of parity complexes is used in Proposition 4.5, (4.3), Lemma 4.16 and Lemma 4.24, and no item states it.

items.name: Tilting modules for the dual group and their tensor products
items.statement: Tilt_k(Ĝ) ⊂ Rep_k(Ĝ) is the full subcategory of finite-dimensional representations having both a filtration with standard (Weyl) subquotients and a filtration with costandard subquotients. It is closed under direct sums, direct summands and tensor products (Donkin, Mathieu, Wang; see the discussion around [JMW16, Theorem 1.2]). In particular, for G = H^p, restriction along the diagonal Ĥ → Ĥ^p = Ĝ maps Tilt_k(Ĝ) into Tilt_k(Ĥ).
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, §4.5, p. 23; footnote 11, p. 27
items.note: Added by the review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24): Tilting modules, and the theorem that tensor products of tilting modules are tilting, are needed for Theorem 4.8 and for Res_BC to be defined on Tilt_k (Theorem 4.20). Not planned: LanglandsParameterStacks:LP3 plans Weyl and dual Weyl modules, good filtrations and their stability under tensor products (under FS VIII.5 hypotheses), from which the tilting statement follows by duality, but tilting modules themselves are planned nowhere.

items.name: Psm ∘ Nm lands in normalized Tate-parity sheaves
items.statement: Assume H is a reductive group over a separably closed field F of characteristic ≠ p, G = H^p with σ acting by cyclic rotation of the factors (the ith factor to the (i+1)st mod p), p is odd and good for Ĝ (equivalently for Ĥ), k is an algebraic closure of F_p and O = W(k). (a) For λ = (λ_1,…,λ_p) ∈ X_*(G)^+ = (X_*(H)^+)^p, Gr^λ_G ∩ Gr_H = Gr^{λ_1}_H if λ_1 = … = λ_p and is empty otherwise. (b) dim Gr^λ_G = ⟨2ρ_G, λ⟩ [Zhu17, Proposition 2.1.5], so dim Gr^{(λ_1,…,λ_1)}_G = p⟨2ρ_H, λ_1⟩ ≡ dim Gr^{λ_1}_H mod 2, and the pariversity induced on Gr_H by the dimension pariversity of Gr_G is the dimension pariversity. (c) For F ∈ Parity^0_{L^+G}(Gr_G;O), F is perverse, Nm(F) is a normalized parity complex in Parity^0_{L^+G⋊σ}(Gr_G;O) [JMW16, Theorem 1.5], its σ-equivariant structure satisfies condition (*) of Proposition 4.15 (Lemma 4.14), and Psm(Nm(F)) ∈ Parity^0_{(L^+H)}(Gr_H;T_O).
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, §4.6.3, p. 26
items.note: Added by the review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24): This unnumbered argument is what makes Psm∘Nm land in normalized Tate-parity sheaves, which Definition 4.18 needs; it is not in any item.

items.name: Psm ∘ Nm is additive and Frobenius-semilinear on morphisms
items.statement: Assume H is a reductive group over a separably closed field F of characteristic ≠ p, G = H^p with σ acting by cyclic rotation of the factors (the ith factor to the (i+1)st mod p), p is odd and good for Ĝ (equivalently for Ĥ), k is an algebraic closure of F_p and O = W(k). For F, F' ∈ Parity^0_{L^+G}(Gr_G;O), morphisms f, g: F → F' and a ∈ O, one has Psm(Nm(f+g)) = Psm(Nm f) + Psm(Nm g) and Psm(Nm(a·f)) = a^p · Psm(Nm f) in Perf_{(L^+H)}(Gr_H;T_O). Proof: the 2^p − 2 mixed terms of Nm(f+g) are permuted freely by σ (p is prime), and the sum over an orbit is a transfer Σ_j σ^j t σ^{−j} of a non-equivariant map t, which factors through an induced object Ind Res(−) whose restriction to Gr_H has stalks free over O[σ], hence vanishes in the Tate category. Consequently L ∘ Psm ∘ Nm kills p·Hom and factors uniquely through F: Parity^0_{L^+G}(Gr_G;O) → Parity^0_{L^+G}(Gr_G;k) as a Frob-semilinear functor.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, §4.6.3, p. 26; Definition 4.18, p. 27 (repair by this review)
items.note: Added by the review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24): Needed to make Definition 4.18 well defined; the paper asserts it without proof (issue below). This proposed item is this review's repair, not a statement of the paper.

items.name: Equivariantization of a category with a group action
items.statement: For a group Γ acting on a category C (by autoequivalences with coherent compositions), the equivariantization C^{BΓ} is the category of pairs (X, (u_γ: γ^*X ≅ X)_{γ∈Γ}) satisfying the cocycle condition, with Γ-compatible morphisms; a Γ-equivariant functor F: C → D induces F^{BΓ}: C^{BΓ} → D^{BΓ} [DGNO10]. For continuous actions of profinite groups such as Aut(F/F_0) one requires continuity. The paper defines Parity^0_{L^+G}(Gr_{G,F_0};k) := Parity^0_{L^+G}(Gr_{G,F};k)^{BAut(F/F_0)}, and for derived categories of sheaves it uses the equivariant derived category rather than the equivariantization of the derived category.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, §4.6.4, p. 28
items.note: Added by the review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24): Equivariantization [DGNO10] defines Parity^0(Gr_{G,F_0};k) and Tilt_k(^LG^geom) ≅ Tilt_k(Ĝ)^{Aut(F/F_0),geom}, on which Corollary 4.23 and the use of BC in §5 rest; item 50 (as corrected) states the result but no item defines the construction.

items.name: The constant term functor commutes with the Smith operation
items.statement: With κ, T = T_H^p, T_H as in §A.4 (so Gr_T^σ = Gr_{T_H}), the square Psm ∘ CT_G ≅ CT_H ∘ Psm of functors D^b_{c,L^+G⋊σ}(Gr_G;Λ) → Perf_{(L^+T_H)}(Gr_{T_H};T_Λ) commutes (Λ ∈ {O, k}), because Psm commutes with i_ν^* and Rp_{ν!} (§A.1) and S_ν ∩ Gr_H is the semi-infinite orbit of H for ν = (ν_1,…,ν_1) and is empty otherwise. The same holds for CT_G[deg_G] and CT_H[deg_H], since deg_G(ν_1,…,ν_1) = p·deg_H(ν_1) ≡ deg_H(ν_1) mod 2 and the shift by 2 is isomorphic to the identity on the Tate category.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, (A.2), p. 58
items.note: Added by the review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24): The compatibility of CT with Psm is used in Lemma A.2 (middle square of (A.4)) and in §A.6, and is not covered: item 27 gives only the general compatibility of Psm with the six operations.

items.name: Tilting modules are determined by their characters
items.statement: Let Ĥ be a split reductive group over k with maximal torus T̂_H. Restriction Rep_k(Ĥ) → Rep_k(T̂_H) is faithful, and two tilting modules for Ĥ are isomorphic if and only if their restrictions to T̂_H are isomorphic (equivalently, have the same character) [Don93, p. 46].
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, §A.4, p. 60
items.note: Added by the review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24): This input carries the reduction of Theorem 4.20 to a torus.

items.name: The base change functor for a torus
items.statement: Let H be a torus over a separably closed field of characteristic ≠ p (reduce to H = G_m by products) and G = H^p. The components of Gr_G are indexed by (n_1,…,n_p) ∈ X_*(H)^p; for F the constant sheaf on Gr_G^{(n_1,…,n_p)}, Nm(F) is the constant sheaf on Gr_G^{(n,…,n)} with n = n_1+…+n_p, and BC^(p)(F) is the constant sheaf k on Gr_H^n, which corresponds under Satake to Res_BC(V_{n_1} ⊠ … ⊠ V_{n_p}) = V_n. BC^(p) sends multiplication by λ to multiplication by λ^p, so BC sends it to multiplication by λ; hence BC ≅ Res_BC under Satake as functors (the categories being semisimple).
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, §A.5, p. 60
items.note: Added by the review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24): The torus case of Theorem 4.20 is proved separately and is the base of the reduction; no item states it.

items.name: Semi-infinite orbits through extreme weights
items.statement: Let H be reductive over a separably closed field, T_H ⊂ H a maximal torus, κ regular, S_ν the semi-infinite orbits for ν ∈ X_*(T_H) and w_0 the longest Weyl element. For λ dominant, S_{w_0(λ)} ∩ Gr^λ_H = {t^{w_0(λ)}} [BR18, Theorem 5.2]; and S_ν meets Gr^μ_H only if ν lies in the convex hull of W·μ (so S_{w_0(λ)} meets Gr^μ_H only if λ ≤ μ).
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, proof of Lemma A.3, §A.6, p. 61
items.note: Added by the review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24): Needed for Lemma A.3 (item 98). GeometricSatakeAndFusion:GS1 plans semi-infinite orbits and their intersections with Schubert strata for the Fargues–Scholze Grassmannian, and Mirković–Vilonen geometry underlies GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands:GS.1, but neither stage names this statement for the equal-characteristic Gr_H; if GS.1's blueprint includes it, cite GS.1 instead.

items.name: The mod p excursion action of Lafforgue and Xue on compactly supported automorphic functions
items.statement: Let G be a smooth generically reductive group scheme over X, D ⊂ X a closed finite subscheme, and H_G the Hecke algebra acting on Sht_{G,D,I} (the tensor product of the local Hecke algebras with k-coefficients at the level fixed by D). For a finite set I and j ∈ Z let H^j_I: Rep_k((^LG^alg)^I) → Mod_{H_G}(Γ^I), V ↦ H^j_c(Sht_{G,D,I}|_{η̄^I};Sat(V)). The a priori π_1(η^I,η̄^I)-action extends to FWeil(η^I,η̄^I). The extension uses the partial Frobenius isomorphisms Frob^*_{{i}}H^j_I(V) ≅ H^j_I(V), induced by the partial Frobenius maps of the iterated stacks Sht^{({1},…,{n})}_{G,D,I} together with Rν_!Sat^{(I_1,…,I_r)}(V) ≅ Sat(V) and F^*_{I_1}Sat^{(I_1,I_2,…,I_r)}(V) ≅ Sat^{(I_2,…,I_r,I_1)}(V). By Drinfeld's lemma in Xue's form [Xue, Lemma 7.4.2] the FWeil-action factors through Γ^I = Weil(F^s/F)^I. Construct this family first from the coefficient-linear geometric Satake functors, with their Galois transport. Verify the unit and forgotten-leg compatibility and all six relations by corrected item 56, rather than infer them solely from fusion and composition. This gives an action of Exc(Γ,^LG) on H^0_{{0}}(1) ≅ H_∅(1) = C_c^∞(Bun_{G,D}(F_ℓ);k) = ⊕_{α∈ker¹(F,G)} C_c^∞(G_α(F)\G_α(A_F)/∏_v K_v;k), where K_v = G(O_v) for v ∉ D and K_v = ker(G(O_v) → G(O_D)) for v ∈ D. The action commutes with H_G and preserves the α-decomposition. On C_cusp^∞ it is Lafforgue's action [Laf18, §13]; on all of C_c^∞ it is Xue's extension ([Xuea, §7] for split G, [Xueb, §6] in general). Its elements are the excursion operators.
items.note: Added by the review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24): Theorem 5.13 and Definition 5.5 act on Lafforgue–Xue's k-coefficient excursion action on C_c^∞(Bun_{G,D}(F_ℓ);k), and no item states it. GS.3–GS.5 plan the characteristic-zero ℓ-adic action on the Hecke-finite (cuspidal) sector only.

beforeRedteamFix.statement: Let G be a smooth generically reductive group scheme over X, D ⊂ X a closed finite subscheme, and H_G the Hecke algebra acting on Sht_{G,D,I} (the tensor product of the local Hecke algebras with k-coefficients at the level fixed by D). For a finite set I and j ∈ Z let H^j_I: Rep_k((^LG^alg)^I) → Mod_{H_G}(Γ^I), V ↦ H^j_c(Sht_{G,D,I}|_{η̄^I};Sat(V)). The a priori π_1(η^I,η̄^I)-action extends to FWeil(η^I,η̄^I). The extension uses the partial Frobenius isomorphisms Frob^*_{{i}}H^j_I(V) ≅ H^j_I(V), induced by the partial Frobenius maps of the iterated stacks Sht^{({1},…,{n})}_{G,D,I} together with Rν_!Sat^{(I_1,…,I_r)}(V) ≅ Sat(V) and F^*_{I_1}Sat^{(I_1,I_2,…,I_r)}(V) ≅ Sat^{(I_2,…,I_r,I_1)}(V). By Drinfeld's lemma in Xue's form [Xue, Lemma 7.4.2] the FWeil-action factors through Γ^I = Weil(F^s/F)^I. The family (H^j_I)_I is admissible (Definition 5.1), since Sat is compatible with fusion and composition, so Construction 5.2 gives an action of Exc(Γ,^LG) on H^0_{{0}}(1) ≅ H_∅(1) = C_c^∞(Bun_{G,D}(F_ℓ);k) = ⊕_{α∈ker¹(F,G)} C_c^∞(G_α(F)\G_α(A_F)/∏_v K_v;k), where K_v = G(O_v) for v ∉ D and K_v = ker(G(O_v) → G(O_D)) for v ∈ D. The action commutes with H_G and preserves the α-decomposition. On C_cusp^∞ it is Lafforgue's action [Laf18, §13]; on all of C_c^∞ it is Xue's extension ([Xuea, §7] for split G, [Xueb, §6] in general). Its elements are the excursion operators.

items.name: The partial Frobenius Weil group FWeil(η^I, η̄^I)
items.statement: Let F^I be the function field of X^I (η^I = Spec F^I), F̄^I an algebraic closure (η̄^I = Spec F̄^I), (F^I)^perf the perfect closure, and Frob_{{i}} the partial Frobenius of (F^I)^perf induced by Frob_ℓ on the i-th factor. FWeil(η^I,η̄^I) := {γ ∈ Aut_{F̄_ℓ}(F̄^I) : ∃(n_i)_{i∈I} ∈ Z^I with γ|_{(F^I)^perf} = ∏_{i∈I}(Frob_{{i}})^{n_i}} (the paper prints Aut_{F̄_q}; see new issue). With π_1^geom(η^I,η̄^I) := ker(π_1(η^I,η̄^I) →deg Ẑ) there is an exact sequence 0 → π_1^geom(η^I,η̄^I) → FWeil(η^I,η̄^I) → Z^I → 0, and a specialisation η̄^I ⇝ Δ(η̄^{{1}}) induces a surjection FWeil(η^I,η̄^I) ↠ Weil(η,η̄)^I [Laf18, Remarque 8.18].
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, §5.2.3, p. 34
items.note: Added by the review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24): Proposition 5.6, Lemma B.5 and items 58, 59 and 104 use FWeil, which no item defines. Its role is exactly GS.4's partial-Frobenius/Drinfeld-lemma set-up.

items.name: Decomposition of Bun_{G,D}(F_ℓ) and Sht_{G,D,I} by ker¹(F,G)
items.statement: Let ker¹(F,G) := ker(H^1(F,G) → ∏_v H^1(F_v,G)). Then Bun_{G,D}(F_ℓ) = ⊔_{α∈ker¹(F,G)} G_α(F)\G_α(A_F)/∏_v K_v, with G_α the pure inner form attached to α, K_v = G(O_v) for v ∉ D and K_v = ker(G(O_v) → G(O_D)) for v ∈ D [Laf18, Remarque 12.2]. More generally Sht_{G,D,I} = ⊔_{α∈ker¹(F,G)}(Sht_{G,D,I})_α according to the isomorphism class of the generic fibre of E. In the base change setup the diagonal φ: H → G induces φ_*: ker¹(F,H) → ker¹(F,G), compatible with Bun_{H,D}(F_ℓ) → Bun_{G,D}(F_ℓ).
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, (5.6), Example 5.4, p. 35; (5.19) and the following paragraph, §5.6, p. 42
items.note: Added by the review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24): Theorem 5.13 is stated componentwise in α ∈ ker¹(F,G) and matches components by φ_*. GS.0 plans the adelic description of rational points in the torsor classes, which is (5.6).

items.name: The Exc(Γ,^LG)^σ-action on Tate cohomology of shtukas
items.statement: In the base change setup σ acts on Exc(Γ,^LG^alg) by transport of structure: σ·S_{I,V,x,ξ,(γ_i)} = S_{I,σ(V),σ(x),σ(ξ),(γ_i)}. For a k[σ]-algebra A and an A-module M with compatible σ-actions, T^*(M) is a module over T^0(A) = A^σ/(N·A). Hence T^*(Sht_{G,D,∅};1) is an Exc(Γ,^LG)^σ-module. If V ∈ Rep_k((^LG)^I)^{Bσ} and x, ξ are σ-equivariant, S_{I,V,x,ξ,(γ_i)} ∈ Exc(Γ,^LG)^σ acts by the composite T^*(Sht_{G,D,∅};1) →[x] T^*(Sht_{G,D,I};V) →[(γ_i)_{i∈I}] T^*(Sht_{G,D,I};V) →[ξ] T^*(Sht_{G,D,∅};1). The middle arrow is defined by Proposition 5.6, and the outer identifications use Remark 5.3. (The paper prints Sht_{G,D,∅} in the two middle terms; see new issue.)
items.note: Added by the review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24): Theorem 5.11 is a statement about the Exc(Γ,^LG)^σ-action on T^j(Sht_{G,D+∞x_0,∅};1), which this subsection defines; no item covers it. Creation and annihilation in the excursion instance are geometric Rep_k(Ĝ^I) morphisms evaluated before Galois descent; the Γ-action is supplied separately as in corrected item 56. Full-L-group invariance of x or ξ is not assumed (E59–E60).

beforeRedteamFix.note: Added by the review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24): Theorem 5.11 is a statement about the Exc(Γ,^LG)^σ-action on T^j(Sht_{G,D+∞x_0,∅};1), which this subsection defines; no item covers it.

items.name: Harder–Narasimhan truncations of shtukas and their representability at deep level
items.statement: Sht_{G,D,I} is exhausted by the quasi-compact open substacks Sht^{≤μ}_{G,D,I} := Sht_{G,D,I} ×_{Bun_G} Bun_G^{≤μ}, μ running over dominant coweights, with the HN truncation as in [Laf18, (1.3)] ([Var04, Proposition 2.16], stated for split G and valid for all G by the same argument). For fixed μ, Sht^{≤μ}_{G,D,I} is the quotient of a quasi-projective scheme by a finite group. For any closed point x_0 ∈ X the scheme can be taken to be Sht^{≤μ}_{G,D+nx_0,I} for n large relative to μ, which is then representable by a quasi-projective scheme, the group being the automorphisms of the level structure. The same holds for the iterated stacks Sht^{(I_1,…,I_r)}_{G,D,I}.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, §5.4.1, pp. 36–37
items.note: Added by the review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24): Lemma 5.7, Definition 5.8, Remark 5.9 and §B.2 all rest on these facts, which no item states. GS.2 plans HN truncations with their representability and finite-type statements.

items.name: HN truncation is compatible with the diagonal map H → G
items.statement: In the base change setup, let μ be a coweight of H and μ̃ the induced coweight of G. Then Bun_H^{≤μ} = Bun_H ×_{Bun_G} Bun_G^{≤μ̃}, and hence Sht^{(I_1,…,I_r),≤μ}_{H,D,I} = Sht^{(I_1,…,I_r)}_{H,D,I} ×_{Sht^{(I_1,…,I_r)}_{G,D,I}} Sht^{(I_1,…,I_r),≤μ̃}_{G,D,I} (5.11). For any cofinal family of HN polygons μ for H, the induced polygons μ̃ are cofinal for G.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, §5.4.1, (5.11), p. 37; the paragraph after Definition 5.10, p. 38
items.note: Added by the review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24): This is the compatibility of HN truncation with the diagonal H → G. Lemma 5.7 uses it to land in Sht^{≤μ}_H, and the G-versions of Definitions 5.8 and 5.10 use it through cofinality. The paper asserts it without proof, and nothing plans it.

items.name: The norm and norm-element operations on representations of (^LG)^I
items.statement: Nm: Rep_k((^LG)^I) → Rep_k((^LG)^I)^{Bσ} sends V to V ⊗_k ^σV ⊗_k … ⊗_k ^{σ^{p−1}}V. Its σ-equivariant structure ^σNm(V) = ^σV ⊗ … ⊗ ^{σ^{p−1}}V ⊗ V ≅ Nm(V) is given by the commutativity constraint, and on morphisms Nm(h) := h ⊗ ^σh ⊗ … ⊗ ^{σ^{p−1}}h. It corresponds under Geometric Satake to Definition 4.12. Nm is neither additive nor k-linear. Its linearisation Nm^{(p^{-1})} := Nm ∘ Frob_p^{-1}, where Frob_p^{-1} is the identity on objects and (−)⊗_{k,Frob_p^{-1}}k on morphisms (§4.6.3), is k-linear but not additive. N·V := V ⊕ ^σV ⊕ … ⊕ ^{σ^{p−1}}V has the σ-equivariant structure given by the commutativity constraint for direct sums, and N·h := h ⊕ ^σh ⊕ … ⊕ ^{σ^{p−1}}h. Finally Δ_p: 1 → 1^{⊕p} is the diagonal map and ∇_p: 1^{⊕p} → 1 the sum map.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, §5.5, p. 38
items.note: Added by the review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24): Theorem 5.11, Proposition 5.12, Lemma 5.16 and Definition 5.19 are stated with these operations on representations. Item 42 covers only the Satake-category norm (Definition 4.12), and item 1 only the norm of an element.

items.name: Lafforgue's operators S_{W,v} on cohomology of shtukas
items.statement: For W ∈ Rep_k(Ĝ) and a closed point v ∈ X°∖D, S_{W,v} is the endomorphism of the cohomology sheaves Rπ_{I!}(Sht_{G,D,I};Sat(V)) (and, by functoriality of the construction, of their Tate cohomology sheaves) defined in [Laf18, §6]. It creates a pair of legs carrying W and its dual at v, applies the partial Frobenius at v, and annihilates the pair; this is the process of excursion operators with a partial Frobenius in place of a Galois element. Its properties used here are Proposition B.1 and Theorem B.2 (S_{W,v} = T_{W,v} away from v). The precise definition is to be quoted from [Laf18, §6], with k-coefficients as in [Xueb, §7] and [XZ, §6].
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Appendix B, §B.1, p. 62 (citing [Laf18, §6])
items.note: Added by the review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24): Proposition B.1, Theorem B.2, Lemma B.3 and the proof of Lemma B.4 are relations among these operators, and no item defines them. The paper cites [Laf18, §6] and says only that they are defined 'by a process similar to one defining excursion operators'. GS.5 has them only implicitly, in characteristic zero, through 'unramified Satake compatibility'.

items.name: Faithfulness of the centre action on shtukas without legs (Remark 6.2)
items.statement: In the setting of Proposition 6.1 (item 72, corrected), for every integer r ≥ 0 and every closed finite subscheme D^v of X supported away from v that is large enough (depending on r), the action of ℨ(G,K_r) on H^0_c(Sht_{G,D,∅}; 1), D = rv + D^v, is faithful. Hence ℨ(G,K_r) → End_{H_G}(H^0_c(Sht_{G,D,∅}; 1)) is injective, and so is its colimit version at D = rv + ∞x_0 used in §6.4.1. The same holds for H with U_r in place of K_r.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Remark 6.2, p. 45, quoting Genestier–Lafforgue, Lemme 1.4; used in §6.4.1, p. 49, and in the proof of Corollary 6.14, p. 50
items.note: Added by the review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24): Genestier–Lafforgue's faithfulness lemma is used twice: to make ℨ(G,K_r) → End(H^0_c(Sht_{G,D,∅};1)) injective (§6.4.1), and for the analogous injectivity for H in the proof of Corollary 6.14. Item 72 cites the remark but does not state it.

items.name: Irreducible representations with K-fixed vectors and simple Hecke modules
items.statement: Let K ⊂ G_v be an open compact subgroup whose pro-order is invertible in k. Then Π ↦ Π^K induces a bijection between isomorphism classes of irreducible smooth representations Π of G_v over k with Π^K ≠ 0 and isomorphism classes of simple H(G,K)-modules, the H(G,K)-module structure on Π^K being given by convolution.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Proof of Theorem 6.26, p. 55 (recalled without reference)
items.note: Added by the review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24): This is the step that turns an irreducible H(G,K_r)-module into the representation Π. The paper recalls it without reference. SR.1 plans the equivalence of smooth representations with nondegenerate modules over the Hecke algebra, and the e_U corners, from which it follows. SR.1 does not state it, so it is missing as it stands.

items.name: Schur's lemma for irreducible admissible representations over k
items.statement: Let Π be an irreducible admissible representation of G_v over k, an algebraic closure of F_p. Then End_{G_v}(Π) = k. Consequently ℨ(G) acts on Π through a character χ_Π: ℨ(G) → k.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, §6.1.1, p. 45; and the proof of Theorem 6.21, p. 53
items.note: Added by the review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24): Every character χ_Π of ℨ(G), and hence the definition of ρ_Π, depends on End_{G_v}(Π) = k. Over the countable field F̄_p this needs admissibility. SR.3 is written for complex coefficients only.

items.name: Equivariance of the Genestier–Lafforgue map under automorphisms of G
items.statement: Let θ be an automorphism of G over F_v; here θ = σ acting on G = Res_{E_v/F_v}(H_{E_v}). Let θ act on Exc(W_v, ^LG) through the induced automorphism of ^LG (well defined up to inner automorphisms of Ĝ, which act trivially on the excursion algebra), and on ℨ(G) by transport of structure. Then Z_G ∘ θ = θ ∘ Z_G. In particular Z_G maps Exc(W_v, ^LG)^σ into ℨ(G)^σ, and χ_Π ∘ Z_G ∘ σ = χ_Π ∘ Z_G for every σ-fixed irreducible admissible Π.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Proof of Theorem 6.21, p. 52 ('as Z_G maps Exc(W_v, ^LG)^σ ⊂ Exc(W_v, ^LG) into ℨ(G)^σ'); and the diagram in the proof of Theorem 6.26, p. 55
items.note: Added by the review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24): Both proofs assert without proof that Z_G maps Exc(W_v,^LG)^σ into ℨ(G)^σ. It is also what makes χ_Π σ-invariant for σ-fixed Π, which gives χ_{Π^{(p)}}(N·S) = 0 in the proof of Theorem 6.21. It is transport of structure for the Genestier–Lafforgue construction, but no item states it.

items.name: Depth of an irreducible smooth representation
items.statement: Let H be a connected reductive group over a local field F_v and let the Moy–Prasad filtration H(F_v)_{x,r} be normalized so that F_v^× has value group Z. For an irreducible smooth representation π of H(F_v) over k, depth(π) is the minimal r ≥ 0 such that π^{H(F_v)_{x,r+}} ≠ 0 for some x ∈ B(H/F_v), where H(F_v)_{x,r+} := ∪_{s>r} H(F_v)_{x,s}.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Remark 6.27, p. 56, after Moy–Prasad [MP96]
items.note: Added by the review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24): Item 95 uses depth without defining it. PAPER-FINTZEN-21/7b routes the same definition to SmoothRepresentationsPartII, but only for groups split over a tame extension with the residue characteristic not dividing |W|. Here H is arbitrary, so the two routes need one owner with the general definition.

items.name: Tame Galois descent of buildings and Moy–Prasad filtrations
items.statement: Let E_v/F_v be a finite Galois extension of degree prime to the residue characteristic ℓ (hence tamely ramified), H a connected reductive group over F_v, and G := Res_{E_v/F_v}(H_{E_v}), with Moy–Prasad filtrations normalized so that F_v^× has value group Z. Then B(H/F_v) = B(G/F_v)^{Gal(E_v/F_v)}. For x ∈ B(H/F_v) and r ≥ 0: G(F_v)_{x,r}^{Gal(E_v/F_v)} ⊃ H(F_v)_{x,r}, and (G(F_v)_{x,r+})^{Gal(E_v/F_v)} = H(F_v)_{x,r+}. If E_v/F_v is unramified, then also G(F_v)_{x,r}^{Gal(E_v/F_v)} = H(F_v)_{x,r}.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, §6.2.2, p. 46; and Remark 6.27, p. 56 (citing Prasad 2020, and Kaletha–Prasad §9, §12 and Proposition 12.9.2)
items.note: Added by the review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24): This splits off the part of item 73 that no stage plans. It is used for U_r ⊃ H(F_v)_{x,r}, for the choice x ∈ B(H/F_v) in §6.6.3, and for the depth estimate.

items.name: Finiteness over invariants (Artin–Tate) and Nakayama
items.statement: Let a finite group Γ act on a commutative k-algebra A of finite type. Then A is integral, hence finite, over A^Γ, and A^Γ is a k-algebra of finite type (Artin–Tate). Nakayama: if M is a finitely generated module over a commutative ring R and I ⊂ R is an ideal with M = IM, then there is a ∈ I with (1 − a)M = 0.
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, Proof of Theorem 6.26, p. 56
items.note: Added by the review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24): The commutative algebra that turns finiteness over the center into existence of the base change. It is library: mathlib:Algebra.IsInvariant.isIntegral (integrality over the invariants of a finite group action), mathlib:Algebra.IsIntegral.finite (integral and of finite type implies finite), mathlib:fg_of_fg_of_fg (root namespace, RingTheory/Adjoin/Tower.lean) (the Artin–Tate lemma), and mathlib:Submodule.exists_sub_one_mem_and_smul_eq_zero_of_fg_of_le_smul (Nakayama). All were read at the pinned Mathlib commit.

items.name: The mod p Bernstein centre as an inverse limit of Hecke centres
items.statement: Let G_v be the F_v-points of a reductive group over a local field of residue characteristic ℓ ≠ p. For open compact subgroups K ⊂ K′ of G_v of pro-order prime to p, convolution with the normalised idempotent 1_{K′} gives a ring homomorphism ℨ(G,K;k) → ℨ(G,K′;k) between the centres of the Hecke algebras H(G,K;k) = C_c(K\G_v/K;k). The ring ℨ(G;k) := lim_K ℨ(G,K;k), over such K, is isomorphic to the ring of endomorphisms of the identity functor on smooth k-representations of G_v, compatibly with the action of ℨ(G,K;k) on V^K for every smooth V. In particular an irreducible admissible Π gives a character χ_Π of ℨ(G;k).
items.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), doi 10.1017/fmp.2023.32, §6.1.1, pp. 44–45
items.note: Added by the review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24): Split off from item 70: SR.1 plans the Hecke algebras and ES0 the centre of the smooth category, but no layer plans the presentation of the mod p centre as an inverse limit over levels or its comparison with End(id).

prerequisites.citation: A. Genestier and V. Lafforgue, "Chtoucas restreints pour les groupes réductifs et paramétrisation de Langlands locale"
prerequisites.why: The semisimplified local Langlands correspondence over local function fields for all reductive groups, given by the homomorphism Z_G from the excursion algebra to the Bernstein center; it is the correspondence whose base change properties the paper's local theorems are about, and its local-global compatibility (Proposition 6.1) is the bridge from the global results.

prerequisites.citation: C. Xue, "Cohomology with integral coefficients of stacks of shtukas"; "Smoothness of the cohomology of stacks of shtukas"; "Finiteness of cohomology groups of stacks of shtukas as modules over Hecke algebras, and applications", Épijournal de Géométrie Algébrique 4 (2020), no. 6
prerequisites.why: The extension of Lafforgue's excursion action from the finite-dimensional cuspidal subspace to all compactly supported automorphic functions, which is what makes Theorem 1.6 a statement about automorphic parameters in general; Xue's Eichler–Shimura relation (Proposition B.1) and Drinfeld's lemma in the form of Lemma B.5 are also quoted from this series.

prerequisites.citation: D. Juteau, C. Mautner and G. Williamson, "Parity sheaves", J. Amer. Math. Soc. 27 (2014), 1169–1212; and "Parity sheaves and tilting modules", Ann. Sci. Éc. Norm. Supér. 49 (2016), 257–275
prerequisites.why: The theory of parity sheaves: JMW stratifications, pariversities, the classification of indecomposable parity complexes (Theorem 4.1), the existence of parity sheaves on affine Grassmannians and their equivariance when p is not a torsion prime.

prerequisites.citation: S. Leslie and G. Lonergan, "Parity sheaves and Smith theory", J. reine angew. Math. 777 (2021), 49–87
prerequisites.why: Tate-parity sheaves and their theory: the classification of indecomposable Tate-parity complexes, modular reduction to the Tate category, the lifting functor, and the functor LL describing the Frobenius contraction functor, which is the model for the base change functor BC.

prerequisites.citation: C. Mautner and S. Riche, "Exotic tilting sheaves, parity sheaves on affine Grassmannians, and the Mirković–Vilonen conjecture", J. Eur. Math. Soc. 20 (2018), 2259–2332
prerequisites.why: Theorem 4.8, that for p good the Geometric Satake equivalence identifies normalized parity sheaves on Gr_G with tilting modules for the dual group; this is the identification through which the base change functor is read as restriction along the diagonal.

prerequisites.citation: D. Treumann, "Smith theory and geometric Hecke algebras", Math. Ann. 375 (2019), 595–628
prerequisites.why: The original sheaf-theoretic Smith theory: the Tate category, the Smith operation and its six-functor formalism, in the complex-analytic setting. Also proposed as a prerequisite by PAPER-TREUMANN-VENKATESH-16, for its Theorem 3.3 on subgroups of the dual group.

prerequisites.citation: S. Riche and G. Williamson, "Smith–Treumann theory and the linkage principle", Publ. Math. IHES 136 (2022), 225–292
prerequisites.why: The algebraic version of Smith theory for p-adic étale sheaves on finite type schemes, which §3 generalizes to locally finite type schemes; the lemmas on free quotients, nearby stalks and the comparison of i^! with i^* are proved there in the finite type case.

prerequisites.citation: J.-F. Dat, D. Helm, R. Kurinczuk and G. Moss, "Finiteness for Hecke algebras of p-adic groups", J. Amer. Math. Soc.
prerequisites.why: Theorem 6.24, that H(G,K_r) is finite over its center and the center is a finitely generated algebra, over an arbitrary Z_p-algebra of coefficients; it is what turns the character-matching argument into an existence statement for the base change representation in Theorem 6.26.

prerequisites.citation: T. Kaletha and G. Prasad, "Bruhat–Tits theory: a new approach", New Mathematical Monographs 44, Cambridge University Press, 2023
prerequisites.why: The reference for the Bruhat–Tits building, parahoric subgroups, the Moy–Prasad filtration and its Galois descent, and the Cartan decomposition at a special vertex with the Kottwitz homomorphism, all used in §6.2 and in the depth estimate of Remark 6.27.

routes.title: Sheaf-theoretic Smith theory, parity sheaves and the base change functor for the Satake category
routes.brief:
Plan sheaf-theoretic Smith theory and the base change functor it produces on the Satake category. The final theorem is Feng's Theorem 4.20: for H reductive over a separably closed field F of characteristic not p, G = H^p with sigma acting by cyclic rotation, and p a good prime for G-hat, the base change functor BC from normalized parity sheaves on Gr_G with k-coefficients to normalized parity sheaves on Gr_H corresponds, under the two Geometric Satake equivalences Parity^0(Gr_G;k) = Tilt_k(G-hat) and Parity^0(Gr_H;k) = Tilt_k(H-hat) of Mautner-Riche, to restriction Res_BC along the diagonal embedding H-hat into G-hat. Two further final statements are Proposition 3.12, that the Smith operation Psm commutes with proper pushforward for a sigma-equivariant morphism of locally finite type schemes of bounded dimension, and its corollary that T^* RGamma_c(Y;F) = RGamma_c(Y^sigma; Psm F), which is the equivariant localisation theorem of Smith, Borel and Quillen in sheaf-theoretic form. Cover: the constructible and ind-constructible Tate categories, that is the Verdier quotients of the bounded constructible and ind-constructible equivariant derived categories by perfect, respectively flat, complexes over the group ring, with the identification of Flat^b as the objects of locally finite tor-amplitude and with the fact that shift by two is the identity on the Tate category; the Smith operation Psm = T^* i^*, the six operations on Tate categories, the lemmas that pushforward along a free quotient and from a free action land in Flat^b, and that the cone of i^! to i^* is flat; Tate cohomology of complexes and of sheaves by the colimit along the two-periodicity map, with its long exact sequence and its behaviour under a trivial action; parity sheaves after Juteau-Mautner-Williamson, with JMW stratifications, pariversities, the structure of indecomposable parity complexes and the existence of parity sheaves on affine Grassmannians; Tate-parity sheaves after Leslie-Lonergan with integral coefficients, modular reduction, and the lifting functor; tilting modules for the dual group with the theorem that normalized parity sheaves on Gr_G are tilting modules and that tiltings generate the bounded derived category of representations; and finally the norm functor Nm on the Satake category, the proof that Psm preserves parity, the Frobenius twist of a k-linear category, the construction of BC, its additivity, Galois equivariance and exactness, and the reduction to a torus through hyperbolic localisation that proves Theorem 4.20. Import from: Geometric Satake over the Fargues-Fontaine curve (GeometricSatakeAndFusion) for the affine Grassmannian, the Satake category with convolution and the Tannakian dual group, and for semi-infinite geometry and the constant-term functor; Etale duality, cycle classes and perverse sheaves (EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves) for the six operations, Verdier duality and the perverse t-structure; Reductive groups, Part II (ReductiveGroupsPartII) for the dual group; and Reductive algebraic groups (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ReductiveGroups) together with the proposed Part II on integral highest weights (ReductiveGroupsIntegralRepresentationsPartII) for Weyl and costandard modules in characteristic p, on which the tilting-module theory rests. Tate cohomology of a finite cyclic group and Witt vectors are already in the libraries and must not be rebuilt.

Corrections from the review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24):
- Ownership. This roadmap also owns the Tate diagonal homomorphism of a commutative algebra over a perfect field of characteristic p, with the unique extension of characters through it (Definition 5.14, Lemma 5.15), and the Frobenius twist and linearization of algebras (Construction 5.17). These moved here from route 2: they are the general form of Treumann–Venkatesh §3.4 and the algebra form of Construction 4.17, which this roadmap already plans. ShtukaTateCohomologyAndGlobalBaseChange and SmithTheoryAndModPFunctoriality import them.
- It also owns hyperbolic localisation and the constant term functor for the equal-characteristic affine Grassmannian with k- and O-coefficients (Remark A.1 and (A.1)). GeometricSatakeAndFusion plans these only for the B_dR^+ Grassmannian, so transport GS1 and GS4:integral-dual-group rather than import them.
- It owns the fact that every flat k[σ]-module, finite or not, is free (Stacks 051E), with the local ring structure k[σ] ≅ k[x]/(x^p). Mathlib has only the finite case.
- Mistakes in the paper to plan around (the source issues give the details):
  - Lemma 3.8 needs Y of bounded dimension. Without it, the cone of i^!F → i^*F need not be bounded (Y = ⊔_n A^n). Every application is to varieties.
  - The filtration argument in the proof of Lemma 4.14 fails, because Nm is not additive and i^* is not t-exact. In the case used, F is a normalized O-parity sheaf on Gr_G = Gr_H^p, and no filtration is needed: F is a sum of external products E(λ_1) ⊠ … ⊠ E(λ_p).
  - Lemma 4.16 is false for the σ-equivariant categories as printed. Reduction mod p is not full: on a σ-fixed point, Hom_{O[σ]}(O, I) = 0 but its reduction is nonzero, where I is the augmentation ideal. For p ≥ 5 it is not essentially surjective either. State it for the non-equivariant categories, which is all §4.6.3 uses. An equivariant form holds only on a subcategory such as the additive closure of the image of Nm, which is also where Psm is defined.
  - §4.6.3: for L ∘ Psm ∘ Nm to factor through reduction mod p, one needs the lemma that Psm ∘ Nm is additive and Frobenius-semilinear on morphisms. This is a new item: the categorical Tate diagonal.
  - Lemma 4.24: the right face of the cube (T^*ε^* ∘ L ≅ F ∘ incl) holds on objects but not as a natural isomorphism of functors. T^*ε^* is essentially surjective but not full, and L kills the components of index i ≠ 0 in (4.2) that F keeps; there is a counterexample on Gr^λ_H ≅ P^1 for GL_2. Restate the lemma on objects. The back face as a natural isomorphism, which the proof of Proposition 5.12(i) uses, then needs its own argument, for instance that Psm of a morphism between objects in the image of Nm has no components of index i ≠ 0.
  - §A.4: the torus case and the faithfulness of restriction to T̂_H give Theorem 4.20 object by object, and as a natural isomorphism after restriction to T̂_H. They do not give a natural isomorphism of functors into Rep(Ĥ), which Proposition 5.12 uses. Plan the Ĥ-equivariance of its components, or build the isomorphism another way (through rank-one Levi subgroups, for instance). The paper does not supply this step.
  - §A.5: BC := BC^(p) ∘ Frob_p^{-1}; the printed order of composition is reversed.

Corrected finite-Tor contract (FIX-RT-PAPER-FENG-24): Keep rev-6 in this roadmap. Separate Rf_! and Rj_*: compact-support pushforward has the [a,b+2d] bound for geometric fibre dimension ≤d and the stated torsion/projection-formula hypotheses; open direct image retains only finite-Tor preservation with an ambient cohomological-dimension bound, not a bound by relative dimension. Check the punctured-line Kummer stalk over Fbar_7 with Fbar_3[C_3] coefficients. The consumer in Feng p.16 needs finiteness. Any adic W(k) passage needs a compatible system with a uniform bound and its limit justification.
routes.reason: A search of data/atlas.json for Smith theory, parity sheaves, Tate categories and tilting modules returns nothing: the only Tate cohomology in the atlas is the class-formation layer of the Tau Ceti class field theory roadmap, and the perverse machinery in EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves is about the perverse t-structure, not about a mod 2 parity condition that survives a Verdier quotient in which shift by two is the identity. Nor is there a direction to extend: GeometricSatakeAndFusion plans the Satake category, its convolution and the dual group, but nothing about equivariant localisation for a Z/p-action on it, and the whole point of §§3–4 is a second, exotic localisation of that category. This material is also not specific to base change: sheaf-theoretic Smith theory, parity sheaves and Tate-parity sheaves are general tools of modular representation theory, used by Riche–Williamson for the linkage principle and by Leslie–Lonergan for the Frobenius contraction functor, so a roadmap of their own is the right home and both those papers and this one are sources for it.

routes.title: Global shtukas and Langlands over function fields, Part II: mod p coefficients, Tate cohomology of shtukas and cyclic base change
routes.reason: The parent roadmap owns precisely the objects §5 acts on — shtuka stacks with legs, level and truncations (GS.2), their compactly supported cohomology with Hecke and cohomological correspondences (GS.3), partial Frobenius and Drinfeld's lemma (GS.4), and excursion operators with the reconstruction of semisimple L-parameters (GS.5) — and the paper is a source for those layers (see the source route below). What it adds is new layers in the same direction: its stated coefficient field is characteristic-zero ℓ-adic, whereas this whole paper lives in characteristic p, where the Hecke-finite cuspidal sector of GS.3 is replaced by Xue's extension of the excursion action to all compactly supported functions; and, on top of that, a Z/pZ-action on the entire shtuka tower, the finite-étale identification of Sht_H with its fixed locus, Tate cohomology of shtukas in place of cohomology, Drinfeld's lemma for Tate cohomology, and the resulting identity between excursion operators for G and for H. None of that is planned anywhere. It is a Part II rather than a new roadmap because every statement is about the moduli of shtukas and the excursion action that the parent roadmap constructs.

routes.title: Smooth representations of local groups, Part II: mod p Bernstein centers, the Brauer homomorphism and local cyclic base change
routes.brief:
Plan the local theory: mod p Hecke algebras at Moy-Prasad level, the base change homomorphism of Bernstein centers, and local cyclic base change for the Genestier-Lafforgue correspondence. The unrestricted source targets are Feng's Theorem 6.21, Theorem 6.26 and Corollary 6.15; the working comparisons are conditional on the finite-étale globalization contract stated below, under the standing hypothesis that p is an odd good prime for G-hat, with F_v a local function field of residue characteristic ell not p, H reductive over F_v, E_v/F_v cyclic of degree p and G = Res_{E_v/F_v}(H_{E_v}). Theorem 6.21: for an irreducible admissible representation Pi of G(F_v) over k with character chi_{Pi^{(p)}} of the excursion algebra attached to its Frobenius twist, every irreducible character chi of Exc(W_v,^LH) appearing in the action on T^*(Pi) satisfies chi composed with phi_BC^* equal to chi_{Pi^{(p)}}; this is the Treumann-Venkatesh conjecture that Tate cohomology realises functoriality. Theorem 6.26: for every irreducible representation pi of H(F_v) over k with nonzero U_r-fixed vectors there is an irreducible representation Pi of G(F_v) with nonzero K_r-fixed vectors and rho_Pi isomorphic to phi_BC composed with rho_pi, with the depth estimate depth(Pi) at most depth(pi) in the normalisation of Remark 6.27. Corollary 6.15: the square formed by phi_BC^* on excursion algebras, the Genestier-Lafforgue maps Z_G and Z_H, and the homomorphism Z_TV of Bernstein centers commutes. Cover: Hecke algebras H(G,K_r) for K_r the Moy-Prasad filtration subgroups at a point of the Bruhat-Tits building, with k-coefficients, their centers and the Bernstein center as the inverse limit; the injectivity of the map of double coset spaces at a special vertex and the surjectivity of restriction it gives; plain subgroups, the unnormalized Brauer homomorphism and its compatibility with Tate cohomology, and the fact that every subgroup of the pro-ell radical is plain; the Treumann-Venkatesh homomorphism at each level, its compatibility with change of level, and the resulting Z_TV; the Genestier-Lafforgue correspondence through the map Z_G from the excursion algebra to the Bernstein center and its local-global compatibility; linkage of local representations and the Treumann-Venkatesh conjecture; and the finiteness of Hecke algebras over their centers, quoted from Dat-Helm-Kurinczuk-Moss, which together with Nakayama produces the base change representation. Import from: Smooth representations of local groups (SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups) for the smooth category over arbitrary coefficients, admissibility, Hecke algebras over rings and the Bernstein center; Reductive groups, Part II (ReductiveGroupsPartII) for buildings, parahoric and congruence group schemes and the Cartan decomposition; Global shtukas and Langlands over function fields, Part II (ShtukaTateCohomologyAndGlobalBaseChange) for the global input, namely the identification of excursion operators under equivariant localisation; and Arithmetic locally symmetric spaces and their cohomology, Part II: Smith theory and mod p functoriality (SmithTheoryAndModPFunctoriality), proposed by PAPER-TREUMANN-VENKATESH-16, which plans the same Brauer homomorphism, plain subgroups, linkage and the conjecture: that Part II owns them, because it states them in the general setting (any automorphism σ of order p of G and any l-space), of which G = Res_{E_v/F_v}(H_{E_v}) with the Galois action is a special case. This roadmap imports from it σ-plain subgroups (item 77), the Brauer homomorphism and its compatibility with Tate cohomology of permutation modules (items 78 and 84), the unique compatible σ-action on a σ-fixed representation (item 88), linkage (item 89) and the Treumann–Venkatesh conjecture (item 90). They stay in this route's item list only because that Part II is not yet in the atlas; if it is rejected, this roadmap owns them. What this roadmap plans is the specialisation at Moy–Prasad level: Lemmas 6.6, 6.7 and 6.10, Definitions 6.8 and 6.11 and what follows from them. In the other direction, the Tate diagonal and the Frobenius twist of algebras (Feng's Definition 5.14, Lemma 5.15 and Construction 5.17, the general form of Treumann–Venkatesh §3.4) are owned by SheafTheoreticSmithTheory, and both Part IIs import them.

Corrections from the review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24):
- Level and base point. Proposition 6.3 and Corollary 6.4 are false at r = 0: there is a counterexample with H = SL_2 and E_v/F_v totally ramified. The Gal(E_v/F_v)-fixed special vertex of B(G/F_v) that §6.2.3 assumes need not exist (H = SL_1(D) with E_v unramified of degree p).
  - Plan both results for r > 0 at any point x ∈ B(H/F_v) ⊂ B(G/F_v)^{Gal}. The paper's r > 0 argument uses only that K_r is Gal-stable and pro-ℓ.
  - The corrected r > 0 input supports Definitions 6.8 and 6.11 and Lemma 6.10 at any σ-fixed point. Corollaries 6.13–6.15 additionally require the qualified global comparison or its separately proved ramified replacement. This repairs the local double-coset input at r > 0, including nonspecial x, but does not complete the proof of Theorem 6.26 until Corollary 6.14 has a valid global ramified comparison (E58).
  - Galois descent of buildings and Moy–Prasad filtrations under tame extensions is a new item of this route. ReductiveGroupsPartII:RG2.2–RG2.3 plan buildings and parahorics, but not the Moy–Prasad filtration in this generality.
- Theorem 6.26 at r = 0 is asserted as 'classical' without argument. State it for r > 0, which is all that Theorem 1.1 and Remark 6.27 need.
- Theorem 1.1 needs the standing hypothesis that p is an odd prime that is good for Ĝ.
- Finiteness of Hecke algebras over their centres is SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups:SR.6 (Dat–Helm–Kurinczuk–Moss). Import it: item 93 is now planned.
- The mod p Bernstein centre as an inverse limit of Hecke centres is a new item of this route. The Hecke algebras themselves come from SR.1, on top of the Hecke ring in the libraries, and the centre of the smooth category comes from ExcursionOperatorsAndSpectralAction:ES0.

Corrected global-input contract (FIX-RT-PAPER-FENG-24): Items 85,86,87,91,94,95 give working comparisons conditional on a compatible finite étale globalization and the necessary faithful local-global input. Such a globalization has unramified completion at v, so it supplies no ramified local result. routes.reason: Section 6 is local representation theory of p-adic groups with characteristic p coefficients: Hecke algebras at Moy-Prasad level and their centers, the Bernstein center, the Brauer homomorphism, and the Genestier-Lafforgue correspondence. The parent roadmap plans the smooth category over arbitrary coefficients (SR.0), Hecke algebras over rings with the explicit instruction that characteristic p is to be handled in the smooth action category by integral double-coset operators (SR.1), and the Bernstein center, though its SR.3 layer is written for complex coefficients. New layers are needed for: the mod p Bernstein center as an inverse limit over Moy-Prasad levels; the base change homomorphism Z_TV, which Haines sought in characteristic zero and which is constructed here for general groups and arbitrary depth; the Genestier-Lafforgue map from the excursion algebra to the Bernstein center with its local-global compatibility; and the two main local theorems. This is distinct from the Part IIs of the same parent already proposed by other extractions — types and supercuspidals (PAPER-FINTZEN-21), Newton cocenters (PAPER-HE-18), parahoric centers (PAPER-HE-21, PAPER-KISIN-PAPPAS-18, PAPER-ZHU-17), general-linear newforms (PAPER-ATOBE-KONDO-YASUDA-22) and unitary spherical representations (PAPER-CIUBOTARU-HARRIS-26) — none of which touches characteristic p coefficients or base change. Where it overlaps the Part II of ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces proposed by PAPER-TREUMANN-VENKATESH-16 — plain subgroups, the unnormalized Brauer homomorphism, its compatibility with Tate cohomology, linkage and the Treumann-Venkatesh conjecture, which are that paper's statements quoted here — the two must not both plan them; the brief says which imports which.

Sections 2 and 5.1 are a careful, self-contained account of exactly what these layers plan, and the paper is a good source for them even though everything it says there is already planned. GS.5 plans excursion operators indexed by invariant functions and Galois tuples with their relations, and the reconstruction of continuous semisimple L-parameters from characters of the excursion algebra: §2 gives the excursion algebra by generators and relations in two presentations — one by invariant functions on G-hat \ (^LG)^I / G-hat, one by a representation with an invariant vector and an invariant functional — together with the comparison between them and Lafforgue's reconstruction theorem in the form proved for modular coefficients by Böckle–Harris–Khare–Thorne. GS.1 and GS.2 plan the global Hecke stack, classical geometric Satake on it, and multi-leg shtukas with bounds, level, partial Frobenius and truncations: §5.1 sets all of that up, including the iterated shtuka stacks and the stratified smallness of the map to Sht_{G,D,I}. GS.4 plans Drinfeld's lemma and the continuous action of a product of global Galois groups, which is the statement Appendix B transports to Tate cohomology. The roadmap is a campaign roadmap, not a Tau Ceti one, so it may take the paper as a source.

Correction from the review (REV-PAPER-FENG-24): the excursion algebra and the reconstruction of L-parameters are used in this paper over k = F̄_p, which GS.5 does not plan (its coefficients are characteristic-zero ℓ-adic), and the Satake functor on shtukas with k-coefficients is the modular branch that GS.1 leaves out. Items 11, 12, 13, 53 and 104 therefore moved to route 2. This route keeps item 10 (L-parameters, whose definition does not depend on the coefficients), items 52 and 54, and the review's new items on the partial Frobenius Weil group (GS.4), the decomposition by ker¹(F,G) (GS.0) and Harder–Narasimhan truncations at deep level (GS.2). For those the paper is a source for the geometric, coefficient-independent part of the layers.

sourceIssues.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), Proposition 2.4, equation (2.3), p. 11 (published; arXiv v6 identical)
sourceIssues.correction: ν(S_{{0,...,n},f,(γ_0,γ_1,...,γ_n)}) = f((ρ_ν(γ_0), ρ_ν(γ_1), ..., ρ_ν(γ_n))). Equivalently, keep the right-hand side and make the subscript of S equal to (γ_0γ_n, ..., γ_{n−1}γ_n, γ_n).
sourceIssues.reason: The relations of §2.2.2 are incompatible with the printed formula. Take G = G_m split, so Ĝ = G_m and ^LG^alg = Ĝ × Γ, and let f(g_0,g_1) := ĝ_0ĝ_1^{−1} on the Ĝ-components. This f is invariant under left and right diagonal translation. Relation (iii) with ζ: {0,1} → {∗} gives S_{{0,1},f,(γ,γ)} = S_{{∗},f^ζ,γ} with f^ζ = 1, and relation (ii) makes this 1. The printed (2.3) gives instead ν(S_{{0,1},f,(γ,γ)}) = f(ρ_ν(γ²), ρ_ν(γ)) = χ(γ), where ρ_ν = (χ, id). Now take any character χ: Γ → k^× with χ ≠ 1. The assignment S_{I,f,(γ_i)} ↦ f((χ(γ_i),γ_i)_i) respects relations (i)–(v), so it is a character ν of Exc. Applying the printed (2.3) with (γ_0,γ_1) = (γ,1) forces ρ_ν = (χ, id), and applying it with (γ,γ) forces χ = 1. So no ρ_ν exists, and Proposition 2.4 as printed is false. For split G the printed right-hand side equals f(ρ(γ_0), ..., ρ(γ_{n−1}), 1), which does not depend on γ_n. The corrected formula satisfies relations (iii)–(v), as one checks directly. With h(g_0,...,g_{n−1}) := f(g_0,...,g_{n−1},1), it is the pseudocharacter identity of BHKT19 §4, Θ_n(h)(γ_1,...,γ_n) = h(ρ(γ_1),...,ρ(γ_n)), taken at γ_iγ_n^{−1}. sourceIssues.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), Lemma 2.7, p. 12
sourceIssues.printed: The source asserts the existence of φ^*: Exc(Γ, ^LG^alg) → Exc(Γ, ^LH^alg) as a homomorphism. In the Proposition 2.4 description of spectral k-points, an input ρ ∈ H^1(Γ, Ĥ(k)) has image φ ∘ ρ ∈ H^1(Γ, Ĝ(k)).
sourceIssues.correction: … sends ρ to the semisimplification (φ∘ρ)^{ss}, the unique semisimple parameter with the same excursion character as φ∘ρ. This equals φ∘ρ when φ∘ρ is semisimple, in particular for φ = φ_BC (see the next finding).
sourceIssues.reason: By Proposition 2.4 the k-points of Spec Exc are semisimple parameters, and ν∘φ^* sends S_{I,f,(γ_i)} to f((φρ(γ_i))_i), which depends only on (φ∘ρ)^{ss}. In characteristic p, φ∘ρ need not be semisimple. Take H = PGL_2 and G = PGL_{p+1} split, with φ = Sym^p × id: SL_2 × Γ → SL_{p+1} × Γ, which is admissible. Let ρ have image SL_2(F_p), which is irreducible on k^2 and so semisimple; Γ = Gal(F^s/F) for a suitable global function field of characteristic ≠ p admits such a surjection, by Igusa (the mod p monodromy of the Legendre curve is SL_2(F_p)). Sym^p(k^2) contains the Frobenius twist span(x^p, y^p) as an SL_2(F_p)-submodule with no invariant complement. A linear-algebra check over F_p for p = 3, 5, 7 finds no equivariant retraction. So φ∘ρ lies in the stabiliser of a 2-plane but in no Levi of it, and is not semisimple. The lemma is used only for φ = φ_BC, where its statement holds once φ_BC is shown to preserve semisimplicity.

sourceIssues.printed: Lemma 4.16 assumes simple connectivity of every stratum Y_λ and existence of every parity sheaf E(λ, L) for Y_λ ∈ S. It concludes Parity^0_{S,σ}(Y; O) ⊗_O k ≅ Parity^0_{S,σ}(Y; k).

A σ-equivariant version holds only on a subcategory whose Hom-lattices M satisfy H^1(⟨σ⟩, M) = 0 and whose objects lift, e.g. the additive closure of the image of Nm. Lemma 4.24 should be stated on such a subcategory.
sourceIssues.reason: Counterexample: Y = pt with trivial σ (or the base-point stratum Gr^0_G of Gr_G, whose L^+G⋊σ-equivariant local systems are O[Z/p]-lattices, since the component group of the stabiliser is Z/p). Then σ-equivariant normalized parity sheaves are O[σ]-lattices in degree 0. For I the augmentation ideal, Hom_{O[σ]}(O, I) = I^σ = 0 (the invariants of O[σ] are O·N and ε(N) = p ≠ 0), while Hom_{k[σ]}(k, I ⊗ k) ≠ 0, because the nonzero k[σ]-module I ⊗ k (the augmentation ideal of k[σ]) has nonzero fixed vectors. So reduction is not full. For p ≥ 5 it is also not essentially surjective: the indecomposable O[Z/p]-lattices for unramified O are O, I and O[σ], of ranks 1, p−1 and p, so the Jordan block k[σ]/(σ−1)^2 is not a reduction. The proof's claim that 'all k-local systems on strata lift to O since they are trivial' fails for σ-equivariant local systems on σ-stable strata. Also, the σ-equivariant stratification is not JMW: Ext^2_σ(O,O) = H^2(Z/p;O) = O/p is not free. The σ-equivariant form is used only in Lemma 4.24, where the unlabeled arrow 'exists by the universal property of the categorical tensor product'. Same text in arXiv v6.

sourceIssues.locator: Forum of Mathematics, Pi 12 (2024), Proof of Lemma 4.14, pp. 24–25
sourceIssues.printed: The source says a finite L^+G-equivariant filtration of F allows the lemma to be verified on its associated graded, provided that graded object meets the hypotheses. It claims such a filtration exists because Gr^λ_G decomposes as a product of spaces homogeneous under a finite type quotient of L^+H, with graded object a direct sum of F_1 ⊠ … ⊠ F_p for F_i ∈ P_{L^+H}(Gr_H; O).
sourceIssues.correction: In the case used (§4.6.3: F a normalized O-parity sheaf, p odd and good) no filtration is needed. F is a direct sum of E(λ_1) ⊠ … ⊠ E(λ_p): an external product of parity sheaves on Gr_G = Gr_H^p is parity, and it is indecomposable since its endomorphism ring is the tensor product of local rings with residue field k. F' = E(λ_1) ⋆ … ⋆ E(λ_p) is parity [JMW16, Theorem 1.5], so its stalks and costalks have O-free cohomology. Nm of a direct sum differs from the sum of the Nm's by induced (free) pieces. The tensor-induction count then applies to H^*(F'_x)^{⊗p} by Künneth; the Koszul signs are harmless for p odd. For F as general as the lemma states, a proof is missing.
sourceIssues.reason: Nm is not additive. A filtration of F gives only a σ-stable filtration of Nm(F) with graded pieces Nm(gr_i F) and induced pieces, and i^* is not t-exact, so the stalk cohomology of i^*Nm(F) is tied to the graded pieces only through long exact sequences. Kernels and cokernels of maps between O-free trivial O[σ]-modules need not be O-free (p: O → O has cokernel O/p, whose odd Tate cohomology is k ≠ 0, exactly what (*) must exclude). The text also does not show that the pieces F_1 ⊠ … ⊠ F_p have O-free stalks and costalks. Nor does it show that the convolution F' has O-free stalk cohomology, which the basis-counting step needs. The homogeneity of Gr^λ_G, offered as the reason for the filtration, does not give one.

sourceIssues.correction: Either drop r = 0 from the statement of Theorem 6.26 (Theorem 1.1 and Remark 6.27 need only r > 0, since the U_r are cofinal and the depth estimate uses the level G(F_v)_{x,r+}), or supply an argument. A possible route: π with parahoric-fixed vectors is a subquotient of a parabolic induction from the minimal Levi; Genestier–Lafforgue parameters are compatible with parabolic induction; and left exactness of K_0-invariants on a finite-length induced representation gives an irreducible subquotient with K_0-fixed vectors.
sourceIssues.reason: No argument or reference is given, and the r > 0 argument does not apply. K_0 = G(F_v)_{x,0} need not have prime-to-p pro-order, so Π ↦ Π^{K_0} need not be a bijection onto simple Hecke modules, and K_0 need not be plain. The statement concerns mod p representations and the Genestier–Lafforgue parametrisation (2018), for which no 'classical' base change result at parahoric level is cited. Theorem 1.1 is unaffected.

Replace the ramified comparison by a separately proved construction and recheck localization, the β-sector argument and the local-global consumers. Do not declare the main existence theorem false.
sourceIssues.reason: With p=3 and geometry over F_7, t=u³, σ(u)=2u, the trivial line bundle with Frobenius identity and frame u modulo (u³−1)^n is fixed via multiplication by 4 for every n. Its framed automorphisms vanish and 4³=1, but inertia at u=0 acts by 4. Pullback degree forces any descended line bundle on P¹_t to be trivial, whose frame is invariant; no constant multiple of u is invariant even at n=1. Thus Lemma 5.7 is false at this permitted level. In the finite étale case, the torsor relation X′×_X X′=C_p×X′ turns the cocycle into effective descent.
